A rough, Old Testament warrior and a 21st century housewife—what might they have in common? Reading through the Psalms, we find a man who was determined to find the heart of God and walk in obedience. While there are not many similarities between my life and the life of this man, his words still touch my need and steady my floundering heart.

David set his heart on God even when his life was fraught with difficulty and distress. He was often unable to have the secure life he craved. As I read through his writings, I embark on a personal journey of faith and obedience. Often when confronted with a need in my life, the first words that come to my lips are “I’ll try”. It is so easy to allow emotions of frustration, fear, and worry to rule, instead of making the conscious choice of obedience. Many times, throughout the book of Psalms, David uses the words “I will”. David was determined to steer his heart in the way of obedience. Follow me on my journey thru this beautiful book as we explore a few of David’s “I wills”.

  • I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart. –Psalm 9:1a
  • I will love thee, O Lord, my strength. –Psalm 18:1
  • I will call upon the Lord, who is worthy to be praised. –Psalm 18:3a
  • I will confess my transgressions unto the Lord. –Psalm 32:5b
  • I will keep my mouth with a bridle. –Psalm 39:1b
  • I will wait on thy name. –Psalm 52:9b
  • I will trust in thee. –Psalm 56:3b
  • I will not fear what flesh can do unto me. –Psalm 56:4b
  • I will declare what he hath done for my soul. –Psalm 66:16b
  • I will praise the name of God with a song. –Psalm 69:30a
  • I will go in the strength of the Lord God. –Psalm 71:16a
  • I will remember the works of the Lord. –Psalm 77:11a
  • I will meditate also of all thy work and talk of thy doings. –Psalm 77:12
  • I will be satisfied when I awake with Thy likeness. –Psalm 17:5b

Most of David’s “I wills” were a conscious, emotional choice in the middle of unruly circumstances. Without emotions, this world would be a cold, hard place unable to be inhabited by God’s Spirit. All humankind was created with emotion, but women especially are easily dominated by them. We deal with the ebb and flow of our emotions daily, often like a wild horse which constantly tries to get out of control. But God also gives us His strength to rein in this ‘wild horse’ and guide it in the right direction. Once the choice is made, God’s grace is all ours. Opposite from what we often tell ourselves, we are not victims of our feelings or emotions. We are responsible to take action, for this is, in fact, a war between good and evil. It is a war between our sin nature and the nature of Christ.

I want to look at a few struggles which are common to women and then we will look at how a God-directed “I will” can change our perspective and ultimately affect our emotional responses and spiritual health.

Comparison

For we dare not make ourselves of the number, or compare ourselves with some that commend themselves: but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise –2 Corinthians 10:12.

It is our natural tendency to compare ourselves with others. Yet every time, we end up feeling either superior or inferior to the other person. This evokes many emotions that can either depress us, or unjustly affirm ourselves. Neither of these responses produces a peaceful heart. Instead of following this tendency of comparison, we can say like David, “I will love thee, O Lord, my strength.” Having our eyes on Christ will fulfill our hearts in a way that our desire for human reassurance and acceptance never can or will.

Fear

What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3.

It doesn’t always feel like we have a choice in this one, as fear tends to crash in on us without warning. But in some of my recent battles with fear, God showed me that living in continual fear is refusing to believe the promises found in His Word. David’s “I will trust in Thee” is a conscious choice that I also need to make. As some have said, “Fear is living in the future without God in it.” God’s grace is here for me today and it will be here for me tomorrow, but I cannot try to find grace today for tomorrow’s trials.

Discontentment

Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content –Philippians 4:11.

And having food and raiment let us be therewith content –1 Timothy 6:8.

Everything about the advertising strategies of today’s world are designed to create a desire for more. No matter how beautiful of a house we live in, our human nature will always crave just one more thing. Consider the peace that is available for you as a woman of God, if you choose to imitate David’s attitude, “I will be satisfied when I awake with thy likeness.” As God fulfills the longings of your heart, there’s no longer a need to search for a counterfeit fulfillment.

Gossip

Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man –Colossians 4:6.

Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers –Ephesians 4:29.

The word ‘gossip’ is defined as “casual or unconstrained conversation or reports about other people, typically involving details which are not confirmed to be true.” It is often an effort to elevate our own ego which is rooted in insecurity. David says, “I will keep my mouth with a bridle.” Even though he had every reason to spread ‘stories’ about his enemies, he found no need to devalue others through gossip.

Here we have considered only a few examples. I encourage each of you to prayerfully evaluate your own emotional responses and the way they can dominate your life. Here is a list of questions to help you discern the areas in your life that may need a change of perspective.

  1. Do you need more of an “I will” attitude in your life?
  2. Are you listless and wondering about the meaning of life?
  3. Are you struggling with depression?
  4. Do you struggle with your priorities and lack of motivation to change them?
  5. Do your children need more words of encouragement?
  6. Do you struggle with unhealthy eating habits?
  7. Are you caught in the cogs of negative thought patterns?
  8. Are you fighting your husband’s desires and leadership?

Good intentions and change are often only separated by lack of faith and motivation. Often, we don’t understand how God intimately cares about these emotions and problems in our lives and is waiting to see our willingness to change. When we take the first step of obedience, His grace is there to do the miracle. The “I’ll try” mindset brings lethargy and defeat. The “I will” opens up God’s endless store of grace. Every day brings hundreds of small decisions. How we respond to these decisions eventually form the woman we become and the woman we will be in our old age.

Mary, the future mother of Jesus, was suddenly face to face with an angel one day. His words troubled her and she “cast in her mind” what he was telling her. She could have allowed herself to be overcome with fear at the thought of what the angel’s words meant for her. Instead, she said, “Behold the handmaiden of the Lord, be it unto me according to Thy word.” She chose faith and it impacted the world in ways she could never have imagined.

It was a choice. A choice for which she could not take days or weeks to prepare. However, her being a part of God’s plan for the salvation of the world hung on that choice.

Esther, the queen was faced with a serious dilemma. Her people were in danger of being wiped out by the treacherous Haman. Mordecai told her that she was a queen for such a time as this and she must go in to the king and beg for his help. Her heart quavered. She was well acquainted with the king’s rules that whoever ventured into his palace without an invitation would likely be killed. But she chose courage… “If I perish, I perish.” She was going to do what she could for her people no matter what the cost.

It was just a choice. Yet the safety of her people and the miracle of their deliverance came through her willingness to make such a difficult choice.

Attitudes and emotions—the negative, or the positive—are all hidden choices we must make. Which will you choose, the faithless “I’ll try” or the courageous “I will”? Will you choose, by God’s grace, to make the right choice? God has promised to perfect the things which concern you, but He will not do His work in your life without your “I will”. It is up to you.

And God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work: –2 Corinthians 9:8.

Um guerreiro rude do Antigo Testamento e uma dona de casa do século XXI — o que poderiam ter em comum? Ao ler os Salmos, encontramos um homem determinado a buscar o coração de Deus e a andar em obediência. Embora haja poucas semelhanças entre a minha vida e a vida desse homem, suas palavras ainda tocam uma necessidade minha e dão firmeza ao meu coração vacilante.

Davi colocou seu coração em Deus mesmo quando sua vida estava repleta de dificuldades e angústias. Muitas vezes, não conseguia ter a vida segura que tanto desejava. Ao ler seus escritos, embarco em uma jornada pessoal de fé e obediência. Muitas vezes, quando me deparo com uma necessidade em minha vida, as primeiras palavras que me vêm aos lábios são: “Vou tentar”. É muito fácil permitir que emoções de frustração, medo e preocupação nos dominem, em vez de fazer a escolha consciente de obedecer. Muitas vezes, ao longo do livro dos Salmos, Davi usa as palavras “Eu farei”. Davi estava determinado a conduzir seu coração pelo caminho da obediência. Acompanhe-me nesta jornada por este belo livro enquanto exploramos algumas das declarações de Davi: “Eu farei”.

  • Louvarei a ti, ó Senhor, de todo o meu coração. –Salmos 9:1a
  • Amar-te-ei, ó Senhor, força minha. –Salmos 18:1
  • Invocarei o Senhor, que é digno de louvor. –Salmos 18:3a
  • Confessarei ao Senhor as minhas transgressões. –Salmos 32:5b
  • Porei freio à minha boca. –Salmos 39:1b
  • Esperarei no teu nome. –Salmos 52:9b
  • Confiarei em ti. –Salmos 56:3b
  • Não temerei o que a carne possa fazer contra mim. –Salmos 56:4b
  • Declararei o que ele fez por minha alma. –Salmos 66:16b
  • Louvarei o nome de Deus com um cântico. –Salmos 69:30a
  • Irei na força do Senhor Deus. –Salmos 71:16a
  • Lembrar-me-ei das obras do Senhor. –Salmos 77:11a
  • Meditarei também sobre todas as tuas obras e falarei dos teus feitos. –Salmos 77:12
  • Ficarei satisfeito quando despertar com a tua semelhança. –Salmos 17:5b

A maioria das declarações de Davi — “Eu farei” — foi uma escolha consciente e emocional em meio a circunstâncias desordenadas. Sem emoções, este mundo seria um lugar frio e duro, incapaz de ser habitado pelo Espírito de Deus. Toda a humanidade foi criada com emoções, mas as mulheres, em especial, são facilmente dominadas por elas. Lidamos diariamente com o fluxo e refluxo das emoções, muitas vezes como um cavalo selvagem que tenta constantemente escapar ao controle. Mas Deus também nos dá sua força para refrear esse “cavalo selvagem” e guiá-lo na direção certa. Uma vez feita a escolha, a graça de Deus é toda nossa. Ao contrário do que muitas vezes dizemos a nós mesmas, não somos vítimas de nossos sentimentos ou emoções. Somos responsáveis por agir, pois, na verdade, esta é uma guerra entre o bem e o mal. É uma guerra entre nossa natureza pecaminosa e a natureza de Cristo.

Quero examinar algumas dificuldades comuns às mulheres e, em seguida, veremos como um “Eu farei” dirigido por Deus pode mudar nossa perspectiva e, por fim, afetar nossas reações emocionais e nossa saúde espiritual.

Comparação

Porque não ousamos classificar-nos ou comparar-nos com alguns que se recomendam a si mesmos; mas estes, medindo-se a si mesmos e comparando-se consigo mesmos, não são sábios –2 Coríntios 10:12.

É nossa tendência natural comparar-nos com os outros. No entanto, a cada vez acabamos nos sentindo superiores ou inferiores à outra pessoa. Isso desperta muitas emoções que podem nos levar à tristeza ou nos fazer afirmar injustamente a nós mesmas. Nenhuma dessas reações produz um coração em paz. Em vez de seguir essa tendência de comparação, podemos dizer como Davi: “Amar-te-ei, ó Senhor, força minha”. Manter os olhos em Cristo satisfará nosso coração de uma maneira que nosso desejo de reafirmação e aceitação humanas nunca pode nem poderá satisfazer.

Medo

Quando eu estiver com medo, confiarei em ti –Salmos 56:3.

Nem sempre parece que temos escolha nessa situação, pois o medo tende a irromper sobre nós sem aviso. Mas, em algumas das minhas batalhas recentes contra o medo, Deus me mostrou que viver em constante temor é recusar-se a crer nas promessas encontradas em sua Palavra. “Confiarei em ti”, de Davi, é uma escolha consciente que também preciso fazer. Como alguns dizem: “O medo é viver no futuro sem Deus nele”. A graça de Deus está aqui para mim hoje e estará aqui para mim amanhã, mas não posso tentar encontrar hoje a graça para as provações de amanhã.

Descontentamento

Não digo isto por causa de necessidade, porque aprendi a estar contente em qualquer situação em que me encontre –Filipenses 4:11.

Tendo, porém, sustento e com que nos vestir, estejamos contentes –1 Timóteo 6:8.

Tudo nas estratégias publicitárias do mundo de hoje é projetado para criar o desejo por mais. Por mais bonita que seja a casa em que vivemos, nossa natureza humana sempre desejará apenas mais uma coisa. Pense na paz que está disponível para você como mulher de Deus, se escolher imitar a atitude de Davi: “Ficarei satisfeito quando despertar com a tua semelhança”. Quando Deus satisfaz os anseios do seu coração, já não há necessidade de buscar uma satisfação falsa.

Fofoca

Que a vossa palavra seja sempre agradável, temperada com sal, para que saibais como deveis responder a cada pessoa –Colossenses 4:6.

Não saia da vossa boca nenhuma palavra torpe, mas somente a que for boa para edificação, conforme a necessidade, para que transmita graça aos que a ouvem –Efésios 4:29.

A palavra “fofoca” é definida como “conversa ou relatos informais ou sem restrições sobre outras pessoas, geralmente envolvendo detalhes cuja veracidade não foi confirmada”. Muitas vezes, é uma tentativa de elevar nosso próprio ego, enraizada na insegurança. Davi diz: “Porei freio à minha boca”. Embora tivesse todos os motivos para espalhar “histórias” sobre seus inimigos, ele não viu necessidade de desvalorizar os outros por meio de fofocas.

Aqui consideramos apenas alguns exemplos. Incentivo cada uma de vocês a avaliar em oração suas próprias reações emocionais e o modo como elas podem dominar sua vida. Eis uma lista de perguntas para ajudá-la a discernir as áreas da sua vida que talvez precisem de uma mudança de perspectiva.

  1. Você precisa de uma atitude mais voltada para o “Eu farei” em sua vida?
  2. Você está apática e se perguntando qual é o sentido da vida?
  3. Está enfrentando depressão?
  4. Tem dificuldades com suas prioridades e falta de motivação para mudá-las?
  5. Seus filhos precisam de mais palavras de encorajamento?
  6. Você tem dificuldades com hábitos alimentares prejudiciais?
  7. Está presa às engrenagens de padrões de pensamento negativos?
  8. Está resistindo aos desejos e à liderança de seu marido?

Boas intenções e mudança muitas vezes estão separadas apenas pela falta de fé e motivação. Muitas vezes não entendemos o quanto Deus se importa intimamente com essas emoções e problemas em nossa vida e espera para ver nossa disposição de mudar. Quando damos o primeiro passo de obediência, sua graça está ali para realizar o milagre. A mentalidade do “Vou tentar” traz apatia e derrota. O “Eu farei” abre o inesgotável estoque da graça de Deus. Cada dia traz centenas de pequenas decisões. A maneira como reagimos a essas decisões acaba por formar a mulher que nos tornamos e a mulher que seremos na velhice.

Maria, a futura mãe de Jesus, certo dia se viu de repente diante de um anjo. As palavras dele a perturbaram, e ela “ponderava” sobre o que ele lhe dizia. Ela poderia ter permitido que o medo a dominasse diante do que as palavras do anjo significavam para ela. Em vez disso, disse: “Eis aqui a serva do Senhor; faça-se em mim segundo a tua palavra”. Ela escolheu a fé, e isso impactou o mundo de maneiras que jamais poderia ter imaginado.

Foi uma escolha. Uma escolha para a qual ela não podia levar dias ou semanas se preparando. No entanto, sua participação no plano de Deus para a salvação do mundo dependia dessa escolha.

Ester, a rainha, enfrentou um dilema sério. Seu povo corria o risco de ser exterminado pelo perverso Hamã. Mordecai lhe disse que ela era rainha para um momento como aquele e que deveria ir ao rei e implorar por sua ajuda. Seu coração tremia. Ela conhecia bem as regras do rei: quem se aventurasse a entrar em seu palácio sem convite provavelmente seria morto. Mas ela escolheu a coragem… “Se perecer, pereci”. Ela faria o que pudesse por seu povo, independentemente do custo.

Foi apenas uma escolha. No entanto, a segurança de seu povo e o milagre de sua libertação vieram por meio de sua disposição de fazer uma escolha tão difícil.

Atitudes e emoções — negativas ou positivas — são escolhas ocultas que temos de fazer. O que você escolherá: o “Vou tentar” sem fé ou o corajoso “Eu farei”? Você escolherá, pela graça de Deus, fazer a escolha certa? Deus prometeu aperfeiçoar as coisas que dizem respeito a você, mas não fará sua obra em sua vida sem o seu “Eu farei”. A escolha é sua.

E Deus é poderoso para fazer abundar em vós toda a graça, a fim de que, tendo sempre, em tudo, toda a suficiência, abundeis em toda boa obra: –2 Coríntios 9:8.

Meet the doctor who wrote this article for our medical column. (See the editorial under the section “continued changes” for further details.)

Hello,

My full name is Vincent “John” Bradford Waldron (I go by John) and I am a Family Physician in south central Virginia. My family and I attend church at Bethel Mennonite Church in Gladys, Virginia. My wife, Elaine, and I have been married since 2002 and have five children. I have been in practice for twenty years; the first seventeen I practiced in southern Indiana.

Currently, I practice in an outpatient setting taking care of patients in the small town of Brookneal. My vision is to care for people as Jesus would. I want to share the Gospel with those who need it and to minister to the needs of those who are hurting. The majority of my patients are not from a conservative Anabaptist background and perhaps the only way they will see Jesus is through me.

John

Editor’s Note:

Currently, the details are changing, sometimes daily, regarding the vaccines, the unexpected problems associated with providing the vaccines to the vast multitudes of the world’s population, and the potential side effects developing from receiving the vaccine. This article was first written prior to the first vaccines being available, since then it has been revised at least twice.

We realize there are many unknowns surrounding this whole issue. It is with this in mind that we have tried to be as balanced as possible as we have considered the information that was available at the time of writing. We plan to keep our ears tuned to the progression of these situations. And we will do our best to continue investigating and evaluating concerns that are directed our way. If the Lord wills, we plan to print updated information regarding these issues in succeeding issues of the magazine.

Bottomline, as a board, we second the comments found in Larry Zook’s article (Admonition for Uncertain Times) found in this issue of the magazine… “Informed Consent and Getting a Second Opinion—both have been the long-standing ethical basis of decision-making in choosing medical treatment. I hope we retain both.”

Coronavirus vaccines are in the news these days. When the first vaccines were finally considered ‘safe’ for use by the medical community the initial focus was on England as many “Brits” were among the first to receive the vaccine including one man, who interestingly enough, has the name of William Shakespeare. As of the writing of this article, here in the U.S., the FDA has approved the initial Covid-19 vaccines developed by Moderna and Pfizer.

The Initial Vaccines

The first two vaccines that have come out and been approved were vaccines that used synthetic mRNA (messenger RNA). In cells, DNA encodes the different proteins that cells need to produce in order to function. The only thing is that no proteins are actually made in the nucleus, they are actually made in the ribosomes of the cell. So, the cell needs a messenger to go from the nucleus to the ribosomes and carry those instructions. That messenger is mRNA.

The mRNA takes the messages from the nucleus to the ribosomes. After a time the message degrades, and the ribosomes stop making that particular protein.

In the case of mRNA vaccines, the synthetic mRNA in the vaccine encodes a protein that looks like the spike protein on the COVID virus. As cells make this protein, the body’s immune system will identify those proteins as foreign and begin to create antibodies to them.

Does mRNA Change DNA?

I know that there is much fear around the idea that these vaccines will change our genetic code. This, of course, could be really dangerous. Fortunately, the mRNA doesn’t make its way to the nucleus and instead is only active where proteins are made. This technology (mRNA vaccines) is quite different than stem cell gene therapies, and the various gene-editing therapies, such as CRISPR. Both of these fields of therapy do affect a person at the level of their genes, but the mRNA vaccine does not.

Effectiveness

In the studies that looked at the two mRNA vaccines, we found that they were quite effective. There were only 8 cases of COVID identified in the patients seven days after the second dose of the Pfizer vaccine, while in those who got the placebo vaccine, there were 162 cases in that same period. Looking at severe cases, there was only one case in the vaccine group (this happened between the first and second doses) and nine cases of severe COVID in the placebo group.1 The Moderna vaccine showed similar effectiveness.2

There is still a question out there. Do these vaccines actually prevent all COVID infections or do they just turn COVID infections into low-symptom or no-symptom infections? Currently, studies are being done to look at this. The only way to know is to run antibody testing on patients who have gotten the COVID vaccine for proteins that are not in the vaccine. So, for instance, there is a protein called the “n” protein that is in a different part of the virus. Someone who has had the vaccine, but not an infection with COVID will not have an antibody to this protein, while someone who has had an actual COVID infection will have this antibody as well as an antibody to the spike protein.

In the meantime, everyone, even those who have received the vaccine, will still need to practice extra caution, such as wearing masks, hand washing, and social distancing, at least until we know for sure whether or not it’s possible to get infections (even with the vaccine) and how contagious these potential infections may be.

Side Effects of COVID Vaccine

The most common side effects that have been noted so far has been arm soreness. This usually lasts for one to three days and then resolves. Many people also often feel tired and achy. They may even run low-grade fevers for one to two days after getting the injections. However, this seems to be a bigger issue with the second injection.

There have been isolated allergic reactions to the vaccines as well. The rate of anaphylaxis (severe allergy) to COVID vaccine does seem to be somewhat higher when compared with other vaccines. Because of this, it is recommended that people get vaccinated in locations where there is treatment available to take care of such a reaction and that they should stay for a minimum of 15 minutes after the shot (or 30 minutes if they normally carry an epi pen).3

Updated Side Effects

In the last several weeks, nearly 15 million people in the United States have gotten at least one dose of the COVID vaccines. There have been a lot more doses given around the world. As we have done this, certain things have been clearer as far as side effects.

Anaphylaxis is the most serious “common” side effect. The CDC is saying that the rate of serious allergy to the Moderna and Pfizer vaccines is about 11 per million doses given. This sort of an allergy requires medications like epinephrine to reverse it and is seen with other vaccines and medications too.

In Norway, nearly all of the patients in nursing homes were vaccinated against COVID.4 In the subsequent six days, 23 of the frailest of those died. At this point, it is being investigated as to whether or not the vaccine contributed in any way to those deaths. From what we know, those patients weren’t in good health prior to the vaccine, but I think I would probably avoid giving the vaccine to people who are in extremely poor health (understanding that if those folks get COVID they probably wouldn’t do well either).

A lot of people have had muscle pains, chills and even low-grade fevers after the second dose of vaccine. Several of my co-workers had these sorts of symptoms and all of them resolved within 48 hours of getting the vaccine.

I think one last thing to remember is that just because something happens after you get vaccinated, it does not mean the vaccine caused it. So, if you get a shot and then get hit by a car, clearly the shot didn’t cause the accident. One possible example of this is a doctor in Florida who got a COVID vaccine and then developed really low platelet counts and eventually died. There is no indication that the vaccination caused the low platelet count and we have not seen this in any other patients who have gotten vaccinated for COVID. The guess is simply that he was probably developing this disorder already and that the vaccine didn’t cause it or affect it.

Simply put, when you give millions of doses of anything, there will always be some who develop other illnesses soon after getting the medicine or vaccine. The challenge is to figure out what is related to the therapy and what is just “noise.”

Ethical Issues

Other than the two vaccines listed above, there are many others being researched and developed. Some of these vaccines are grown on cell lines that were derived from babies that were aborted in the 70s and 80s. I need to be clear that there are no ongoing abortions being utilized to make any vaccines.

In light of this, the one good thing is that the Pfizer and Moderna vaccines are not grown on these fetal cell lines.

Other Vaccines

Janssen (Johnson and Johnson) Pharmaceuticals and Astra Zeneca are both working on vaccines that are more traditional vaccines—that is they grow the virus, then kill it, and then give small doses of the killed virus to trigger the immune response. create immunity. The Astra Zeneca vaccine probably will be released before too long. The studies on it are a little more unclear with regard to its effectiveness.

The important thing with these vaccines is that they are both grown on HEK293 fetal cells, which are derived from an aborted infant.

There are a number of other vaccines that are a little further away from release, but there is one from Merck is a non-mRNA vaccine that is also ethically sourced (not grown on aborted fetal cells). The Lozier Institute has a web page that lists which vaccines use fetal cell lines and which ones do not.5

Other Questions

There have been a number of questions about who was behind these vaccines and a variety of concerns with respect to their development. Some have even speculated about companies introducing a “microchip” into the vaccines.

The needles being used to administer these vaccines are a very small caliber (21 gauge or smaller) which makes it unlikely that a microchip could be administered through such a needle. It seems probable that to administer a microchip, it would require a significantly larger needle than the ones being recommended, (the microchips that are normally used in pets are roughly the size of a kernel of rice).

Making a Decision

Is it worthwhile to get one of these vaccines, and, if so, which one?

The biggest reason to get a COVID vaccine is to avoid the possible long-term effects of a COVID infection. In some people, COVID produces chronic fatigue, a long-term cough, and “brain fog.” Getting one of these vaccines certainly would help to avoid those disease-induced problems along with the possibility that COVID could also cause some heart damage.6

What if You’ve Had COVID already?

Many in our circles have already had COVID. If you know you had COVID then probably the best thing to do is to wait. There is no particular reason to run out and get vaccinated, since we believe your antibodies should remain active for three to six months. In studies, they did seem to decline over time, but folks who had COVID should be immune for a minimum of 3 months and probably longer.

It seems most reasonable to wait and see if one of the vaccines shows itself to be superior, with regard either to effectiveness or fewer side effects, than the others.

Who Should Not Get Vaccinated?

Currently, there are certain people who should not get the vaccine. The first category are groups that weren’t in the studies. So, children under the age of 16, pregnant women, and nursing mothers should all avoid the COVID vaccines for the time being. It may be that the vaccine would be safe for people in these groups, but since they weren’t tested, they shouldn’t get it for now.

Secondly, if you actively have COVID or are currently isolating because of being exposed to it, you shouldn’t get the vaccine. I suppose this makes sense as we don’t typically give vaccinations to people who are already sick.

Finally, you should be careful if you have a history of severe reactions to other vaccines.

Everyone else

If someone has not had a COVID infection, I would certainly lean towards getting the vaccine. Personally, I have started getting vaccinated using the Pfizer vaccine and feel comfortable with that. For those who are working in health care, I would lean towards getting one of the vaccines. The issue for me is not the risk of infection to me, rather my concern as a Christian doctor is the danger that I might pass COVID on to one of my patients.

If you are caring for the elderly and have not had a COVID infection, I would also think strongly about getting vaccinated. Once again, the primary concern should not be how you will handle the infection, but instead who you might pass that infection on to.

Conclusion

I understand that others’ comfort level may be lower with these new vaccines and if that is the case, I would wait. These vaccines are being given to millions of people and if there are issues, they will become apparent fairly quickly.

Finally, I am glad that there are going to be several ethically sourced vaccines available to those who desire them.

Hej,

Mitt fullständiga namn är Vincent ”John” Bradford Waldron (jag kallas John), och jag är familjeläkare i södra centrala Virginia. Min familj och jag går i Bethel Mennonite Church i Gladys, Virginia. Min fru Elaine och jag har varit gifta sedan 2002 och har fem barn. Jag har arbetat som läkare i tjugo år; de första sjutton åren arbetade jag i södra Indiana.

För närvarande arbetar jag i öppenvården och tar hand om patienter i den lilla orten Brookneal. Min vision är att ta hand om människor så som Jesus skulle göra. Jag vill dela evangeliet med dem som behöver det och tjäna dem som lider. De flesta av mina patienter har inte en konservativ anabaptistisk bakgrund, och kanske är det bara genom mig som de kommer att få se Jesus.

John

De första vaccinerna

De två första vaccinerna som kom ut och godkändes var vacciner som använde syntetiskt mRNA (budbärar-RNA). I cellerna kodar DNA för de olika proteiner som cellerna behöver tillverka för att fungera. Men proteiner tillverkas faktiskt inte i cellkärnan, utan i cellens ribosomer. Cellen behöver alltså en budbärare som går från cellkärnan till ribosomerna och bär med sig instruktionerna. Den budbäraren är mRNA.

mRNA för med sig meddelandena från cellkärnan till ribosomerna. Efter en tid bryts meddelandet ned och ribosomerna slutar tillverka det aktuella proteinet.

När det gäller mRNA-vacciner kodar det syntetiska mRNA:t i vaccinet för ett protein som liknar spikproteinet på covidviruset. När cellerna tillverkar detta protein känner kroppens immunförsvar igen proteinerna som främmande och börjar bilda antikroppar mot dem.

Förändrar mRNA DNA?

Jag vet att många är rädda för att dessa vacciner ska förändra vår genetiska kod. Det skulle naturligtvis kunna vara mycket farligt. Lyckligtvis tar sig mRNA inte in i cellkärnan, utan är bara aktivt där proteiner tillverkas. Denna teknik (mRNA-vacciner) skiljer sig mycket från genterapier med stamceller och olika genredigeringsterapier, till exempel CRISPR. Båda dessa behandlingsområden påverkar en person på gennivå, men mRNA-vaccinet gör inte det.

Effektivitet

I studierna av de två mRNA-vaccinerna fann man att de var mycket effektiva. Sju dagar efter den andra dosen av Pfizer-vaccinet hade endast 8 fall av covid konstaterats bland patienterna, medan 162 fall under samma period konstaterades bland dem som hade fått placebovaccinet. Om man ser till allvarliga fall fanns det bara ett fall i vaccingruppen (det inträffade mellan den första och den andra dosen) och nio fall av allvarlig covid i placebogruppen.1 Modernas vaccin visade liknande effektivitet.2

En fråga återstår. Förhindrar dessa vacciner verkligen alla covidinfektioner, eller gör de bara att covidinfektioner ger få eller inga symtom? Studier pågår för att undersöka detta. Det enda sättet att få veta är att testa antikroppar hos patienter som har fått covidvaccinet, mot proteiner som inte ingår i vaccinet. Det finns till exempel ett protein som kallas ”n”-proteinet i en annan del av viruset. Den som har fått vaccinet men inte haft en covidinfektion kommer inte att ha antikroppar mot detta protein, medan den som har haft en faktisk covidinfektion också kommer att ha sådana antikroppar, utöver antikroppar mot spikproteinet.

Under tiden behöver alla, även de som har fått vaccinet, fortfarande iaktta extra försiktighet, till exempel genom att använda munskydd, tvätta händerna och hålla avstånd, åtminstone tills vi säkert vet om det går att bli smittad (även efter vaccination) och hur smittsamma sådana eventuella infektioner kan vara.

Biverkningar av covidvaccinet

Den vanligaste biverkningen som hittills har noterats är ömhet i armen. Den varar vanligtvis i en till tre dagar och går sedan över. Många känner sig också ofta trötta och ömma i kroppen. De kan till och med få lätt feber under en till två dagar efter injektionen. Detta verkar dock vara ett större problem efter den andra injektionen.

Det har också förekommit enstaka allergiska reaktioner mot vaccinerna. Förekomsten av anafylaxi (allvarlig allergisk reaktion) efter covidvaccin verkar vara något högre jämfört med andra vacciner. Därför rekommenderas det att människor vaccineras på platser där behandling finns tillgänglig för att hantera en sådan reaktion och att de stannar kvar i minst 15 minuter efter sprutan (eller 30 minuter om de vanligtvis bär med sig en adrenalinpenna).3

Uppdatering om biverkningar

Under de senaste veckorna har närmare 15 miljoner människor i USA fått minst en dos av covidvaccinerna. Många fler doser har getts runt om i världen. I takt med detta har vissa saker kring biverkningarna blivit tydligare.

Anafylaxi är den allvarligaste ”vanliga” biverkningen. CDC uppger att frekvensen av allvarliga allergiska reaktioner mot Modernas och Pfizers vacciner är omkring 11 per miljon givna doser. En sådan allergisk reaktion kräver läkemedel som adrenalin för att hävas, och den förekommer även med andra vacciner och läkemedel.

I Norge vaccinerades nästan alla patienter på vårdhem mot covid.4 Under de följande sex dagarna dog 23 av de sköraste patienterna. För närvarande undersöker man om vaccinet på något sätt bidrog till dessa dödsfall. Enligt vad vi vet var patienterna inte vid god hälsa före vaccinationen, men jag tror att jag nog skulle undvika att ge vaccinet till personer som är vid extremt dålig hälsa (samtidigt som jag förstår att de förmodligen inte heller skulle klara sig bra om de fick covid).

Många har fått muskelvärk, frossa och till och med lätt feber efter den andra vaccindosen. Flera av mina kollegor hade sådana symtom, och de gick alla över inom 48 timmar efter vaccinationen.

En sista sak att komma ihåg är att om något händer efter att man har blivit vaccinerad betyder det inte att vaccinet orsakade det. Om du till exempel får en spruta och sedan blir påkörd av en bil, så orsakade sprutan uppenbarligen inte olyckan. Ett möjligt exempel på detta är en läkare i Florida som fick ett covidvaccin och därefter utvecklade mycket låga trombocytvärden och till slut dog. Det finns inget som tyder på att vaccinationen orsakade det låga trombocytvärdet, och vi har inte sett detta hos någon annan som har vaccinerats mot covid. Man antar helt enkelt att han förmodligen redan höll på att utveckla den här sjukdomen och att vaccinet varken orsakade den eller påverkade den.

Enkelt uttryckt kommer det alltid att finnas några som utvecklar andra sjukdomar kort efter att ha fått ett läkemedel eller vaccin, när man ger miljontals doser av vad som helst. Utmaningen är att ta reda på vad som har samband med behandlingen och vad som bara är ”brus”.

Etiska frågor

Förutom de två vacciner som nämnts ovan undersöks och utvecklas många andra. Vissa av dessa vacciner odlas på cellinjer som härrör från barn som aborterades på 70- och 80-talen. Jag vill vara tydlig med att inga pågående aborter används för att framställa några vacciner.

Mot den bakgrunden är en positiv sak att Pfizers och Modernas vacciner inte odlas på dessa fostercellinjer.

Andra vacciner

Janssen (Johnson and Johnson) Pharmaceuticals och Astra Zeneca arbetar båda med mer traditionella vacciner – det vill säga att man odlar viruset, dödar det och sedan ger små doser av det avdödade viruset för att utlösa immunförsvaret och skapa immunitet. Astra Zenecas vaccin kommer troligen att släppas inom kort. Studierna av det är något mer oklara när det gäller effektiviteten.

Det viktiga med dessa vacciner är att båda odlas på fosterceller av typen HEK293, som härrör från ett aborterat spädbarn.

Det finns ett antal andra vacciner som ligger lite längre fram i tiden innan de kan släppas, men ett vaccin från Merck är ett icke-mRNA-vaccin som också har en etisk tillverkningskedja (odlas inte på aborterade fosterceller). Lozier Institute har en webbsida med en lista över vilka vacciner som använder fostercellinjer och vilka som inte gör det.5

Andra frågor

Det har ställts ett antal frågor om vilka som ligger bakom vaccinerna och olika farhågor kring deras utveckling. En del har till och med spekulerat i att företag skulle föra in ett ”mikrochip” i vaccinerna.

Kanylerna som används för att ge dessa vacciner har mycket liten diameter (21 gauge eller mindre), vilket gör det osannolikt att ett mikrochip skulle kunna injiceras genom en sådan kanyl. Det verkar troligt att det skulle krävas en betydligt större kanyl än de rekommenderade för att föra in ett mikrochip (mikrochipp som vanligtvis används på husdjur är ungefär lika stora som ett riskorn).

Att fatta ett beslut

Är det värt att ta ett av dessa vacciner, och i så fall vilket?

Det främsta skälet att ta ett covidvaccin är att undvika möjliga långtidseffekter av en covidinfektion. Hos vissa människor leder covid till kronisk trötthet, långvarig hosta och ”hjärndimma”. Att ta ett av dessa vacciner skulle helt klart hjälpa till att undvika dessa sjukdomsrelaterade problem och även den möjliga hjärtskada som covid också kan orsaka.6

Vad händer om du redan har haft covid?

Många i våra kretsar har redan haft covid. Om du vet att du har haft covid är det förmodligen bäst att vänta. Det finns ingen särskild anledning att skynda sig iväg och vaccinera sig, eftersom vi tror att dina antikroppar bör förbli aktiva i tre till sex månader. I studier verkade de minska med tiden, men personer som har haft covid bör vara immuna i minst 3 månader och sannolikt längre.

Det verkar mest rimligt att vänta och se om något av vaccinerna visar sig vara bättre än de andra, antingen när det gäller effektivitet eller färre biverkningar.

Vilka bör inte vaccineras?

För närvarande finns det vissa personer som inte bör få vaccinet. Den första gruppen är de som inte ingick i studierna. Barn under 16 år, gravida och ammande bör därför alla avstå från covidvaccinerna tills vidare. Det kan hända att vaccinet skulle vara säkert för personer i dessa grupper, men eftersom det inte har testats på dem bör de inte få det just nu.

För det andra bör du inte få vaccinet om du har covid just nu eller isolerar dig efter att ha blivit utsatt för smitta. Jag antar att detta är rimligt, eftersom vi vanligtvis inte vaccinerar människor som redan är sjuka.

Slutligen bör du vara försiktig om du tidigare har fått allvarliga reaktioner av andra vacciner.

Alla andra

Om någon inte har haft en covidinfektion skulle jag helt klart luta åt att rekommendera vaccination. Själv har jag börjat vaccinera mig med Pfizers vaccin och känner mig trygg med det. För dem som arbetar inom vården skulle jag luta åt att rekommendera ett av vaccinerna. För mig handlar frågan inte om risken att själv bli smittad, utan som kristen läkare oroar jag mig för risken att föra covid vidare till en av mina patienter.

Om du tar hand om äldre och inte har haft en covidinfektion skulle jag också starkt överväga att du vaccinerar dig. Återigen bör den främsta oron inte vara hur du själv skulle klara infektionen, utan vem du skulle kunna föra den vidare till.

Slutsats

Jag förstår att andra kan känna sig mindre trygga med dessa nya vacciner, och om det är så skulle jag vänta. Miljontals människor får dessa vacciner, och om det finns problem kommer de att bli synliga ganska snabbt.

Slutligen är jag glad att det kommer att finnas flera vacciner med en etisk tillverkningskedja tillgängliga för dem som önskar dem.

Greetings of Christian love to each one. Hopefully, you have found Christ as the anchor for your soul and the solution to your difficulties. Another year is past and gone, and what a year it was… An unseen virus encircling the world, unsettling cultures from third-world countries to the most advanced and industrialized. World leaders blaming each other for the ever-increasing pandemic as their country’s economies continued to spiral downward. And churches struggling to maintain unity in the midst of their various government’s mandates regarding social distancing, mask wearing, and limits on the size of gatherings.

For many, the year 2020 has destroyed or radically altered that which used to be considered normal and has begun establishing new norms and many things may never be the same again. ‘Six feet’ has become a well-recognized unit of measurement. The sound of coughing draws glances from those within hearing distance. Mask wearing has become the focus of jokes and endless arguments regarding the pros and cons.

Through it all, many have suffered in various ways. Most importantly, I wonder if we have considered the spiritual fallout happening to those around us?

I have heard numerous reports of folks who couldn’t handle the loss of fellowship when their local church completely stopped having in-person worship services. Some silently pined away, growing increasingly disillusioned with Christianity. Others, deciding this was ‘the straw that broke their camel’s back’, took action and left their old church, then joined a new group that was more supportive of their views. There were, however, many churches that chose to “obey God rather than man” and continued to quietly meet for worship.

Conscience in Crisis

This issue alone (governments telling churches how and when to worship) has been the cause of much discussion, disorder, and even dissension in many churches. We are facing unprecedented times. For most of us, we don’t have any experience in our past to fall back on which will help us make a clear decision. Some Christians’ consciences will not allow them peace while ‘disobeying the civil authorities’, while other Christians’ consciences will not allow them peace while ‘forsaking the assembling of themselves together’. Somehow, this “intrusion” of government into the everyday life of the church just hasn’t seemed quite right.

During the 1600s and the 1700s, our Anabaptist forefathers emigrated from Europe to foreign countries in search of a new home where they were free to worship as their conscience directed. Ever since, one of the key aspects of living in America has been that of the “separation of church and state”. So, it was with uncertainty and trepidation that we, conservative Anabaptists, have considered that which our local, state, or federal governments have asked of us. One thing that I am extremely grateful for is that the leaders of our local fellowship have maintained very strong admonishment throughout this time, that: “As we sort through each new challenge that comes our way, we must ALWAYS exhibit a godly respect (in thought, in word, and in action) for our civil authorities”, especially if we find it necessary to “obey God rather than man”.

Another major point of concern was that of the United States elections at the end of 2020. Somehow, this country has become more and more polarized over the last four years, (maybe it has been longer). I heard a report of one man from the world who said that if Trump doesn’t win the election then he sees no hope to continue living and he is contemplating whether he should just take his own life and end it all. Sure, a man of the world may not have the hope of a better life to come since he probably doesn’t see himself as a “stranger and a pilgrim” here on this earth and most likely he doesn’t believe in life eternal. But what about those of us who claim to be Christians, are we doing any better? Are we responding to each situation in fear or in faith?

All of this upheaval in our ‘normal’ way of life, has brought uncertainty. Uncertainty about jobs. Uncertainty about our future. Uncertainty about our families. Uncertainty about the end of time. And the list could go on with each person filling in the blanks for him or herself.

The Vaccines

The most recent issue of upheaval that is taking front stage both in our minds and in our conversations is that of the vaccine. Will it be “forced” upon us? Are there properties included in this new type of vaccine that will enable others to ‘track’ us and listen in to all our private conversations? Is it true that there is somehow a microchip, or a multitude of nano robots immersed in that small volume of liquid? Will this new technology that has been manufactured as a synthetic mRNA vaccine somehow change my DNA if I allow them to prick my skin? Is this vaccine the mark of the beast? All these, and more, are questions which I have been hearing with ever-increasing frequency and urgency.

Conspiracy Theories

The uncertainty of it all (the virus, the election, and the vaccine) has spawned many, many conspiracy theories. Usually, if there is a negative connotation surrounding something, then we tend to close ourselves to the possibility that we may be involved. “Surely, the ideas that I am passing on are not a conspiracy theory!”

Or are they? Let’s stop and think about this a minute. Conspiracy = a secret plan by a group to do something unlawful or harmful. Theory = a supposition or a system of ideas intended to explain something. Doesn’t this fit most of the allegations and claims that have been circulated among us? Almost every new ‘story’ will claim that ‘certain’ people are secretly involved in an all-encompassing agenda to use this certain negative issue of upheaval to bring about a specific negative change that will harm the masses. Most often these ‘stories’ are designed to play on our emotions, triggering a response rooted in fear, that is ultimately designed to protect myself from the alleged personal harm—that of being personally controlled by others, loss of personal rights, loss of personal privacy, etc., etc.

If we are honest about the actual definition of ‘conspiracy’ and of ‘theory’, then we would also need to admit that many, if not most, of the ‘stories’ that are spreading through the rumor-mill are indeed conspiracy theories. I am not suggesting that we bury our heads in the sand, or that we shouldn’t be a prepared people. I am simply cautioning against being sucked into the emotional rhetoric of the many ‘stories’ that are continually being promoted.

There are some questions we can ask ourselves that will help to sort through the confusion of all the various claims or allegations being made. Am I being asked to join the fight to protect the Constitution of the United States? Am I being advised to join others in standing up for our ‘rights’? If I stop and consider what’s happening in my heart, what is motivating me to action—Faith? or Fear? If there is any truth in that which is being alleged, is there anything that I can do about it?

Like I said before, we are facing unprecedented times. Let’s face our future with faith—our God is sovereignly in control. Let’s not lose sight of our future home in heaven—we are called to be strangers and pilgrims in this world. Let’s always remember the promises of God—that He will be with us always even unto the end of the world, and that He will NOT allow us to be tempted above that which we are able to bear. These promises and many, many more are clearly specified in the Scriptures.

The virus hits home

My (Curvin’s) family contracted the Covid-19 virus in the middle of October 2020. It affected each of our family members in slightly different ways, which was interesting to observe. One of the intriguing aspects was that most of us lost our sense of taste and smell. Most of our family didn’t suffer more than we normally would with the normal flu. However, my mother, who lives with us, ended up on the very verge of needing to be hospitalized due to low oxygen levels in her blood. Thankfully, this was averted through a doctor prescribing some potent drugs which had an almost immediate effect on reversing this.

For myself, I was so sick from the virus that I wasn’t able to work for over two months. The only thing that kept me out of the hospital was a daily intake of one restricted drug and double the recommended dose of steroids through nebulizer treatments. This went on for over six weeks. It is now almost two months since I finally started to recover and yet I am still not fully back to where I was prior to contracting Covid-19.

On a side note, we have included an article bringing recognition to the life of Mose Stoltzfus, an older brother from one of our sister churches who died after contracting Covid-19. Considering these two situations, I can say of a surety that the virus is real and not a hoax; that the virus affects everybody in slightly different ways; that some people have hardly any ill effects even though they do contract the virus; and that there are some who do become very ill indeed.

The Vaccine booklet

Back a number of issues we ran a number of articles written by a doctor on the whole issue of vaccines. Our goal was to try to present as balanced of a view as possible. We had numerous requests to have those articles compiled into a booklet format, which we had announced previously that we were planning to do. We encountered a number of practical issues that needed to be sorted through, which took time (much longer than we had anticipated). Finally, we have now arrived at the point of being ready to compile and publish this booklet.

If you want to receive one or more copies of this booklet, we ask that you contact us with your contact information and the number of booklets desired, even if you have previously done so. This will help us gauge the interest level to know how many we should print. We can be reached by mail, phone, or email, each of which can be found inside the front cover of each issue of our magazine, The Heartbeat of the Remnant.

Continued Changes

Over the last year or two we have pursued various ways of streamlining our production efforts. One of these, which we have mentioned before is that of working towards having multiple authors write articles for the various specific columns, such as the Children’s Corner, Sister to Sister, A Word from The Doctor, etc. One of the changes you will see is that we will have more than one doctor writing articles for the medical column.

Finances

As you will notice, we have included a financial report in this issue for the year of 2020. A year ago, we had made known through our annual newsletter that things were quite desperate for us financially and that we needed funds if we were going to keep going forward. The response was overwhelming, and we have been blessed by all who decided to partner with us in this need. However, as you can see by the financial report, there is a need for continued financial support since our expenses are ongoing. For those of you who are actively involved in this way, we say thank you and may God richly bless your generosity.

A Point of Interest

The children’s story in this issue of the magazine holds special interest for me. While the details of the story may not all be according to fact, there was a John M. and Catharine Kurtz family that lost five children in infancy and then years later they lost six children to diphtheria. Only John S. Kurtz survived, but was joined by two younger siblings later on. John was ordained to the ministry at the age of 27 and married Maria Horning almost two years later.

John S. and Maria (Horning) Kurtz were my great, great grandparents. So, that line of my ancestry can be traced back through the time of another pandemic and tremendous upheaval in people’s lives, through that of the only surviving child out of a family of 12. For me, this brings personal interest and perspective to some of the situations we are facing today.

May God bless and keep each one. As the world becomes ever darker and more chaotic, let us as Christians draw ever closer to our Lord. In this, He has given a command containing a promise for each of us to: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded –James 4:8.

Curvin L Wenger

Christliche Grüße in Liebe an jeden Einzelnen. Hoffentlich habt ihr Christus als Anker eurer Seele und als Lösung für eure Schwierigkeiten gefunden. Ein weiteres Jahr ist vergangen, und was für ein Jahr es war … Ein unsichtbares Virus umkreiste die Welt und brachte Kulturen von Ländern der Dritten Welt bis hin zu den am weitesten entwickelten und industrialisierten Ländern aus dem Gleichgewicht. Weltführer machten einander für die immer weiter zunehmende Pandemie verantwortlich, während die Wirtschaft ihres jeweiligen Landes immer weiter abrutschte. Und Gemeinden bemühten sich, die Einheit aufrechtzuerhalten, während ihre jeweiligen Regierungen Vorschriften zu sozialer Distanzierung, zum Tragen von Masken und zur Begrenzung der Größe von Versammlungen erließen.

Für viele hat das Jahr 2020 das zerstört oder grundlegend verändert, was früher als normal galt, und neue Normalitäten haben sich herausgebildet. Vieles wird vielleicht nie wieder so sein wie zuvor. „Sechs Fuß“ ist zu einer weithin bekannten Maßeinheit geworden. Husten lässt die Menschen in Hörweite Blicke zuwerfen. Das Tragen von Masken ist zum Gegenstand von Witzen und endlosen Diskussionen über Vor- und Nachteile geworden.

All dies hat vielen auf unterschiedliche Weise zu schaffen gemacht. Vor allem frage ich mich, ob wir bedacht haben, welche geistlichen Folgen sich für die Menschen um uns herum ergeben?

Ich habe zahlreiche Berichte von Leuten gehört, die den Verlust der Gemeinschaft nicht verkrafteten, als ihre Ortsgemeinde die Gottesdienste mit persönlicher Anwesenheit vollständig einstellte. Einige litten still vor sich hin und wurden zunehmend desillusioniert vom Christentum. Andere entschieden, dies sei „der Tropfen, der das Fass zum Überlaufen bringt“, handelten danach und verließen ihre bisherige Gemeinde; anschließend schlossen sie sich einer neuen Gruppe an, die ihre Ansichten stärker unterstützte. Es gab jedoch viele Gemeinden, die beschlossen, „Gott mehr zu gehorchen als den Menschen“ und sich weiterhin still zum Gottesdienst zu versammeln.

Das Gewissen in der Krise

Allein dieses Thema (dass Regierungen Gemeinden vorschreiben, wie und wann sie Gottesdienst feiern sollen) hat in vielen Gemeinden zu zahlreichen Diskussionen, Unordnung und sogar Zwietracht geführt. Wir stehen vor beispiellosen Zeiten. Die meisten von uns haben keine Erfahrungen aus der Vergangenheit, auf die sie zurückgreifen könnten, um eine klare Entscheidung zu treffen. Manche Christen können keinen Frieden finden, wenn sie „den staatlichen Behörden nicht gehorchen“, während andere Christen keinen Frieden finden, wenn sie „das Zusammenkommen nicht versäumen“. Irgendwie hat sich dieser „Eingriff“ der Regierung in den Alltag der Gemeinde einfach nicht ganz richtig angefühlt.

Im 17. und 18. Jahrhundert wanderten unsere täuferischen Vorväter aus Europa in fremde Länder aus, auf der Suche nach einer neuen Heimat, in der sie frei nach ihrem Gewissen Gottesdienst feiern konnten. Seitdem ist einer der entscheidenden Aspekte des Lebens in Amerika die „Trennung von Kirche und Staat“. So haben wir konservativen Täufer mit Unsicherheit und Bangen erwogen, was unsere örtlichen, bundesstaatlichen oder Bundesregierungen von uns verlangt haben. Eine Sache, für die ich äußerst dankbar bin, ist, dass die Leiter unserer örtlichen Gemeinschaft während dieser ganzen Zeit nachdrücklich ermahnt haben: „Während wir jede neue Herausforderung, die auf uns zukommt, prüfen, müssen wir unseren staatlichen Behörden IMMER eine gottgefällige Achtung entgegenbringen (in Gedanken, Worten und Taten)“, besonders dann, wenn wir es für notwendig halten, „Gott mehr zu gehorchen als den Menschen“.

Ein weiterer großer Anlass zur Sorge waren die Wahlen in den Vereinigten Staaten Ende 2020. Irgendwie ist dieses Land in den vergangenen vier Jahren (vielleicht auch schon länger) immer stärker polarisiert worden. Ich hörte von einem Mann aus der Welt, der sagte, wenn Trump die Wahl nicht gewinne, sehe er keine Hoffnung mehr, weiterzuleben, und überlege, ob er sich nicht einfach das Leben nehmen und allem ein Ende setzen solle. Natürlich hat ein Mann aus der Welt vielleicht nicht die Hoffnung auf ein besseres kommendes Leben, da er sich wahrscheinlich nicht als „Fremdling und Pilger“ auf dieser Erde sieht und höchstwahrscheinlich nicht an das ewige Leben glaubt. Aber wie steht es mit uns, die wir behaupten, Christen zu sein? Geht es uns besser? Reagieren wir auf jede Situation mit Furcht oder mit Glauben?

All diese Erschütterungen unserer „normalen“ Lebensweise haben Unsicherheit mit sich gebracht. Unsicherheit in Bezug auf die Arbeit. Unsicherheit in Bezug auf unsere Zukunft. Unsicherheit in Bezug auf unsere Familien. Unsicherheit in Bezug auf das Ende der Zeit. Und diese Liste könnte weitergehen, wobei jeder für sich die Lücken ausfüllt.

Die Impfstoffe

Das jüngste Thema, das sowohl in unseren Gedanken als auch in unseren Gesprächen im Mittelpunkt steht, ist der Impfstoff. Wird man ihn uns „aufzwingen“? Sind in dieser neuen Art von Impfstoff Bestandteile enthalten, die es anderen ermöglichen, uns zu „verfolgen“ und all unsere privaten Gespräche abzuhören? Stimmt es, dass sich darin irgendwie ein Mikrochip oder eine Vielzahl von Nanorobotern in dieser kleinen Flüssigkeitsmenge befinden? Wird diese neue Technologie, die als synthetischer mRNA-Impfstoff hergestellt wurde, irgendwie meine DNA verändern, wenn ich zulasse, dass man mir in die Haut sticht? Ist dieser Impfstoff das Zeichen des Tieres? All dies und noch mehr sind Fragen, die mir immer häufiger und dringlicher gestellt werden.

Verschwörungstheorien

Die Ungewissheit des Ganzen (des Virus, der Wahl und des Impfstoffs) hat sehr viele Verschwörungstheorien hervorgebracht. Wenn etwas negativ behaftet ist, neigen wir gewöhnlich dazu, uns der Möglichkeit zu verschließen, dass wir selbst darin verwickelt sein könnten. „Sicher sind die Gedanken, die ich weitergebe, keine Verschwörungstheorie!“

Oder doch? Halten wir einen Moment inne und denken darüber nach. Verschwörung = ein geheimer Plan einer Gruppe, etwas Unrechtes oder Schädliches zu tun. Theorie = eine Annahme oder ein Gedankensystem, das etwas erklären soll. Passt das nicht auf die meisten Anschuldigungen und Behauptungen, die unter uns verbreitet worden sind? Fast jede neue „Geschichte“ behauptet, dass „bestimmte“ Menschen heimlich an einer allumfassenden Agenda beteiligt seien, um dieses bestimmte negative Thema der Erschütterung auszunutzen und eine bestimmte negative Veränderung herbeizuführen, die den Massen schaden werde. Meistens sind diese „Geschichten“ darauf angelegt, mit unseren Gefühlen zu spielen und eine von Furcht geprägte Reaktion auszulösen, die letztlich dazu dienen soll, mich vor dem angeblichen persönlichen Schaden zu schützen – davor, von anderen persönlich kontrolliert zu werden, persönliche Rechte zu verlieren, die Privatsphäre einzubüßen usw. usw.

Wenn wir ehrlich mit der eigentlichen Definition von „Verschwörung“ und „Theorie“ umgehen, müssten wir auch zugeben, dass viele, wenn nicht die meisten der „Geschichten“, die sich über die Gerüchteküche verbreiten, tatsächlich Verschwörungstheorien sind. Ich schlage nicht vor, den Kopf in den Sand zu stecken oder unvorbereitet zu sein. Ich warne lediglich davor, sich von der emotionalen Rhetorik der vielen „Geschichten“ mitreißen zu lassen, die ständig verbreitet werden.

Wir können uns einige Fragen stellen, die uns helfen, die Verwirrung angesichts all der verschiedenen Behauptungen und Anschuldigungen zu ordnen. Wird von mir erwartet, mich dem Kampf zum Schutz der Verfassung der Vereinigten Staaten anzuschließen? Wird mir geraten, gemeinsam mit anderen für unsere „Rechte“ einzutreten? Wenn ich innehalte und bedenke, was in meinem Herzen vorgeht: Was treibt mich zum Handeln an – Glaube oder Furcht? Falls an den Behauptungen etwas Wahres ist, kann ich überhaupt etwas dagegen tun?

Wie ich bereits sagte, stehen wir vor beispiellosen Zeiten. Lasst uns unserer Zukunft im Glauben begegnen – unser Gott hat souverän alles unter Kontrolle. Lasst uns unsere zukünftige Heimat im Himmel nicht aus den Augen verlieren – wir sind berufen, Fremdlinge und Pilger in dieser Welt zu sein. Lasst uns stets an Gottes Verheißungen denken: dass er allezeit bei uns sein wird bis ans Ende der Welt und dass er nicht zulassen wird, dass wir über unser Vermögen versucht werden. Diese und viele, viele weitere Verheißungen sind in der Schrift klar festgehalten.

Das Virus trifft uns persönlich

Meine (Curvins) Familie infizierte sich Mitte Oktober 2020 mit dem Covid-19-Virus. Es wirkte sich auf jedes Familienmitglied etwas anders aus, was interessant zu beobachten war. Eine der bemerkenswerten Folgen war, dass die meisten von uns den Geschmacks- und Geruchssinn verloren. Die meisten in unserer Familie litten nicht stärker als bei einer gewöhnlichen Grippe. Meine Mutter jedoch, die bei uns wohnt, stand schließlich kurz davor, wegen eines niedrigen Sauerstoffgehalts in ihrem Blut ins Krankenhaus eingeliefert werden zu müssen. Glücklicherweise ließ sich das abwenden, als ein Arzt einige starke Medikamente verschrieb, die fast sofort eine Besserung bewirkten.

Ich selbst war durch das Virus so krank, dass ich über zwei Monate nicht arbeiten konnte. Nur die tägliche Einnahme eines Medikaments, dessen Verwendung eingeschränkt ist, und die doppelte empfohlene Dosis Steroide mittels Verneblerbehandlungen bewahrten mich vor einem Krankenhausaufenthalt. Das ging über sechs Wochen so. Seit ich mich endlich zu erholen begann, sind nun fast zwei Monate vergangen, und dennoch bin ich noch immer nicht vollständig wieder auf dem Stand vor meiner Covid-19-Erkrankung.

Am Rande sei erwähnt, dass wir einen Artikel aufgenommen haben, der an das Leben von Mose Stoltzfus erinnert, einem älteren Bruder aus einer unserer Schwesterngemeinden, der nach einer Covid-19-Erkrankung gestorben ist. Betrachtet man diese beiden Situationen, kann ich mit Sicherheit sagen, dass das Virus real und kein Schwindel ist; dass es jeden etwas anders trifft; dass manche Menschen kaum Beschwerden haben, obwohl sie sich mit dem Virus infizieren; und dass manche tatsächlich sehr schwer erkranken.

Das Impfbüchlein

Vor einigen Ausgaben veröffentlichten wir mehrere Artikel eines Arztes zum gesamten Thema Impfstoffe. Unser Ziel war, eine möglichst ausgewogene Sicht darzustellen. Wir erhielten zahlreiche Anfragen, diese Artikel in einem Büchlein zusammenzustellen, was wir bereits zuvor angekündigt hatten. Dabei stießen wir auf verschiedene praktische Fragen, die geklärt werden mussten, was Zeit in Anspruch nahm (viel mehr, als wir erwartet hatten). Nun sind wir endlich so weit, dieses Büchlein zusammenzustellen und zu veröffentlichen.

Wenn ihr ein oder mehrere Exemplare dieses Büchleins erhalten möchtet, bitten wir euch, uns eure Kontaktdaten und die gewünschte Anzahl mitzuteilen, auch wenn ihr dies bereits getan habt. So können wir das Interesse einschätzen und wissen, wie viele Exemplare wir drucken sollten. Ihr erreicht uns per Post, Telefon oder E-Mail; die jeweiligen Angaben findet ihr auf der Innenseite des vorderen Umschlags jeder Ausgabe unserer Zeitschrift The Heartbeat of the Remnant.

Weitere Veränderungen

Im vergangenen oder vorvergangenen Jahr haben wir verschiedene Möglichkeiten verfolgt, unsere Produktionsabläufe effizienter zu gestalten. Eine davon, die wir bereits erwähnt haben, ist unser Bestreben, mehrere Autoren Artikel für die verschiedenen festen Rubriken schreiben zu lassen, etwa die Kinderecke, Schwester zu Schwester, Ein Wort vom Arzt usw. Eine der Veränderungen, die euch auffallen wird, ist, dass künftig mehr als ein Arzt Beiträge für die medizinische Rubrik schreiben wird.

Finanzen

Wie ihr sehen werdet, haben wir in diese Ausgabe einen Finanzbericht für das Jahr 2020 aufgenommen. Vor einem Jahr hatten wir in unserem jährlichen Rundbrief mitgeteilt, dass unsere finanzielle Lage ziemlich verzweifelt war und wir Mittel benötigten, um weitermachen zu können. Die Reaktion war überwältigend, und wir sind durch alle gesegnet worden, die sich entschlossen haben, uns in dieser Notlage zu unterstützen. Wie dem Finanzbericht jedoch zu entnehmen ist, benötigen wir weiterhin finanzielle Unterstützung, da unsere Ausgaben fortlaufend anfallen. Allen, die sich aktiv daran beteiligen, danken wir und bitten Gott, eure Großzügigkeit reich zu segnen.

Ein interessanter Punkt

Die Kindergeschichte in dieser Ausgabe der Zeitschrift ist für mich von besonderem Interesse. Auch wenn vielleicht nicht alle Einzelheiten der Geschichte den Tatsachen entsprechen, gab es eine Familie von John M. und Catharine Kurtz, die fünf Kinder im Säuglingsalter verlor und Jahre später sechs Kinder an Diphtherie verlor. Nur John S. Kurtz überlebte; später kamen zwei jüngere Geschwister hinzu. John wurde im Alter von 27 Jahren zum Predigtdienst ordiniert und heiratete fast zwei Jahre später Maria Horning.

John S. und Maria (Horning) Kurtz waren meine Ururgroßeltern. So lässt sich dieser Zweig meiner Abstammung bis in die Zeit einer anderen Pandemie und großer Erschütterungen im Leben der Menschen zurückverfolgen – bis zu dem einzigen überlebenden Kind einer zwölfköpfigen Familie. Für mich verleihen diese Umstände einigen der Situationen, mit denen wir heute konfrontiert sind, eine persönliche Bedeutung und Perspektive.

Möge Gott jeden segnen und bewahren. Während die Welt immer dunkler und chaotischer wird, lasst uns Christen unserem Herrn immer näher kommen. Dazu hat er jedem von uns ein Gebot mit einer Verheißung gegeben: Naht euch Gott, so naht er sich euch. Reinigt die Hände, ihr Sünder, und läutert eure Herzen, ihr Wankelmütigen – Jakobus 4,8.

Curvin L Wenger
