A rough, Old Testament warrior and a 21st century housewife—what might they have in common? Reading through the Psalms, we find a man who was determined to find the heart of God and walk in obedience. While there are not many similarities between my life and the life of this man, his words still touch my need and steady my floundering heart.

David set his heart on God even when his life was fraught with difficulty and distress. He was often unable to have the secure life he craved. As I read through his writings, I embark on a personal journey of faith and obedience. Often when confronted with a need in my life, the first words that come to my lips are “I’ll try”. It is so easy to allow emotions of frustration, fear, and worry to rule, instead of making the conscious choice of obedience. Many times, throughout the book of Psalms, David uses the words “I will”. David was determined to steer his heart in the way of obedience. Follow me on my journey thru this beautiful book as we explore a few of David’s “I wills”.

  • I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart. –Psalm 9:1a
  • I will love thee, O Lord, my strength. –Psalm 18:1
  • I will call upon the Lord, who is worthy to be praised. –Psalm 18:3a
  • I will confess my transgressions unto the Lord. –Psalm 32:5b
  • I will keep my mouth with a bridle. –Psalm 39:1b
  • I will wait on thy name. –Psalm 52:9b
  • I will trust in thee. –Psalm 56:3b
  • I will not fear what flesh can do unto me. –Psalm 56:4b
  • I will declare what he hath done for my soul. –Psalm 66:16b
  • I will praise the name of God with a song. –Psalm 69:30a
  • I will go in the strength of the Lord God. –Psalm 71:16a
  • I will remember the works of the Lord. –Psalm 77:11a
  • I will meditate also of all thy work and talk of thy doings. –Psalm 77:12
  • I will be satisfied when I awake with Thy likeness. –Psalm 17:5b

Most of David’s “I wills” were a conscious, emotional choice in the middle of unruly circumstances. Without emotions, this world would be a cold, hard place unable to be inhabited by God’s Spirit. All humankind was created with emotion, but women especially are easily dominated by them. We deal with the ebb and flow of our emotions daily, often like a wild horse which constantly tries to get out of control. But God also gives us His strength to rein in this ‘wild horse’ and guide it in the right direction. Once the choice is made, God’s grace is all ours. Opposite from what we often tell ourselves, we are not victims of our feelings or emotions. We are responsible to take action, for this is, in fact, a war between good and evil. It is a war between our sin nature and the nature of Christ.

I want to look at a few struggles which are common to women and then we will look at how a God-directed “I will” can change our perspective and ultimately affect our emotional responses and spiritual health.

Comparison

For we dare not make ourselves of the number, or compare ourselves with some that commend themselves: but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise –2 Corinthians 10:12.

It is our natural tendency to compare ourselves with others. Yet every time, we end up feeling either superior or inferior to the other person. This evokes many emotions that can either depress us, or unjustly affirm ourselves. Neither of these responses produces a peaceful heart. Instead of following this tendency of comparison, we can say like David, “I will love thee, O Lord, my strength.” Having our eyes on Christ will fulfill our hearts in a way that our desire for human reassurance and acceptance never can or will.

Fear

What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3.

It doesn’t always feel like we have a choice in this one, as fear tends to crash in on us without warning. But in some of my recent battles with fear, God showed me that living in continual fear is refusing to believe the promises found in His Word. David’s “I will trust in Thee” is a conscious choice that I also need to make. As some have said, “Fear is living in the future without God in it.” God’s grace is here for me today and it will be here for me tomorrow, but I cannot try to find grace today for tomorrow’s trials.

Discontentment

Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content –Philippians 4:11.

And having food and raiment let us be therewith content –1 Timothy 6:8.

Everything about the advertising strategies of today’s world are designed to create a desire for more. No matter how beautiful of a house we live in, our human nature will always crave just one more thing. Consider the peace that is available for you as a woman of God, if you choose to imitate David’s attitude, “I will be satisfied when I awake with thy likeness.” As God fulfills the longings of your heart, there’s no longer a need to search for a counterfeit fulfillment.

Gossip

Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man –Colossians 4:6.

Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers –Ephesians 4:29.

The word ‘gossip’ is defined as “casual or unconstrained conversation or reports about other people, typically involving details which are not confirmed to be true.” It is often an effort to elevate our own ego which is rooted in insecurity. David says, “I will keep my mouth with a bridle.” Even though he had every reason to spread ‘stories’ about his enemies, he found no need to devalue others through gossip.

Here we have considered only a few examples. I encourage each of you to prayerfully evaluate your own emotional responses and the way they can dominate your life. Here is a list of questions to help you discern the areas in your life that may need a change of perspective.

  1. Do you need more of an “I will” attitude in your life?
  2. Are you listless and wondering about the meaning of life?
  3. Are you struggling with depression?
  4. Do you struggle with your priorities and lack of motivation to change them?
  5. Do your children need more words of encouragement?
  6. Do you struggle with unhealthy eating habits?
  7. Are you caught in the cogs of negative thought patterns?
  8. Are you fighting your husband’s desires and leadership?

Good intentions and change are often only separated by lack of faith and motivation. Often, we don’t understand how God intimately cares about these emotions and problems in our lives and is waiting to see our willingness to change. When we take the first step of obedience, His grace is there to do the miracle. The “I’ll try” mindset brings lethargy and defeat. The “I will” opens up God’s endless store of grace. Every day brings hundreds of small decisions. How we respond to these decisions eventually form the woman we become and the woman we will be in our old age.

Mary, the future mother of Jesus, was suddenly face to face with an angel one day. His words troubled her and she “cast in her mind” what he was telling her. She could have allowed herself to be overcome with fear at the thought of what the angel’s words meant for her. Instead, she said, “Behold the handmaiden of the Lord, be it unto me according to Thy word.” She chose faith and it impacted the world in ways she could never have imagined.

It was a choice. A choice for which she could not take days or weeks to prepare. However, her being a part of God’s plan for the salvation of the world hung on that choice.

Esther, the queen was faced with a serious dilemma. Her people were in danger of being wiped out by the treacherous Haman. Mordecai told her that she was a queen for such a time as this and she must go in to the king and beg for his help. Her heart quavered. She was well acquainted with the king’s rules that whoever ventured into his palace without an invitation would likely be killed. But she chose courage… “If I perish, I perish.” She was going to do what she could for her people no matter what the cost.

It was just a choice. Yet the safety of her people and the miracle of their deliverance came through her willingness to make such a difficult choice.

Attitudes and emotions—the negative, or the positive—are all hidden choices we must make. Which will you choose, the faithless “I’ll try” or the courageous “I will”? Will you choose, by God’s grace, to make the right choice? God has promised to perfect the things which concern you, but He will not do His work in your life without your “I will”. It is up to you.

And God is able to make all grace abound toward you; that ye, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work: –2 Corinthians 9:8.

একজন রুক্ষ, পুরাতন নিয়মের যোদ্ধা আর একবিংশ শতাব্দীর গৃহিণী—তাদের মধ্যে কী মিল থাকতে পারে? গীতসংহিতা পড়তে গিয়ে আমরা এমন একজন মানুষকে পাই, যিনি ঈশ্বরের হৃদয় খুঁজে পেতে এবং বাধ্যতার পথে চলতে দৃঢ়প্রতিজ্ঞ ছিলেন। আমার জীবন আর এই মানুষটির জীবনের মধ্যে খুব বেশি মিল না থাকলেও, তাঁর কথাগুলো এখনও আমার প্রয়োজনকে স্পর্শ করে এবং টলমল হৃদয়কে স্থির করে।

জীবন দুর্দশা ও সংকটে ভরা থাকলেও দায়ূদ ঈশ্বরের প্রতি তাঁর মন স্থির রেখেছিলেন। যে নিরাপদ জীবন তিনি আকাঙ্ক্ষা করতেন, তা প্রায়ই তাঁর পক্ষে পাওয়া সম্ভব হতো না। তাঁর লেখা পড়তে পড়তে আমি বিশ্বাস ও বাধ্যতার এক ব্যক্তিগত যাত্রায় পা রাখি। আমার জীবনে কোনো প্রয়োজন দেখা দিলে প্রায়ই আমার মুখে প্রথম যে কথাগুলো আসে তা হলো, “আমি চেষ্টা করব।” হতাশা, ভয় ও দুশ্চিন্তার আবেগকে কর্তৃত্ব করতে দেওয়া খুব সহজ—বাধ্য হওয়ার সচেতন সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়ার বদলে। গীতসংহিতা বই জুড়ে দায়ূদ বারবার “আমি করব” কথাগুলো ব্যবহার করেছেন। বাধ্যতার পথে নিজের হৃদয়কে চালিত করতে তিনি দৃঢ়প্রতিজ্ঞ ছিলেন। এই সুন্দর বইটির মধ্য দিয়ে আমার যাত্রায় সঙ্গী হোন; আসুন দায়ূদের কয়েকটি “আমি করব” নিয়ে ভাবি।

  • আমি করব, হে সদাপ্রভু, সমস্ত হৃদয় দিয়ে তোমার প্রশংসা। –গীতসংহিতা ৯:১ক
  • আমি করব তোমাকে প্রেম, হে সদাপ্রভু, আমার শক্তি। –গীতসংহিতা ১৮:১
  • আমি করব সদাপ্রভুকে ডাক, যিনি প্রশংসার যোগ্য। –গীতসংহিতা ১৮:৩ক
  • আমি করব সদাপ্রভুর কাছে আমার অধর্ম স্বীকার। –গীতসংহিতা ৩২:৫খ
  • আমি করব লাগাম দিয়ে আমার মুখ সংযত রাখব। –গীতসংহিতা ৩৯:১খ
  • আমি করব তোমার নামের জন্য অপেক্ষা। –গীতসংহিতা ৫২:৯খ
  • আমি করব তোমাতে বিশ্বাস। –গীতসংহিতা ৫৬:৩খ
  • আমি করব না ভয়, মানুষ আমার কী করতে পারে। –গীতসংহিতা ৫৬:৪খ
  • আমি করব ঘোষণা, তিনি আমার প্রাণের জন্য যা করেছেন। –গীতসংহিতা ৬৬:১৬খ
  • আমি করব গানের দ্বারা ঈশ্বরের নামের প্রশংসা। –গীতসংহিতা ৬৯:৩০ক
  • আমি করব প্রভু ঈশ্বরের শক্তিতে চলা। –গীতসংহিতা ৭১:১৬ক
  • আমি করব সদাপ্রভুর কাজ স্মরণ। –গীতসংহিতা ৭৭:১১ক
  • আমি করব তোমার সমস্ত কাজ নিয়ে ধ্যান করব এবং তোমার কার্যকলাপের কথা বলব। –গীতসংহিতা ৭৭:১২
  • আমি করব তোমার প্রতিমূর্তিতে জেগে উঠলে সন্তুষ্ট হব। –গীতসংহিতা ১৭:৫খ

দায়ূদের অধিকাংশ “আমি করব” ছিল বিশৃঙ্খল পরিস্থিতির মধ্যে সচেতন, আবেগপূর্ণ সিদ্ধান্ত। আবেগ না থাকলে এই জগৎ হতো এক শীতল, কঠিন স্থান, যেখানে ঈশ্বরের আত্মা বাস করতে পারতেন না। সমস্ত মানবজাতিকে আবেগসহ সৃষ্টি করা হয়েছে, কিন্তু বিশেষ করে নারীরা সহজেই আবেগের দ্বারা পরিচালিত হন। প্রতিদিন আমরা আমাদের আবেগের উত্থান-পতনের সঙ্গে মোকাবিলা করি—প্রায়ই এমন এক বুনো ঘোড়ার মতো, যা ক্রমাগত নিয়ন্ত্রণের বাইরে যাওয়ার চেষ্টা করে। কিন্তু ঈশ্বর এই ‘বুনো ঘোড়াকে’ লাগাম পরাতে এবং সঠিক পথে চালাতে তাঁর শক্তিও আমাদের দেন। সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়ার পর ঈশ্বরের অনুগ্রহ আমাদের সম্পূর্ণভাবে মেলে। আমরা নিজেদের প্রায়ই যা বলি তার বিপরীতে, আমরা আমাদের অনুভূতি বা আবেগের শিকার নই। পদক্ষেপ নেওয়ার দায়িত্ব আমাদের, কারণ এটি আসলে ভালো ও মন্দের মধ্যে যুদ্ধ। এটি আমাদের পাপস্বভাব এবং খ্রিস্টের স্বভাবের মধ্যে যুদ্ধ।

নারীদের মধ্যে সাধারণ কয়েকটি সংগ্রাম নিয়ে আমি আলোচনা করতে চাই; তারপর দেখব, ঈশ্বর-নির্দেশিত “আমি করব” কীভাবে আমাদের দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি বদলাতে পারে এবং শেষ পর্যন্ত আমাদের আবেগগত প্রতিক্রিয়া ও আত্মিক সুস্থতাকে প্রভাবিত করতে পারে।

তুলনা

কারণ যারা নিজেদের প্রশংসা করে, তাদের মধ্যে নিজেদের গণ্য করতে বা তাদের সঙ্গে নিজেদের তুলনা করতে আমরা সাহস করি না; কিন্তু তারা নিজেদের দ্বারা নিজেদের মেপে এবং নিজেদের মধ্যে নিজেদের তুলনা করে, তাই তারা জ্ঞানী নয় –২ করিন্থীয় ১০:১২।

অন্যদের সঙ্গে নিজেদের তুলনা করা আমাদের স্বাভাবিক প্রবণতা। কিন্তু প্রত্যেকবারই আমরা হয় অন্য ব্যক্তির চেয়ে নিজেদের শ্রেষ্ঠ, নয়তো নিকৃষ্ট মনে করি। এতে নানা আবেগ জাগে, যা হয় আমাদের বিষণ্ণ করতে পারে, নয়তো অন্যায্যভাবে নিজেদের সম্পর্কে উচ্চ ধারণা দিতে পারে। কোনোটিই শান্ত হৃদয় দেয় না। তুলনা করার এই প্রবণতা অনুসরণ না করে আমরা দায়ূদের মতো বলতে পারি, “আমি তোমাকে প্রেম করব, হে সদাপ্রভু, আমার শক্তি।” খ্রিস্টের দিকে দৃষ্টি রাখলে আমাদের হৃদয় এমনভাবে পরিতৃপ্ত হবে, যা মানুষের আশ্বাস ও গ্রহণযোগ্যতার আকাঙ্ক্ষা কখনোই পারে না, পারবেও না।

ভয়

যখন আমি ভীত হই, তখন তোমাতে বিশ্বাস করব –গীতসংহিতা ৫৬:৩।

এ ক্ষেত্রে আমাদের সবসময় মনে হয় না যে আমাদের কোনো বেছে নেওয়ার সুযোগ আছে, কারণ ভয় কোনো সতর্কতা ছাড়াই আমাদের ওপর আছড়ে পড়ে। কিন্তু ভয়ের সঙ্গে সাম্প্রতিক কয়েকটি লড়াইয়ে ঈশ্বর আমাকে দেখিয়েছেন যে ক্রমাগত ভয়ের মধ্যে বাস করা মানে তাঁর বাক্যে থাকা প্রতিশ্রুতিগুলো বিশ্বাস করতে অস্বীকার করা। দায়ূদের “আমি তোমাতে বিশ্বাস করব”—এটিও এমন এক সচেতন সিদ্ধান্ত, যা আমাকেও নিতে হবে। কেউ কেউ যেমন বলেছেন, “ভয় হলো ঈশ্বরকে বাদ দিয়ে ভবিষ্যতে বাস করা।” আজ ঈশ্বরের অনুগ্রহ আমার জন্য আছে এবং আগামীকালও থাকবে, কিন্তু আগামীকালের পরীক্ষাগুলোর জন্য আজই অনুগ্রহ খুঁজতে পারি না।

অসন্তোষ

অভাবের কথা বলছি না; কেননা যে অবস্থায় থাকি, তাতেই সন্তুষ্ট থাকতে আমি শিখেছি –ফিলিপীয় ৪:১১।

খাদ্য ও বস্ত্র থাকলে তাতেই আমরা সন্তুষ্ট থাকব –১ তীমথিয় ৬:৮।

আজকের জগতের বিজ্ঞাপন কৌশলের প্রতিটি দিকই আরও বেশি পাওয়ার আকাঙ্ক্ষা তৈরি করার জন্য পরিকল্পিত। আমরা যত সুন্দর বাড়িতেই বাস করি না কেন, আমাদের মানবস্বভাব সবসময় আরও একটি জিনিস চাইবে। ঈশ্বরের নারী হিসেবে আপনার জন্য যে শান্তি পাওয়া সম্ভব, তা বিবেচনা করুন—যদি আপনি দায়ূদের মনোভাব অনুকরণ করার সিদ্ধান্ত নেন: “তোমার প্রতিমূর্তিতে জেগে উঠলে আমি সন্তুষ্ট হব।” ঈশ্বর যখন আপনার হৃদয়ের আকাঙ্ক্ষাগুলো পূরণ করেন, তখন আর নকল পরিতৃপ্তির সন্ধান করার প্রয়োজন থাকে না।

পরনিন্দা

তোমাদের বাক্য সর্বদা অনুগ্রহপূর্ণ হোক, লবণে আস্বাদিত হোক, যেন প্রত্যেক ব্যক্তিকে কীভাবে উত্তর দিতে হয় তা জানতে পার –কলসীয় ৪:৬।

তোমাদের মুখ থেকে কোনো দূষিত কথা বের না হোক; বরং যা গঠন করার জন্য উপযুক্ত, তাই বলো, যেন শ্রোতাদের প্রতি অনুগ্রহ প্রকাশ পায় –ইফিষীয় ৪:২৯।

‘পরনিন্দা’ শব্দটির সংজ্ঞা হলো, “অন্য লোকদের নিয়ে অনানুষ্ঠানিক বা বাধাহীন কথাবার্তা কিংবা তাদের সম্বন্ধে বিবরণ, যাতে সাধারণত এমন বিশদ তথ্য থাকে যার সত্যতা নিশ্চিত নয়।” এটি প্রায়ই আমাদের নিজেদের অহংকে বড় করে দেখানোর চেষ্টা, যার মূলে রয়েছে নিরাপত্তাহীনতা। দায়ূদ বলেন, “আমি লাগাম দিয়ে আমার মুখ সংযত রাখব।” শত্রুদের নিয়ে ‘গল্প’ ছড়ানোর যথেষ্ট কারণ থাকা সত্ত্বেও, পরনিন্দার মাধ্যমে অন্যদের হেয় করার কোনো প্রয়োজন তিনি বোধ করেননি।

এখানে আমরা মাত্র কয়েকটি উদাহরণ বিবেচনা করেছি। আপনাদের প্রত্যেককে উৎসাহ দিচ্ছি, প্রার্থনাপূর্বক নিজেদের আবেগগত প্রতিক্রিয়া এবং সেগুলো কীভাবে আপনাদের জীবনকে নিয়ন্ত্রণ করতে পারে তা যাচাই করুন। আপনার জীবনের কোন কোন ক্ষেত্রে দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি বদলানোর প্রয়োজন হতে পারে, তা বুঝতে সাহায্য করার জন্য এখানে কয়েকটি প্রশ্ন রয়েছে।

  1. আপনার জীবনে কি আরও বেশি “আমি করব” মনোভাবের প্রয়োজন?
  2. আপনি কি উদ্যমহীন এবং জীবনের অর্থ নিয়ে ভাবছেন?
  3. আপনি কি বিষণ্ণতার সঙ্গে লড়ছেন?
  4. আপনি কি আপনার অগ্রাধিকারগুলো নিয়ে সংগ্রাম করছেন এবং সেগুলো বদলানোর প্রেরণার অভাব বোধ করছেন?
  5. আপনার সন্তানদের কি আরও উৎসাহমূলক কথা শোনা দরকার?
  6. আপনি কি অস্বাস্থ্যকর খাদ্যাভ্যাস নিয়ে সংগ্রাম করছেন?
  7. আপনি কি নেতিবাচক চিন্তার ধারার গিয়ারে আটকে পড়েছেন?
  8. আপনি কি আপনার স্বামীর ইচ্ছা ও নেতৃত্বের বিরোধিতা করছেন?

সৎ উদ্দেশ্য আর পরিবর্তনের মধ্যে প্রায়ই শুধু বিশ্বাস ও প্রেরণার অভাবই ব্যবধান তৈরি করে। ঈশ্বর আমাদের জীবনের এসব আবেগ ও সমস্যার প্রতি কত গভীরভাবে যত্নশীল, এবং পরিবর্তনের জন্য আমাদের ইচ্ছা দেখতে অপেক্ষা করছেন—তা আমরা প্রায়ই বুঝি না। আমরা যখন বাধ্যতার প্রথম পদক্ষেপ নিই, তখন অলৌকিক কাজ করার জন্য তাঁর অনুগ্রহ উপস্থিত থাকে। “আমি চেষ্টা করব” মনোভাব নিয়ে আসে জড়তা ও পরাজয়। “আমি করব” ঈশ্বরের সীমাহীন অনুগ্রহের ভাণ্ডার খুলে দেয়। প্রতিদিন শত শত ছোট সিদ্ধান্ত আসে। এসব সিদ্ধান্তে আমরা কীভাবে সাড়া দিই, তা শেষ পর্যন্ত আমরা যে নারী হয়ে উঠি এবং বার্ধক্যে যে নারী হব, তাকে গড়ে তোলে।

যিশুর ভবিষ্যৎ মা মরিয়ম একদিন হঠাৎ একজন স্বর্গদূতের মুখোমুখি হলেন। তাঁর কথাগুলো তাঁকে বিচলিত করল, আর তিনি মনে মনে “বিবেচনা করতে লাগলেন” স্বর্গদূত তাঁকে কী বলছেন। স্বর্গদূতের কথার অর্থ তাঁর জীবনের জন্য কী হতে পারে, তা ভেবে তিনি ভয়ে অভিভূত হতে পারতেন। তার বদলে তিনি বললেন, “দেখ, আমি প্রভুর দাসী; তোমার বাক্য অনুসারেই আমার প্রতি ঘটুক।” তিনি বিশ্বাস বেছে নিয়েছিলেন, আর তা এমনভাবে পৃথিবীকে প্রভাবিত করেছিল, যা তিনি কখনো কল্পনাও করতে পারতেন না।

এটি ছিল একটি সিদ্ধান্ত। এমন একটি সিদ্ধান্ত, যার জন্য প্রস্তুতি নিতে তাঁর দিন বা সপ্তাহ সময় ছিল না। তবু জগতের পরিত্রাণের জন্য ঈশ্বরের পরিকল্পনায় তাঁর অংশগ্রহণ সেই সিদ্ধান্তের ওপর নির্ভর করেছিল।

রানি ইষ্টের এক গুরুতর সংকটের মুখোমুখি হয়েছিলেন। বিশ্বাসঘাতক হামনের হাতে তাঁর জাতি নিশ্চিহ্ন হওয়ার বিপদে ছিল। মর্দখয় তাঁকে বলেছিলেন, এমন সময়ের জন্যই তিনি রানি হয়েছেন, এবং তাঁকে রাজার কাছে গিয়ে সাহায্যের জন্য অনুনয় করতে হবে। তাঁর হৃদয় কেঁপে উঠল। আমন্ত্রণ ছাড়া যে কেউ রাজার প্রাসাদে প্রবেশের চেষ্টা করলে তাকে সম্ভবত হত্যা করা হবে—রাজার এই নিয়মগুলো তাঁর ভালোভাবেই জানা ছিল। কিন্তু তিনি সাহস বেছে নিলেন… “যদি বিনষ্ট হই, তবে হই।” পরিণাম যা-ই হোক, তিনি তাঁর জাতির জন্য যা করতে পারেন তা করবেন।

এটি ছিল কেবল একটি সিদ্ধান্ত। তবু তাঁর জাতির নিরাপত্তা এবং তাদের মুক্তির অলৌকিক ঘটনা সম্ভব হয়েছিল, এমন কঠিন সিদ্ধান্ত নিতে তাঁর ইচ্ছার মাধ্যমে।

মনোভাব ও আবেগ—নেতিবাচক হোক বা ইতিবাচক—সবই এমন গোপন সিদ্ধান্ত, যা আমাদের নিতে হয়। আপনি কোনটি বেছে নেবেন—বিশ্বাসহীন “আমি চেষ্টা করব”, নাকি সাহসী “আমি করব”? ঈশ্বরের অনুগ্রহে কি আপনি সঠিক সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়া বেছে নেবেন? ঈশ্বর প্রতিশ্রুতি দিয়েছেন, আপনার সংশ্লিষ্ট বিষয়গুলো তিনি পূর্ণতা দেবেন; কিন্তু আপনার “আমি করব” ছাড়া তিনি আপনার জীবনে তাঁর কাজ করবেন না। সিদ্ধান্ত আপনার।

আর ঈশ্বর তোমাদের প্রতি সমস্ত অনুগ্রহ উপচে পড়তে সক্ষম, যেন তোমরা সর্বদা সব বিষয়ে যথেষ্টতা পেয়ে প্রতিটি সৎকর্মে উপচে পড় –২ করিন্থীয় ৯:৮।

I used to pray for sunshine,
No storms to mark the sky.
For cool breezes and flowers
To please and turn my eye.

I used to pray for happiness,
For smiles, joy, and peace.
That all things would be easy,
And all harsh things would cease.

I used to pray for someone,
To walk with in this life.
To love, laugh with, and cherish,
And dissipate all strife.

I used to pray that always
Life’s pathways would be clear.
That no unwanted circumstance
Would make existence drear.

But those prayers seemed to go unheeded,
For life didn’t flow that way.
The storms—they came uninvited,
Thick rains made many a dark day.

The flowers were not to be seen,
The wind did cut and slash.
No peace could be found about me;
Instead, the thunder did crash.

Not one was found to walk with me,
Alone, through rough ways I did roam.
Gone were the dreams of tranquility,
My soul cried with desire for a home.

Then, a rich voice spoke inside me,
“You’ve been seeking the things you can see.
The true prayers of your heart can be answered,
If you would only but look unto Me.

I have heard your needs and desires,
Your prayers did not fall unheard.
But I saw that your heart needed different
Than the way that ease had preferred.

You prayed for clear skies and sunshine,
For cool breezes and flowers to start.
But I saw that just these would not yield you
The real peace you sought in your heart.

I ordered the rough ways you have followed,
Not to disappoint, but to purge.
For I knew that true happiness begins only
In the heart that with Me does merge.”

So I fell at the feet of my Master
And yielded to His will and His plan.
No longer demanding my wants now,
But trusting He’d finish what He began.

Not long after, I found I was happy;
Not a cloud in my heart could prevail.
Even if my circumstances seemed weary,
No outer storm my inner Sunshine could pale.

The cool breezes of sweet rest in Him,
Did calm all my worries and fears.
And always the flowers of His promises,
Were visible when life brought me tears.

I found also, I no longer walked alone;
The Good Shepherd was there by my side!
With Him I could share my joys and sorrows,
And amidst any battle, in Him I could hide.

So now instead of praying
For things of earthly ease,
I thank the Lord for sending things
That brought me to my knees.

I pray instead for humility,
To lead me through the day.
For an eye to serve, and share the blessings,
That the Lord does send my way.

I pray that my heart would be yielded,
To the touch of the Master’s hand.
Allowing His will to change me,
Through everything He has planned.

For I’ve found that true happiness,
Is not in a smooth, perfect life.
But it’s found when in Christ we are rooted,
Not moved through fire or strife.

If He rules the inmost being,
Then nothing outside will disturb.
For He is the solid Foundation,
And the real source of True Life superb.

Ik bad vroeger om zonneschijn,
Geen stormen die de hemel doorkruisten.
Om koele briesjes en bloemen
Die mijn blik zouden verblijden en boeien.

Ik bad vroeger om geluk,
Om glimlachen, vreugde en vrede.
Dat alles gemakkelijk zou gaan,
En alle narigheid zou ophouden.

Ik bad vroeger om iemand
Om mee door dit leven te gaan.
Om lief te hebben, mee te lachen en te koesteren,
En alle strijd te doen verdwijnen.

Ik bad vroeger dat de wegen
Van het leven altijd helder zouden zijn.
Dat geen ongewenste omstandigheid
Het bestaan somber zou maken.

Maar het leek alsof die gebeden geen gehoor vonden,
Want het leven verliep niet zo.
De stormen — ze kwamen ongevraagd,
Zware regen maakte menige dag donker.

De bloemen waren nergens te zien,
De wind sneed en geselde.
Nergens om mij heen was vrede te vinden;
In plaats daarvan daverde de donder.

Er was niemand om met mij mee te gaan,
Alleen dwaalde ik over ruwe wegen.
De dromen van rust waren verdwenen,
Mijn ziel schreeuwde om een thuis.

Toen sprak een krachtige stem in mij,
‘Je hebt gezocht naar de dingen die je kunt zien.
De ware gebeden van je hart kunnen worden verhoord,
als je maar naar Mij wilt opzien.

Ik heb je behoeften en verlangens gehoord,
Je gebeden zijn niet onbeantwoord gebleven.
Maar Ik zag dat je hart iets anders nodig had
Dan wat gemak verkoos.

Je bad om heldere luchten en zonneschijn,
Om koele briesjes en bloemen die opkwamen.
Maar Ik zag dat juist die dingen je niet zouden geven
De ware vrede die je in je hart zocht.

Ik heb de ruwe wegen bepaald die je bent gegaan,
Niet om je teleur te stellen, maar om je te louteren.
Want Ik wist dat waar geluk alleen begint
In het hart dat zich met Mij verenigt.’

Dus viel ik neer aan de voeten van mijn Meester
En onderwierp mij aan Zijn wil en Zijn plan.
Ik eiste niet langer dat ik kreeg wat ik wilde,
Maar vertrouwde erop dat Hij zou voltooien wat Hij begonnen was.

Niet lang daarna merkte ik dat ik gelukkig was;
Geen wolk in mijn hart kon standhouden.
Zelfs als mijn omstandigheden zwaar leken,
Kon geen storm van buiten mijn innerlijke Zonneschijn doen verbleken.

De koele bries van zoete rust in Hem
Kalmeerde al mijn zorgen en angsten.
En telkens waren de bloemen van Zijn beloften
Zichtbaar wanneer het leven mij tranen bracht.

Ik ontdekte ook dat ik niet langer alleen liep;
De Goede Herder was daar aan mijn zijde!
Met Hem kon ik mijn vreugde en verdriet delen,
En midden in elke strijd kon ik bij Hem schuilen.

Dus bid ik nu in plaats daarvan
Om aardse gemakken,
Maar dank ik de Heer voor de dingen die Hij zond
Die mij op mijn knieën brachten.

In plaats daarvan bid ik om nederigheid,
Om mij door de dag te leiden.
Om oog te hebben voor dienstbaarheid en het delen van de zegeningen
Die de Heer op mijn weg zendt.

Ik bid dat mijn hart zich zal overgeven
Aan de aanraking van de hand van de Meester.
Dat Zijn wil mij mag veranderen,
Door alles heen wat Hij heeft gepland.

Want ik heb ontdekt dat waar geluk
Niet te vinden is in een probleemloos, volmaakt leven.
Maar wanneer we in Christus geworteld zijn,
En niet wijken bij vuur of strijd.

Als Hij heerst over ons diepste wezen,
Dan zal niets van buiten ons verstoren.
Want Hij is het vaste Fundament,
En de ware bron van het heerlijke Ware Leven.

Picture yourself on a hot, humid, sunny day hiking back to a remote village in the mountains of Haiti. You are there to share the gospel with the many hurting and dying souls who need to hear about Jesus. As you are nearing the end of your journey, the terrain is very hilly and rough. You are almost ready to stop for a rest when somehow you trip over a rock. In the process of falling and trying to not get hurt, your precious jug of water opens and spills onto the dry, dusty ground.

I want to liken our lives to that jug of water. What kind of water comes spilling out when somebody knocks us over? How about when we’re having a really busy day and someone pulls out in front of us as we’re driving to our next destination, what’s our reaction? How about our co-workers, can they feel God’s love, peace, and joy flowing from our life in such a way that it draws them to Him? Or what about when we’re in town shopping, are we encouraging others with our smile, and being friendly to the man at the gas station? I’m not saying this to put anyone on a guilt trip but rather encourage our thoughts down those lines.

Paul says, Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. Let’s take a closer look at this verse. It starts out with, Let no man despise thy youth. How should we view our youth—our teenage years? Some view this as a time to live life to the fullest, to have a party, and to do whatever they want. This path leads to much sin, foolishness, immorality, and more. I think we should view the time of our youth as a huge opportunity to do all we can do, and to be all we can be, for Jesus!

Something that the world does not often see is a spirit-filled young person who is passionate about serving God, someone who is not afraid to be different than the world. A young person who is living a pure, holy, upright life is so unusual in today’s world, that this type of youth should really stand out to those around them. So, my question is, are we living up to that? Are we loving God with all of our heart, soul, mind, and strength? Or are we only doing just enough so that we can get by? For example, it is easy for an employer to tell if one of his employees is putting his heart into his work, or not, by how well he does his job, by how he relates to others, and by his attitude. In the same way, I believe the world can tell very quickly if we are serious about serving God and following His principles, or if we are only doing what we are doing because the church ‘requires’ it, while our heart is far from it….

Going on into that verse it says, But be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity. It makes me think of a man in my life who I really appreciate. He has a zeal for God and a burden for the lost that is refreshing and inspiring…. So, what kind of example are you and I leaving for our younger siblings, our friends, our co-workers, and whoever else it might be that our life comes in contact with? We are having an impact on those around us! Is that impact positive or negative?

You may feel like you’re young and not able to do big things for God, but I would encourage you that God has a plan for each one of us. If we have a broken will, a yielded heart, and a willing spirit He will use us—maybe in ways we never thought or dreamed of.

But first, we must learn to be faithful in the small things in life. What about our thought life? You may say, “Nobody will ever know what goes through my mind.” But God knows all the thoughts and intents of our heart which is why He wants us to continually be Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ; –2 Corinthians 10:5.

In this day and age that we live in, Satan is doing his best to discourage, distract, and derail as many people as he possibly can. All he wants you to do is cool off just a little in your love and zeal for God. What is that thing in your life that is shifting your focus off of God? Let’s take some time to ponder that question. Because too often it is something that happens so slowly that we ourselves don’t even realize it.

What is it that Satan is trying to use to get our minds off God? Maybe it’s bad music or maybe it’s being under a wrong influence. Whatever it is, we each have a tendency towards something. Let’s each allow God’s Spirit to honestly search our heart; because, unless we are serious about our walk with God, we will become lukewarm….

So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth –Revelation 3:16. This makes it pretty clear that God wants people who are on fire for Him and who are sold out for Jesus! What must you and I do in order to remain faithful? I believe that at the core of it all there needs to be a deep personal relationship with God…. So how do I get to that point? In response to that question, I would like to ask another, how did we get to know our best friend? Did it happen overnight that suddenly, we just had a best friend, or did our relationship develop over time as we spent lots of time together, sharing struggles, goals, dreams, and many other things?

I believe that spending time with God is the only way we can ever expect to learn to be totally dependent on Him. He wants us to surrender every area of our life to Him so He can use us as a vessel ‘fit for the Master’s use’. We may need to sacrifice other things in our life in order to make this happen. I have found that no matter what, I make time for the things that I really want to do. So then it comes down to what my priorities are….

In conclusion, I would like to bring us back to my title, “What Are You Living For?” I want to encourage all of us to be 100% sold out for Jesus and to be willing to do whatever it takes to keep a vibrant relationship with Him so that we can fulfill Jesus’ teaching in Matthew… Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid –Matthew 5:13-14.

Immaginate di trovarvi in una giornata calda, umida e soleggiata, mentre fate ritorno a piedi a un remoto villaggio tra le montagne di Haiti. Siete lì per condividere il Vangelo con le tante anime sofferenti e morenti che hanno bisogno di sentire parlare di Gesù. Quando il vostro viaggio sta per concludersi, il terreno diventa molto collinoso e accidentato. State quasi per fermarvi a riposare quando, chissà come, inciampate in una roccia. Nel cadere e cercare di non farvi male, la vostra preziosa brocca d’acqua si apre e l’acqua si riversa sul terreno asciutto e polveroso.

Vorrei paragonare la nostra vita a quella brocca d’acqua. Che tipo di acqua fuoriesce quando qualcuno ci fa cadere? E quando abbiamo una giornata davvero intensa e qualcuno ci taglia la strada mentre guidiamo verso la nostra prossima destinazione, come reagiamo? E i nostri colleghi: riescono a sentire l’amore, la pace e la gioia di Dio fluire dalla nostra vita in modo tale da essere attratti a Lui? Oppure, quando siamo in città a fare acquisti, incoraggiamo gli altri con il nostro sorriso e siamo gentili con l’uomo alla stazione di servizio? Non lo dico per far sentire in colpa qualcuno, ma piuttosto per incoraggiarci a riflettere su questi aspetti.

Paolo dice: Nessuno disprezzi la tua giovane età; ma sii esempio dei credenti, nella parola, nella condotta, nell’amore, nello spirito, nella fede, nella purezza –1 Timoteo 4:12. Esaminiamo più da vicino questo versetto. Inizia così: Nessuno disprezzi la tua giovane età. Come dovremmo considerare la nostra giovinezza, gli anni dell’adolescenza? Alcuni la vedono come un periodo in cui vivere la vita al massimo, fare festa e fare tutto ciò che vogliono. Questa strada conduce a molto peccato, stoltezza, immoralità e altro ancora. Penso che dovremmo considerare la nostra giovinezza come una grande opportunità per fare tutto ciò che possiamo e diventare tutto ciò che possiamo essere, per Gesù!

Una cosa che il mondo non vede spesso è un giovane ripieno dello Spirito, appassionato nel servire Dio, qualcuno che non ha paura di essere diverso dal mondo. Un giovane che vive una vita pura, santa e retta è così insolito nel mondo di oggi che dovrebbe davvero distinguersi agli occhi di chi gli sta intorno. Dunque, la domanda è: stiamo vivendo all’altezza di questo? Amiamo Dio con tutto il cuore, con tutta l’anima, con tutta la mente e con tutta la forza? Oppure facciamo solo il minimo indispensabile per cavarcela? Per esempio, un datore di lavoro capisce facilmente se un dipendente mette il cuore nel proprio lavoro o no, da quanto bene svolge il suo compito, da come si relaziona con gli altri e dal suo atteggiamento. Allo stesso modo, credo che il mondo capisca molto rapidamente se siamo seri nel servire Dio e seguire i Suoi principi, oppure se facciamo ciò che facciamo soltanto perché la chiesa lo «richiede», mentre il nostro cuore ne è lontano….

Proseguendo nel versetto, leggiamo: Ma sii esempio dei credenti, nella parola, nella condotta, nell’amore, nello spirito, nella fede, nella purezza. Mi fa pensare a un uomo che fa parte della mia vita e che apprezzo molto. Ha zelo per Dio e un profondo interesse per i perduti, qualità che sono rinfrancanti e fonte d’ispirazione…. Dunque, quale esempio lasciamo tu ed io ai nostri fratelli e sorelle minori, ai nostri amici, ai colleghi e a chiunque altro entri in contatto con la nostra vita? Stiamo influenzando chi ci sta intorno! Questa influenza è positiva o negativa?

Forse ti senti giovane e incapace di fare grandi cose per Dio, ma vorrei incoraggiarti: Dio ha un piano per ciascuno di noi. Se abbiamo una volontà spezzata, un cuore sottomesso e uno spirito disponibile, Egli ci userà, forse in modi che non avremmo mai immaginato o sognato.

Ma prima dobbiamo imparare a essere fedeli nelle piccole cose della vita. E i nostri pensieri? Potresti dire: «Nessuno saprà mai cosa mi passa per la mente». Ma Dio conosce tutti i pensieri e le intenzioni del nostro cuore; per questo vuole che continuiamo a demolire i ragionamenti e ogni altezza che si eleva contro la conoscenza di Dio, e a fare prigioniero ogni pensiero perché obbedisca a Cristo; –2 Corinzi 10:5.

In questi tempi in cui viviamo, Satana fa del suo meglio per scoraggiare, distrarre e far deviare quante più persone gli è possibile. Vuole soltanto che il tuo amore e il tuo zelo per Dio si raffreddino un po’. Che cosa nella tua vita sta distogliendo la tua attenzione da Dio? Prendiamoci un po’ di tempo per riflettere su questa domanda. Perché troppo spesso si tratta di qualcosa che accade così lentamente che nemmeno noi ce ne rendiamo conto.

Che cosa cerca di usare Satana per distogliere i nostri pensieri da Dio? Forse è la musica sbagliata, oppure una cattiva influenza. Qualunque cosa sia, ognuno di noi tende verso qualcosa. Lasciamo che lo Spirito di Dio scruti sinceramente il nostro cuore; perché, se non prendiamo sul serio il nostro cammino con Dio, diventeremo tiepidi….

Così, perché sei tiepido e non sei né freddo né fervente, io ti vomiterò dalla mia bocca –Apocalisse 3:16. Questo chiarisce abbastanza bene che Dio vuole persone ardenti per Lui e totalmente devote a Gesù! Che cosa dobbiamo fare tu ed io per rimanere fedeli? Credo che alla base di tutto debba esserci una profonda relazione personale con Dio…. Come posso arrivare a questo punto? Per rispondere a questa domanda, vorrei farne un’altra: come siamo arrivati a conoscere il nostro migliore amico? È successo da un giorno all’altro, ritrovandoci all’improvviso con un migliore amico, oppure la nostra relazione si è sviluppata nel tempo, trascorrendo molto tempo insieme e condividendo difficoltà, obiettivi, sogni e tante altre cose?

Credo che trascorrere del tempo con Dio sia l’unico modo per poter imparare a dipendere totalmente da Lui. Vuole che Gli sottomettiamo ogni ambito della nostra vita, così che possa usarci come vaso «adatto all’uso del Maestro». Potremmo dover sacrificare altre cose nella nostra vita perché ciò accada. Ho scoperto che, qualunque cosa succeda, trovo il tempo per le cose che desidero davvero fare. Alla fine, dunque, tutto si riduce a quali sono le mie priorità….

In conclusione, vorrei riportarci al titolo: «Per che cosa stai vivendo?». Vorrei incoraggiare tutti noi a essere totalmente consacrati a Gesù e disposti a fare tutto il necessario per mantenere con Lui una relazione viva, affinché possiamo mettere in pratica l’insegnamento di Gesù in Matteo… Voi siete il sale della terra; ma se il sale perde il suo sapore, con che cosa gli si ridarà sapore? Non serve più a nulla se non a essere gettato via e calpestato dagli uomini. Voi siete la luce del mondo. Una città posta sopra un monte non può rimanere nascosta –Matteo 5:13-14.

That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive; But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ: –Ephesians 4:14-15.

Often these verses, namely the latter, are discussed in our day. Sometimes, I wonder if we have not misrepresented the words of our dear brother Paul.

We all know that Jesus never had to retract a statement, he never misspoke or talked out of place. How do we know? Hebrews 4:15 and 9:28 both say that Jesus was without sin, so we can confidently affirm this both in our hearts and in our words.

Now as we look at some of the accounts that Jesus spoke to those around Him, we may say that He didn’t sound very loving! Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves –Matthew 23:14-15.

He called the Pharisees hypocrites many times. He even called one of His most dedicated disciples, Peter, ‘Satan’. This account seems to have been quite significant since it is recorded by three of the gospel writers in Matthew 16:23, Mark 8:33, and Luke 4:8.

What does it mean to ‘speak the truth in love’? Does it mean that we always talk with a pleasing tone? Does it mean that we never say a sharp or harsh word? Paul tells Titus to …speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee –Titus 2:15. In the book of Revelation, Jesus says… As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten… –Revelation 3:19. It’s almost as if Jesus is saying that you cannot rebuke someone unless you first love them.

The Scriptures record the Apostle Paul as admonishing the church at Ephesus to …have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them. For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret. But all things that are reproved are made manifest by the light: for whatsoever doth make manifest is light –Ephesians 5:11-13. Let’s just be honest, it is easier to speak with love and gentleness than it is to rebuke someone that we love. (Or is it rather someone that we want to keep loving us?) Somehow, we will need to forget or ignore the more than 70 times that the Bible talks about rebuke if we want to be a part of the easy, love-only gospel that is all too common today!

When is the last time you spoke the truth in love? Hopefully, most would say today, or a few minutes ago, and that is good. But when is the last time that you rebuked someone for a wayward act? Maybe it has been a while. Maybe the companions you fellowship with believe that it’s judging to speak into someone else’s life. After all, it could be justified, “We all have beams in our own eyes, right?!” God forbid, let us repent and remove the beams from our eyes so that we can help our brother!

What about in our churches? Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin –Hebrews 3:12-13. If we only speak ‘nice’ words to each other, we will tend to start drifting away. The Apostle Paul instructs Timothy… Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear –1 Timothy 5:20. Do we find ourselves obeying these scriptures? Or are we leaning too heavily on others, and thus we justify not doing our part?

Could it be that we have a problem? Could it be that we cannot obey both commands—”Rebuke” and “Speak in love”? Obviously not. We all would agree that these verses do not contradict each other. So how can this be? How can we rebuke sharply (Titus 1:13) while at the same time be speaking the truth in love (Ephesians 4:15)?

I believe that first we must look closer at the verse in Ephesians. What does the word in mean? Does it mean the same thing as the word with? I believe not. We can speak the truth with love and not be speaking it in love. On the other hand, if we speak in love it will always be with love in our heart (God’s love—love for a soul’s eternal welfare), but it may not be the kind of love that is felt by the other person if they are going by feelings. Could it be that this little in word is causing all the confusion?

Let’s look at an example. Imagine that you take your 4-year-old son out to fell some trees for firewood. Everything is going well, because you and your son have a good understanding of how this works. However, when you have almost cut through the first tree you suddenly notice that your son is walking towards the spot where the tree is going to fall. What do you do? Your son’s life is in danger. Should you possibly tell him softly and gently to turn around and come to you? Maybe you should ponder for a bit about how to speak to him in a way that would not offend him? There are obviously many different approaches to how the next crucial moments would go. Certainly, the tone of your voice would reflect the love you have for your child. No father would simply not care in a moment like this. His love for his son would cause him to call out to his son with urgency. For me, because I love my son dearly, I would holler or scream. I would do whatever it takes. I would even run into harm’s way to pull him to safety. I would then probably scold him to be more careful, to walk more circumspectly.

I believe that speaking in love can sound quite sharp at times. In fact, I believe that according to the Bible’s teaching, we can rebuke sharply, with authority, and at the same time do it in love. The problem is within the heart, when we do not have love in our hearts for our brethren, we disqualify ourselves from speaking the truth to them.

Over the years we have lived in Haiti, I have found that a sharp word spoken in love goes a lot farther that a soft word without love. People often know whether you love them or not. When that love is present, it is necessary at times to reprove, rebuke, and exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine. We will end up with a one-sided relationship if we are never allowed to correct someone or speak a word of admonition into their life.

When we see a problem in a brother’s life, our love for him causes us to share our concern with him. That is what true love does. If we are more interested in friendship and smooth sailing, we will neglect this very important practice. Too often we fear speaking into each other’s lives because we think that if we speak honestly to our friend, then they will no longer appreciate us. But remember, if we do not have love one for another, we should just keep quiet. If this is where we find ourselves then we should pray that God would work in our hearts so that we change; after all, God IS love.

Am I saying that we should forget about how we talk? Absolutely not. I hope that is not the message I’m portraying. I know there is a fine line between erring on either side of this issue, but if we allow our hearts to speak with honesty and Holy Spirit discretion, our relationships will be improved and strengthened.

For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears –2 Timothy 4:3. I feel that the church of today has become too soft. We cannot handle rebuke and therefore we no longer practice this vital part of the Christian life. Due to this, our love and our close fellowship is failing. Instead, we go along with only speaking words that are kind and gentle, thereby never motivating each other to grow. Have we become so easily offended that we can no longer hear God speaking through our brothers? Have we become so sensitive that our fellow laborers do not have the liberty to speak into our lives? God open our eyes! God help us!

Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend –Proverbs 27:17. When we sharpen each other, it may not always feel good. Often it will sting or downright hurt. But it is very good for us and very worthwhile.

Let’s say your vehicle is broken down on the side of the road; you’re not sure what the problem is. Along comes a brother, and wanting to show you his love, he looks for something ‘nice’ to say. He comments about the beautiful paint on your car and how clean the windows look. When he leaves, what has he done? Nothing but temporarily lift your spirits. You still have a problem. Another brother comes and it goes quite differently. He looks over the car and says little about the paint and windows. He quickly examines the engine and pronounces that there is a problem that needs to be fixed. He tells you that unless you fix this problem, you’re not going anywhere. Would you be angry with him? Of course not. Would you complain that he didn’t even care about how nice the tires were? That he didn’t say anything about the paint or windows? Not a chance.

But when it comes to the brotherhood, we all want to sit around and talk about the nice things and leave the things that are too ‘sensitive’ in the dark. Have we silently agreed with each other to not correct one another? It almost seems that when a brother wants to rebuke or exhort another brother, he may as well prepare for ‘war’. It should not be this way. If we love each other, which God says we must or we cannot love Him, then we will be open to speak and listen to each other’s concerns.

If we consider anything else in this life—a classroom, the workplace, and even our city streets—without correction there will be failure. We need to listen to those around us who desire to help us. Too many times we would rather be left to ourselves and miss out on a great benefit of true Christian brotherhood. If we want this blessing in our lives, we will need to purposely choose to embrace any constructive criticism that may come our way, no matter from whom it is coming or how unkind it may seem. One thing that goes a long way towards being able to receive ‘hurtful’ rebukes is to always tell ourselves that the other person is wanting to ‘help’ us, not ‘hurt’ us, even though it may feel otherwise.

But speaking the truth in love… Maybe the emphasis in this verse is actually on the word truth. Speaking the truth is not always easy; it takes a love for someone else to pull you out of your comfort zone. When you have a group of brethren that truly love each other, they will speak into each other’s lives—they will speak truth in love.

How we speak to one another certainly means a great deal. The power of the tongue is no small matter. But if we are not unwilling to speak the truth if it means someone will be displeased with us, are we not then at fault? I believe that the fear of man has crept in and controls us more than we would like to admit.

Let’s consider some examples in the Holy Bible. If Jesus had allowed fear of man to influence His life, His ministry would have been much different—He would have remained quiet much of the time. Consider the disciples, each one of them suffered for their Ultimately, they couldn’t but speak of the things they had seen and heard. John the Baptist rebuked Herod! And he lost his head for it. If you read through the martyr’s mirror, in many of the stories the martyrs could have stayed alive if only they would have kept quiet, or spoke nice, agreeable words. But they couldn’t, they had to speak the truth, no matter what the outcome was. They loved not their lives, even unto death. I don’t think it was the tone of voice that these martyrs used which brought the wrath of man down on themselves, but rather it was what they said.

Let’s be honest. We all like it when people are happy with us. We work hard and live upright lives for this cause. But is it biblical? I believe that this verse, speaking the truth in love, is meant to cause us to get off easy street and begin to say the hard things of Scripture that will cause the world to hate us, to say the hard things that cause a brother or sister to consider their ways and repent.

When we speak in love, I believe we have an open door to say the hard things. I’m so thankful for those that loved me enough to say the things that I needed to hear. I pray that God will continue to put those people into my life, the ones who are willing to sacrifice friendship, if need be, to warn me of error in my way.

O that God would raise up men who have eternity in their vision and know the worth of one soul. Those who know how to sacrifice being well liked, so they can be the light of the world. I believe the first step we need to take to fulfill this verse, is to repent for our lack of true biblical love one for another. Then and only then, will we be able to start … speaking the truth in love, [so that we] may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ –Ephesians 4:15.

Sodat ons voortaan nie meer kinders sou wees nie, wat heen en weer geslinger en rondgedryf word deur elke wind van lering, deur die bedrog van mense, deur hulle listige slinkse planne waardeur hulle op die loer lê om te mislei; maar die waarheid in liefde spreek, in alles na Hom toe kan groei, wat die Hoof is, naamlik Christus: –Efesiërs 4:14-15.

Hierdie verse, naamlik die laaste een, word deesdae dikwels bespreek. Soms wonder ek of ons nie die woorde van ons geliefde broer Paulus verkeerd voorgestel het nie.

Ons weet almal dat Jesus nooit ’n stelling hoef terug te trek nie; Hy het nooit verkeerd gepraat of iets buite sy plek gesê nie. Hoe weet ons dit? Hebreërs 4:15 en 9:28 sê albei dat Jesus sonder sonde was, daarom kan ons dit met vertroue in ons harte én met ons woorde bevestig.

Wanneer ons nou kyk na sommige van die verslae oor wat Jesus vir die mense om Hom gesê het, kan ons sê dat Hy nie baie liefdevol geklink het nie! Wee julle, skrifgeleerdes en Fariseërs, geveinsdes, want julle eet die huise van weduwees op, en vir die skyn doen julle lang gebede. Daarom sal julle ’n groter verdoemenis ontvang. Wee julle, skrifgeleerdes en Fariseërs, geveinsdes, want julle deurkruis see en land om een bekeerling te maak, en wanneer hy dit word, maak julle hom ’n kind van die hel, twee maal erger as julle self –Matteus 23:14-15.

Hy het die Fariseërs baie keer geveinsdes genoem. Hy het selfs een van sy mees toegewyde dissipels, Petrus, ‘Satan’ genoem. Hierdie gebeurtenis was blykbaar nogal belangrik, aangesien drie van die Evangelieskrywers dit opgeteken het in Matteus 16:23, Markus 8:33 en Lukas 4:8.

Wat beteken dit om ‘die waarheid in liefde te spreek’? Beteken dit dat ons altyd op ’n aangename toon praat? Beteken dit dat ons nooit ’n skerp of harde woord sê nie? Paulus sê vir Titus om …te spreek en te vermaan en met alle gesag te bestraf. Laat niemand jou verag nie –Titus 2:15. In die boek Openbaring sê Jesus… Almal wat Ek liefhet, bestraf en tugtig Ek… –Openbaring 3:19. Dit is amper asof Jesus sê dat jy iemand nie kan bestraf tensy jy hom eers liefhet nie.

Die Skrif teken aan hoe die apostel Paulus die gemeente in Efese vermaan om …geen deel te hê aan die onvrugbare werke van die duisternis nie, maar dit liewer te bestraf. Want dit is skandelik om selfs te praat oor die dinge wat hulle in die geheim doen. Maar al die dinge wat bestraf word, word deur die lig openbaar gemaak; want alles wat openbaar maak, is lig –Efesiërs 5:11-13. Kom ons wees eerlik: dit is makliker om met liefde en sagmoedigheid te praat as om iemand wat ons liefhet, te bestraf. (Of is dit eerder iemand wat ons wil hê ons moet bly liefhê?) Op die een of ander manier sal ons die meer as 70 keer wat die Bybel oor bestraffing praat, moet vergeet of ignoreer as ons deel wil wees van die gerieflike, liefde-alleen-evangelie wat vandag alte algemeen is!

Wanneer laas het jy die waarheid in liefde gespreek? Hopelik sal die meeste sê vandag, of ’n paar minute gelede, en dit is goed. Maar wanneer laas het jy iemand oor ’n verkeerde daad bestraf? Miskien is dit ’n ruk gelede. Miskien glo die mense met wie jy gemeenskap het dat dit veroordelend is om iets oor iemand anders se lewe te sê. Per slot van rekening, dit kan mos geregverdig word: “Ons het almal balke in ons eie oë, né?!” God verhoede dit; laat ons ons bekeer en die balke uit ons oë verwyder, sodat ons ons broer kan help!

En wat van in ons gemeentes? Neem ag, broeders, dat daar nie miskien in een van julle ’n bose en ongelowige hart is deurdat hy van die lewende God afvallig word nie. Maar vermaan mekaar elke dag, so lank as dit vandag genoem word, sodat niemand van julle deur die verleiding van die sonde verhard word nie –Hebreërs 3:12-13. As ons net ‘mooi’ woorde vir mekaar sê, sal ons geneig wees om te begin afdwaal. Die apostel Paulus gee Timoteus die opdrag… Die wat sondig, bestraf hulle in die teenwoordigheid van almal, sodat ook die ander kan vrees –1 Timoteus 5:20. Vind ons dat ons hierdie Skrifgedeeltes gehoorsaam? Of steun ons te swaar op ander en regverdig ons so dat ons nie ons deel doen nie?

Kan dit wees dat ons ’n probleem het? Kan dit wees dat ons nie albei bevele kan gehoorsaam nie—”Bestraf” en “Praat in liefde”? Natuurlik nie. Ons sal almal saamstem dat hierdie verse mekaar nie weerspreek nie. Hoe kan dit dan wees? Hoe kan ons skerp bestraf (Titus 1:13) en terselfdertyd die waarheid in liefde spreek (Efesiërs 4:15)?

Ek glo dat ons eers die vers in Efesiërs van naderby moet bekyk. Wat beteken die woord in? Beteken dit dieselfde as die woord met? Ek glo nie. Ons kan die waarheid met liefde praat en dit tog nie in liefde spreek nie. Aan die ander kant, as ons in liefde praat, sal daar altyd liefde in ons hart wees (God se liefde—liefde vir ’n siel se ewige heil), maar dit is dalk nie die soort liefde wat die ander persoon voel as hy deur gevoelens gelei word nie. Kan dit wees dat hierdie klein woordjie in al die verwarring veroorsaak?

Kom ons kyk na ’n voorbeeld. Stel jou voor jy neem jou 4-jarige seun saam om ’n paar bome vir vuurmaakhout af te saag. Alles gaan goed, want jy en jou seun verstaan goed hoe dit werk. Maar wanneer jy die eerste boom amper deursaag het, sien jy skielik dat jou seun na die plek toe loop waar die boom gaan val. Wat doen jy? Jou seun se lewe is in gevaar. Moet jy hom dalk saggies en vriendelik vra om om te draai en na jou toe te kom? Miskien moet jy ’n bietjie nadink oor hoe om met hom te praat op ’n manier wat hom nie sal aanstoot gee nie? Daar is natuurlik baie verskillende maniere waarop die volgende beslissende oomblikke kan verloop. Jou stemtoon sal beslis die liefde weerspieël wat jy vir jou kind het. Geen vader sou in so ’n oomblik eenvoudig onverskillig wees nie. Sy liefde vir sy seun sou hom daartoe dryf om dringend na hom te roep. Omdat ek my seun innig liefhet, sou ek op hom skree of hard roep. Ek sou alles doen wat nodig is. Ek sou selfs in gevaar inhardloop om hom na veiligheid te trek. Daarna sou ek hom waarskynlik berispe dat hy versigtiger moet wees en versigtiger moet loop.

Ek glo dat dit soms nogal skerp kan klink om in liefde te praat. Trouens, ek glo dat ons volgens die Bybel se lering skerp en met gesag kan bestraf, en dit terselfdertyd in liefde kan doen. Die probleem lê in die hart: wanneer ons nie liefde in ons harte vir ons broeders het nie, diskwalifiseer ons onsself om die waarheid met hulle te praat.

Oor die jare wat ons in Haïti gewoon het, het ek gevind dat ’n skerp woord wat in liefde gespreek word, baie verder kom as ’n sagte woord sonder liefde. Mense weet dikwels of jy hulle liefhet of nie. Wanneer daardie liefde daar is, is dit soms nodig om met alle lankmoedigheid en lering te bestraf, te berispe en te vermaan. Ons sal ’n eensydige verhouding hê as ons nooit toegelaat word om iemand reg te help of ’n vermanende woord in sy lewe te spreek nie.

Wanneer ons ’n probleem in ’n broer se lewe sien, beweeg ons liefde vir hom ons om ons besorgdheid met hom te deel. Dít is wat ware liefde doen. As ons meer belangstel in vriendskap en om alles seepglad te laat verloop, sal ons hierdie baie belangrike gebruik nalaat. Te dikwels is ons bang om iets oor mekaar se lewens te sê, omdat ons dink dat ons vriend ons nie meer sal waardeer as ons eerlik met hom praat nie. Maar onthou, as ons mekaar nie liefhet nie, moet ons maar stilbly. As dit is waar ons ons bevind, moet ons bid dat God in ons harte sal werk sodat ons verander; God IS immers liefde.

Sê ek dat ons nie hoef om te gee oor hoe ons praat nie? Glad nie. Ek hoop dit is nie die boodskap wat ek uitdra nie. Ek weet daar is ’n fyn lyn tussen foute aan weerskante van hierdie saak, maar as ons toelaat dat ons harte met eerlikheid en die Heilige Gees se onderskeidingsvermoë spreek, sal ons verhoudings verbeter en versterk word.

Want daar sal ’n tyd wees wanneer hulle die gesonde leer nie sal verdra nie, maar omdat hulle in hulle gehoor gestreel wil wees, vir hulle volgens hulle eie begeerlikhede ’n menigte leraars sal versamel –2 Timoteus 4:3. Ek voel dat die kerk van vandag te toegeeflik geword het. Ons kan nie bestraffing hanteer nie en daarom beoefen ons nie meer hierdie noodsaaklike deel van die Christelike lewe nie. Gevolglik verswak ons liefde en ons innige gemeenskap. In plaas daarvan praat ons net woorde wat vriendelik en sag is, en spoor ons mekaar dus nooit aan om te groei nie. Het ons so maklik aanstoot geneem dat ons God nie meer deur ons broeders kan hoor praat nie? Het ons so sensitief geword dat ons medearbeiders nie die vrymoedigheid het om iets oor ons lewens te sê nie? God, open ons oë! God, help ons!

Yster slyp yster; so slyp die een mens die ander –Spreuke 27:17. Wanneer ons mekaar slyp, voel dit dalk nie altyd lekker nie. Dikwels sal dit steek of sommer seermaak. Maar dit is baie goed vir ons en beslis die moeite werd.

Sê nou jou voertuig het langs die pad gebreek; jy is onseker wat die probleem is. ’n Broer kom daar aan en wil jou sy liefde betoon deur iets ‘moois’ te sê. Hy lewer kommentaar oor die pragtige verfwerk aan jou motor en hoe skoon die vensters lyk. Wanneer hy vertrek, wat het hy gedoen? Niks behalwe om jou gemoed tydelik op te beur nie. Jy het steeds ’n probleem. ’n Ander broer kom, en dit verloop heel anders. Hy kyk na die motor en sê min oor die verfwerk en vensters. Hy ondersoek gou die enjin en sê dat daar ’n probleem is wat reggemaak moet word. Hy sê vir jou dat jy nêrens heen gaan voordat jy hierdie probleem reggemaak het nie. Sal jy kwaad wees vir hom? Natuurlik nie. Sal jy kla dat hy nie eers omgegee het hoe mooi die bande is nie? Dat hy niks oor die verfwerk of vensters gesê het nie? Glad nie.

Maar wanneer dit by die broederskap kom, wil ons almal net sit en oor die mooi dinge praat en die dinge wat te ‘sensitief’ is in die donker laat. Het ons in stilte met mekaar ooreengekom om mekaar nie reg te help nie? Dit lyk amper asof ’n broer maar vir ‘oorlog’ kan voorberei wanneer hy ’n ander broer wil bestraf of vermaan. Dit behoort nie so te wees nie. As ons mekaar liefhet—en God sê ons moet, anders kan ons Hom nie liefhê nie—sal ons bereid wees om mekaar se bekommernisse uit te spreek en aan te hoor.

As ons enigiets anders in hierdie lewe in ag neem—’n klaskamer, die werkplek en selfs ons stadsstrate—sal daar sonder teregwysing mislukking wees. Ons moet luister na die mense om ons wat ons wil help. Te dikwels verkies ons om aan onsself oorgelaat te word en mis ons ’n groot voordeel van ware Christelike broederskap. As ons hierdie seën in ons lewens wil hê, sal ons doelbewus moet kies om enige opbouende kritiek wat oor ons pad kom, te aanvaar, ongeag van wie dit kom of hoe onvriendelik dit mag klink. Een ding wat baie help om ‘seermaak’-bestraffings te kan ontvang, is om altyd vir onsself te sê dat die ander persoon ons wil ‘help’, nie ‘seermaak’ nie, al voel dit dalk anders.

Maar die waarheid in liefde spreek… Miskien val die klem in hierdie vers eintlik op die woord waarheid. Dit is nie altyd maklik om die waarheid te praat nie; dit verg liefde vir iemand anders om jou uit jou gemaksone te laat tree. Wanneer jy ’n groep broeders het wat mekaar waarlik liefhet, sal hulle iets oor mekaar se lewens sê—hulle sal die waarheid in liefde praat.

Hoe ons met mekaar praat, maak beslis baie saak. Die mag van die tong is geen geringe saak nie. Maar as ons bereid is om die waarheid te praat, selfs al beteken dit dat iemand ontevrede met ons sal wees, is ons dan nie skuldig nie? Ek glo dat die vrees vir mense ingesluip het en ons meer beheers as wat ons graag wil erken.

Kom ons dink aan ’n paar voorbeelde in die Heilige Bybel. As Jesus toegelaat het dat mensevrees sy lewe beïnvloed, sou sy bediening baie anders gewees het—Hy sou dikwels stilgebly het. Dink aan die dissipels: elkeen van hulle het vir hulle gely. Uiteindelik kon hulle nie anders as om te praat oor die dinge wat hulle gesien en gehoor het nie. Johannes die Doper het Herodes bestraf! En daarvoor het hy sy kop verloor. As jy die Martelaarsboek deurlees, kon die martelare in baie van die verhale aan die lewe gebly het as hulle maar stilgebly het of mooi, instemmende woorde gesê het. Maar hulle kon nie; hulle moes die waarheid praat, ongeag die gevolge. Hulle het hulle lewe nie liefgehad nie, selfs tot die dood toe. Ek dink nie dit was die stemtoon wat hierdie martelare gebruik het wat die mense se toorn oor hulle gebring het nie, maar eerder wat hulle gesê het.

Kom ons wees eerlik. Ons hou almal daarvan wanneer mense tevrede met ons is. Ons werk hard en leef opreg om hierdie rede. Maar is dit Bybels? Ek glo dat hierdie vers, die waarheid in liefde sprekende, bedoel is om ons van die maklike pad af te kry en ons te laat begin om die moeilike dinge van die Skrif te sê—dinge wat sal veroorsaak dat die wêreld ons haat, en dinge wat ’n broer of suster sal laat nadink oor hulle weë en hulle bekeer.

Wanneer ons in liefde praat, glo ek dat die deur oopstaan om die moeilike dinge te sê. Ek is so dankbaar vir dié wat my genoeg liefgehad het om die dinge te sê wat ek moes hoor. Ek bid dat God daardie mense steeds in my lewe sal plaas: mense wat, indien nodig, bereid is om vriendskap op te offer om my teen ’n verkeerde weg te waarsku.

Ag, mag God manne oprig wat die ewigheid voor oë het en weet wat een siel werd is. Manne wat weet hoe om gewildheid op te offer, sodat hulle die lig van die wêreld kan wees. Ek glo dat die eerste stap wat ons moet neem om hierdie vers te vervul, is om ons te bekeer oor ons gebrek aan ware Bybelse liefde vir mekaar. Eers dan, en slegs dan, sal ons kan begin … die waarheid in liefde spreek, [sodat ons] in alles na Hom toe kan groei, wat die Hoof is, naamlik Christus –Efesiërs 4:15.

Death seemed certain, the doctors all said.
Was it really true “That in days he’d be dead”?
He didn’t want to admit, yet he was driven by fear.
He broadened his shoulders, hid every tear.
Before he knew when his end might be,
He boldly proclaimed his own sovereignty.
To admit his fear of what is unknown,
Would be worse than death and eternity alone.

“No one can know my anguish inside!
I’ll act like I’m fine, my feelings I’ll hide.
People speak of God, oh the anger that brings!
Please go away, or talk of other things!”
Alone on the bed, his mind starts to race.
“I’m tired of bondage; could there be grace?
No, it will never work, for me it’s too late.”
With his back turned on God, he awaited his fate.

The preacher knew not what exactly to say,
At the funeral of the man who had gone his own way.
All that he knew, was that he’d made a bad choice,
Hardening his heart and blocking God’s voice.
There’s no changing it now, he must pay the cost.
Death swallowed its victim—his soul eternally lost.

Kifo kilionekana hakiepukiki, ndivyo madaktari wote walivyosema.
Je, kweli ilikuwa kweli “kwamba angekuwa amekufa baada ya siku chache”?
Hakutaka kukubali, lakini alisukumwa na hofu.
Alijikaza, akaficha kila chozi.
Kabla hajajua mwisho wake ungefika lini,
Alitangaza kwa ujasiri enzi yake mwenyewe.
Kukubali hofu yake ya yasiyojulikana,
Kungekuwa vibaya kuliko kifo na umilele wa upweke.

“Hakuna ajuaye uchungu nilio nao ndani!
Nitafanya kana kwamba niko sawa, nitaficha hisia zangu.
Watu wanazungumza kuhusu Mungu—lo, hilo hunikasirisha kiasi gani!
Tafadhali ondokeni, au zungumzieni mambo mengine!”
Akiwa peke yake kitandani, mawazo yake yakaanza kwenda mbio.
“Nimechoshwa na utumwa; je, kunaweza kuwa na neema?
Hapana, haitafanikiwa kamwe; kwangu mimi, muda umekwisha.”
Akiwa amempa Mungu kisogo, alingojea hatima yake.

Mhubiri hakujua hasa la kusema,
Katika mazishi ya mtu aliyekuwa amejichagulia njia yake mwenyewe.
Alichokijua tu ni kwamba alikuwa amefanya uchaguzi mbaya,
Akaufanya moyo wake kuwa mgumu na kuzuia sauti ya Mungu.
Sasa hakuna la kubadilisha; lazima alipe gharama yake.
Kifo kikammeza mwathiriwa wake—nafsi yake ikapotea milele.

Picture yourself on a hot, humid, sunny day hiking back to a remote village in the mountains of Haiti. You are there to share the gospel with the many hurting and dying souls who need to hear about Jesus. As you are nearing the end of your journey, the terrain is very hilly and rough. You are almost ready to stop for a rest when somehow you trip over a rock. In the process of falling and trying to not get hurt, your precious jug of water opens and spills onto the dry, dusty ground.

I want to liken our lives to that jug of water. What kind of water comes spilling out when somebody knocks us over? How about when we’re having a really busy day and someone pulls out in front of us as we’re driving to our next destination, what’s our reaction? How about our co-workers, can they feel God’s love, peace, and joy flowing from our life in such a way that it draws them to Him? Or what about when we’re in town shopping, are we encouraging others with our smile, and being friendly to the man at the gas station? I’m not saying this to put anyone on a guilt trip but rather encourage our thoughts down those lines.

Paul says, Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. Let’s take a closer look at this verse. It starts out with, Let no man despise thy youth. How should we view our youth—our teenage years? Some view this as a time to live life to the fullest, to have a party, and to do whatever they want. This path leads to much sin, foolishness, immorality, and more. I think we should view the time of our youth as a huge opportunity to do all we can do, and to be all we can be, for Jesus!

Something that the world does not often see is a spirit-filled young person who is passionate about serving God, someone who is not afraid to be different than the world. A young person who is living a pure, holy, upright life is so unusual in today’s world, that this type of youth should really stand out to those around them. So, my question is, are we living up to that? Are we loving God with all of our heart, soul, mind, and strength? Or are we only doing just enough so that we can get by? For example, it is easy for an employer to tell if one of his employees is putting his heart into his work, or not, by how well he does his job, by how he relates to others, and by his attitude. In the same way, I believe the world can tell very quickly if we are serious about serving God and following His principles, or if we are only doing what we are doing because the church ‘requires’ it, while our heart is far from it….

Going on into that verse it says, But be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity. It makes me think of a man in my life who I really appreciate. He has a zeal for God and a burden for the lost that is refreshing and inspiring…. So, what kind of example are you and I leaving for our younger siblings, our friends, our co-workers, and whoever else it might be that our life comes in contact with? We are having an impact on those around us! Is that impact positive or negative?

You may feel like you’re young and not able to do big things for God, but I would encourage you that God has a plan for each one of us. If we have a broken will, a yielded heart, and a willing spirit He will use us—maybe in ways we never thought or dreamed of.

But first, we must learn to be faithful in the small things in life. What about our thought life? You may say, “Nobody will ever know what goes through my mind.” But God knows all the thoughts and intents of our heart which is why He wants us to continually be Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ; –2 Corinthians 10:5.

In this day and age that we live in, Satan is doing his best to discourage, distract, and derail as many people as he possibly can. All he wants you to do is cool off just a little in your love and zeal for God. What is that thing in your life that is shifting your focus off of God? Let’s take some time to ponder that question. Because too often it is something that happens so slowly that we ourselves don’t even realize it.

What is it that Satan is trying to use to get our minds off God? Maybe it’s bad music or maybe it’s being under a wrong influence. Whatever it is, we each have a tendency towards something. Let’s each allow God’s Spirit to honestly search our heart; because, unless we are serious about our walk with God, we will become lukewarm….

So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth –Revelation 3:16. This makes it pretty clear that God wants people who are on fire for Him and who are sold out for Jesus! What must you and I do in order to remain faithful? I believe that at the core of it all there needs to be a deep personal relationship with God…. So how do I get to that point? In response to that question, I would like to ask another, how did we get to know our best friend? Did it happen overnight that suddenly, we just had a best friend, or did our relationship develop over time as we spent lots of time together, sharing struggles, goals, dreams, and many other things?

I believe that spending time with God is the only way we can ever expect to learn to be totally dependent on Him. He wants us to surrender every area of our life to Him so He can use us as a vessel ‘fit for the Master’s use’. We may need to sacrifice other things in our life in order to make this happen. I have found that no matter what, I make time for the things that I really want to do. So then it comes down to what my priorities are….

In conclusion, I would like to bring us back to my title, “What Are You Living For?” I want to encourage all of us to be 100% sold out for Jesus and to be willing to do whatever it takes to keep a vibrant relationship with Him so that we can fulfill Jesus’ teaching in Matthew… Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid –Matthew 5:13-14.

Stel jou voor jy stap op ’n warm, vogtige, sonnige dag terug na ’n afgeleë dorpie in die berge van Haïti. Jy is daar om die evangelie te deel met die talle gekweste en sterwende siele wat van Jesus moet hoor. Wanneer jy die einde van jou reis nader, is die terrein baie heuwelagtig en ruig. Jy is amper gereed om stil te staan en te rus wanneer jy op die een of ander manier oor ’n klip struikel. Terwyl jy val en probeer keer dat jy seerkry, gaan jou kosbare waterkruik oop en mors die water op die droë, stowwerige grond uit.

Ek wil ons lewens met daardie waterkruik vergelyk. Watter soort water stroom uit wanneer iemand ons omstamp? Wat van wanneer ons ’n baie besige dag het en iemand voor ons inry terwyl ons na ons volgende bestemming ry—hoe reageer ons? En ons medewerkers: kan hulle God se liefde, vrede en vreugde op so ’n manier uit ons lewens sien vloei dat dit hulle na Hom toe trek? Of wat van wanneer ons in die dorp inkopies doen—bemoedig ons ander met ons glimlag, en is ons vriendelik teenoor die man by die vulstasie? Ek sê dit nie om iemand skuldig te laat voel nie, maar eerder om ons gedagtes in daardie rigting te stuur.

Paulus sê: Laat niemand jou jonkheid verag nie, maar wees ’n voorbeeld vir die gelowiges in woord, in lewenswandel, in liefde, in gees, in geloof, in reinheid –1 Timoteus 4:12. Kom ons kyk nader na hierdie vers. Dit begin met: Laat niemand jou jonkheid verag nie. Hoe behoort ons ons jeug—ons tienerjare—te beskou? Sommige beskou dit as ’n tyd om die lewe ten volle te geniet, partytjie te hou en te doen wat hulle wil. Hierdie pad lei tot baie sonde, dwaasheid, onsedelikheid en meer. Ek dink ons behoort die tyd van ons jeug te beskou as ’n wonderlike geleentheid om alles te doen wat ons kan en alles te wees wat ons kan, vir Jesus!

Iets wat die wêreld nie dikwels sien nie, is ’n jongmens wat met die Gees vervul is en passievol is daaroor om God te dien—iemand wat nie bang is om anders as die wêreld te wees nie. ’n Jongmens wat ’n rein, heilige en opregte lewe lei, is so ongewoon in vandag se wêreld dat so ’n jongmens werklik behoort uit te staan vir die mense om hom of haar. Dus is my vraag: leef ons inderdaad so? Het ons God lief met ons hele hart, siel, verstand en krag? Of doen ons net genoeg om kop bo water te hou? Dit is byvoorbeeld maklik vir ’n werkgewer om te sien of een van sy werknemers sy hart in sy werk sit, aan die hand van hoe goed hy sy werk doen, hoe hy met ander omgaan en wat sy gesindheid is. Net so glo ek dat die wêreld baie gou kan sien of ons ernstig is daaroor om God te dien en sy beginsels te volg, en of ons net doen wat ons doen omdat die kerk dit ‘vereis’, terwyl ons hart ver daarvan is….

Verder in daardie vers staan daar: Maar wees ’n voorbeeld vir die gelowiges in woord, in lewenswandel, in liefde, in gees, in geloof, in reinheid. Dit laat my dink aan ’n man in my lewe vir wie ek baie waardering het. Hy het ’n ywer vir God en ’n diepe besorgdheid oor die verlorenes wat verkwikkend en inspirerend is…. Watter voorbeeld laat ek en jy dus vir ons jonger broers en susters, ons vriende, ons medewerkers en enigiemand anders met wie ons lewens in aanraking kom? Ons het ’n invloed op die mense om ons! Is daardie invloed positief of negatief?

Jy voel dalk dat jy jonk is en nie groot dinge vir God kan doen nie, maar ek wil jou bemoedig: God het ’n plan vir elkeen van ons. As ons ’n gebroke wil, ’n oorgegewe hart en ’n gewillige gees het, sal Hy ons gebruik—dalk op maniere wat ons nooit verwag of waarvan ons nooit gedroom het nie.

Maar eers moet ons leer om getrou te wees in die klein dingetjies van die lewe. Wat van ons gedagtes? Jy sê dalk: “Niemand sal ooit weet wat deur my gedagtes gaan nie.” Maar God ken al die gedagtes en bedoelings van ons hart, en daarom wil Hy hê dat ons voortdurend die redenasies en elke hooghartige ding wat hom teen die kennis van God verhef, moet afbreek, en elke gedagte gevange moet neem om dit aan Christus gehoorsaam te maak; –2 Korintiërs 10:5.

In die tyd waarin ons leef, doen Satan sy bes om soveel mense as moontlik te ontmoedig, af te lei en van die regte pad af te bring. Al wat hy wil hê, is dat jou liefde vir God en jou ywer vir Hom net ’n bietjie moet afkoel. Wat is dit in jou lewe wat jou aandag van God af wegskuif? Kom ons neem ’n bietjie tyd om oor daardie vraag na te dink. Want alte dikwels gebeur dit so stadig dat ons dit self nie eens agterkom nie.

Wat probeer Satan gebruik om ons gedagtes van God af weg te kry? Dalk is dit slegte musiek, of dalk is dit ’n verkeerde invloed. Wat dit ook al is, ons het elkeen ’n neiging tot iets. Kom ons laat elkeen God se Gees toe om ons hart eerlik te deursoek; want tensy ons ernstig is oor ons wandel met God, sal ons lou word….

Omdat jy dan lou is en nie koud of warm nie, sal Ek jou uit my mond spoeg –Openbaring 3:16. Dit maak baie duidelik dat God mense wil hê wat vir Hom aan die brand is en hulle heeltemal aan Jesus oorgegee het! Wat moet ek en jy doen om getrou te bly? Ek glo dat daar heel diep in die kern ’n persoonlike verhouding met God moet wees…. Hoe kom ek dan by daardie punt? As antwoord op daardie vraag wil ek ’n ander vraag vra: hoe het ons ons beste vriend leer ken? Het dit oornag gebeur—dat ons skielik net ’n beste vriend gehad het—of het ons verhouding mettertyd gegroei namate ons baie tyd saam deurgebring en probleme, doelwitte, drome en baie ander dinge gedeel het?

Ek glo dat tyd saam met God deurbring die enigste manier is waarop ons kan verwag om te leer om volkome op Hom staat te maak. Hy wil hê dat ons elke terrein van ons lewe aan Hom moet oorgee sodat Hy ons kan gebruik as ’n voorwerp wat ‘geskik is vir die Meester se gebruik’. Ons sal dalk ander dinge in ons lewe moet opoffer om dit moontlik te maak. Ek het gevind dat ek, wat ook al gebeur, tyd maak vir die dinge wat ek regtig wil doen. Uiteindelik kom dit dus neer op wat my prioriteite is….

Ten slotte wil ek ons terugbring by my titel: “Waarvoor leef jy?” Ek wil ons almal aanmoedig om ons 100% heeltemal aan Jesus toe te wy en bereid te wees om alles te doen wat nodig is om ’n lewende verhouding met Hom te behou, sodat ons Jesus se lering in Matteus kan uitleef… Julle is die sout van die aarde; maar as die sout laf geword het, waarmee sal dit weer sout gemaak word? Dit deug nêrens meer voor nie as om buite gegooi en deur die mense vertrap te word. Julle is die lig van die wêreld. ’n Stad wat bo-op ’n berg lê, kan nie weggesteek word nie –Matteus 5:13-14.
