Sitting squarely on the great divide of our measured timeline of years lies the incarnate birth of our Lord Jesus Christ. He rightfully owns this place, for no other advent could so astutely impact humanity. The years before His birth are known as B.C. or “Before Christ”, while the years following are known as A.D. (Anno Domini, Latin for “The year of our Lord”). While His birth has been utterly cluttered and confused by pagan influences and personal indulgence, the simple radiant beauty of the occasion is still available for all who will but candidly gaze upon the unbeguiled scene.

While the calendar has placed the birth of Christ on December 25, most scholars have concluded that this date is inaccurate. It has also been determined that the actual year ascribed to His birth is also inaccurate by 4-6 years. The date was set by the bishop of Rome in accordance with a popular pagan festival called Saturnalia. The heathen Romans worshiped Saturn as the god of agriculture by feasting, parties, adorning their houses with evergreens, the exchanging of gifts, and general merry making. It was the bishop’s endeavor to provide a sanctifying influence upon the revelry and turn the minds of the general populace away from selfish indulgence to God incarnate. As we may well expect, the heathen festivities never missed a beat and continued on at the same pace. The church that initially frowned upon the proposition eventually accepted the idea and by the fourth century was fully acclimated and indoctrinated to the hybrid mixture of that which was Christian and pagan.

Thus, we are left with a dilemma today. How should a Christian regard the birth of Christ? Should we attempt to keep Christ in Christmas or get Him out? Regardless of our opinion, each of us must veritably resolve to understand the significance of the virgin birth apart from the emotional ties to the hybrid celebration and recognize the birth in a God-ordained fashion. In contrast to the millions who celebrate His birth in our day, there were but a paltry handful who were able and worthy to attend the actual event.

And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night. And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid. And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord. And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger. And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying, Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men –Luke 2:8-14.

It was a band of lowly shepherds who received the first birth announcement. Even these foolish and unlearned men knew of, and longed for, the anticipated Messiah. But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting –Micah 5:2.

As the star-spangled heavens erupted to life, the shepherds gazed in mesmerized awe at the scene before them and a new day began to dawn upon the horizon of their souls. The angelic host proclaimed their message to the shepherds, then soon vanished; yet the good news remained. The encounter was but a brief vapor, yet a three-fold fragrance lingered in the burning hearts of these men: A Savior… A Sign… and A Song…

…A Savior

The very fact that a Savior is promised, implies that there is something that we need to be saved from. Whatever our physical lot may be, man’s spiritual condition has been on the precipice of despair since the fall in Eden. Through four millennia, the human race had cowered under the diabolical cloud of sin and many had fallen prey to its menacing darkness. Sin can take a candle of hope and snuff it out in an instant. It can breathe its icy breath upon the fairest of flowers and wilt them in an instant. It takes loving marriages and introduces them to the throes of internal war. It takes the sincere bloom of youth and robs it of the fragrance of its innocence. Those who have managed to break free from the bondage of its personal subjugation can easily see their narrow escape from the mad society about them. Thus, the humble shepherds rejoiced at the advent of a Savior.

All have sinned and come under its condemnation. The very thought of freedom from the impending jurisdiction of our just punishment is a breath of fresh air. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved –John 3:17. Those who have been genuinely converted carry in their soul the hope of eternal life and the promise of heaven. They become new creatures as the Holy Spirit takes up residence in their hearts. While this bears a dramatic effect on the life of a believer, these are not the only issues of salvation. This Savior is also a Lord.

Just as the title of “Savior” implies a desperate need, so likewise, the name of “Christ, the Lord” implies a dominating victory. He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil –1 John 3:8. Not only shall we be freed from the condemnation of sin, we must also be rescued from its power and influence as well. The debilitating habits that we have accumulated in our sinful nature must be dealt a death blow. The passions and lusts that overpowered us before His influence came upon our lives must be subject to Him. The egotistical pride and driving temper within man that has destroyed relationships and wounded the lives of those that we love about us, must also be swallowed up in this victory. If Christ is not our Lord, then neither is He our Savior.

What child is this. Who laid to rest,
On Mary’s lap is sleeping?
Whom angels greet with anthems sweet,
While shepherds watch are keeping?
This, this is Christ the King,
Whom shepherds guard and angels sing.
Haste, haste to bring Him laud,
The Babe the Son of Mary.

…A Sign

One may well think that the angelic visitation was a much larger sign than the infant in the manger. Who among us has ever experienced the delight of hearing such a heavenly chorus? As we read the account, one can only imagine the enrapturing beauty of a myriad of celestial voices resounding together and filling the mountainside with a glimmer of heaven that earth has never known since the day of creation, When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy –Job 38:7. Yet the angels were not the sign.

The fact that this child was conceived by the Holy Ghost as detailed in Matthew 1:20, must be received by faith and can hardly be reckoned as a terrestrial sign. The fact that the child was wrapped in swaddling clothes was nothing unusual, for all mothers of the day did that. In one of the most graphic chapters depicting the birth of a child, God mentions that no one cared for Israel at their birth: And as for thy nativity, in the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed in water to supple thee; thou wast not salted at all, nor swaddled at all –Ezekiel 16:4. These clues will be useless in a search for the child. The tell-tale sign of this event is marked by the cradle of the infant. No mother would choose a cattle lot for a birthing suite and lay her newborn in a feed trough unless necessity demanded it.

The sign of the manger in conjunction with their scriptural knowledge of Bethlehem were all that was needed for the shepherds to find the child. Scripture makes no mention of the comforts of a stable at all. The shepherds were intimately familiar with the areas of town allotted for the animals and their journey began.

Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach –Hebrews 13:12-13. This sign calls for personal participation. Everyone whose heart beats loyal to the scene must also go to accompany Him. This will not be fulfilled by attending a living nativity scene, a “Messiah” performance, or by going to Grandmother’s house for Christmas dinner. We must be a partaker in his sufferings as Thomas when he said …unto his fellow disciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him –John 11:16.

To visit the Christ child will require us to haunt the place outside the inn. The Inn Crowd is the place of popular reception, popular understanding, and popular behavior. There awaits the comforts of friends, family, and fraternity, while it ministers a sense of belonging and acceptance. Christ knew no such luxury in His birth nor in His death, and He made His choice outside of the Inn Crowd.

Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed? For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not –Isaiah 53:1-3.

The despised shepherds lived most of their lives outside of the Inn Crowd and were the first to believe and receive Him. Loyalty to Christ requires separation from the loyalties of the world including most of its ever-popular celebration of Christ’s birth. It is a call to follow His choice to go without the camp. This is the difference between nominal worship and the heartfelt praise of His redeemed who will but follow Him to the manger.

Why lies He in such mean estate,
Where ox and ass are feeding?
Good Christians, fear, for sinners here
The silent Word is pleading.
Nails, spears shall pierce him through,
The cross he bore for me, for you.
Hail, hail the Word made flesh,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

…A Song

Those who desire to know him must venture outside The Inn and partake in …the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10. As they reap the scoffing and scorn of the Inn Crowd, they will also find that they are greeted with a heavenly song. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men –Luke 2:14.

As our portion in this earthly life diminishes, our quantum of glorious praise shall increase. The Jews were offended that the Messiah did not come to give them a larger portion and victory over the Roman world. Jesus …beheld the city, and wept over it, Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes –Luke 19:41-42. Peace on earth will never be apprehended by environmental perfection. Those lodged at The Inn, find their peace within the clean, convenient, and courteous companionship of each other. This is the popular, pampered peace the world promotes and portrays, but does not coincide with that of the babe in the meager manger. But it was those outside the inn that learned the song.

And they sung as it were a new song … and no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth –Revelation 14:3. These are those who are at peace with their earthly lot. These shall not be moved when someone else is promoted, carries more earthly possessions, or receives more attention. They are content with a cottage while others cloister in a castle. They cannot be persuaded to envy though others are… going there, doing that, or owning one. Others …think it strange that ye run not with them to the same excess of riot, speaking evil of you –1 Peter 4:4.

Peace on earth is nothing more than the great gain that arrives with godliness and contentment. Some wonder how David could fall into sin with Bathsheba while he possessed his multiple wives. How could he not? An abundance of options does not breed greater contentment. The fussing child in the store bawls because his hands are full, and he cannot have more. So, do the motel connoisseurs on our day depreciate any lodging accommodations that are less than perfect. They can sing the praises of a five-star hotel and diner, but are oblivious to the song by the manger.

Those whose hearts resound with goodwill to men, experience great joy as the wealthiest of earth’s inhabitants. They can rejoice in another’s promotion, good fortune, and success. In doing so, they inherit the earth. This is the song that Stephen sang proceeding his earthly departure. He spake of Abraham removing himself from his land, Acts 7:3 of Joseph being sold out of his home, vs.9 and of Moses being cast out, and fleeing to Midian. vs.21. This is he, that was in the church in the wilderness. vs.38. This was the same despised church that Stephen took up membership in and thus he received the same treatment. Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, And cast him out of the city, and stoned him … And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep –Acts 7:57-60.

So bring him incense, gold, and myrrh,
Come, peasant, king, to own him.
The King of kings salvation brings,
Let loving hearts enthrone him.

This is glory to God. This is peace on earth. This is goodwill toward men.

Op die groot skeidslyn van ons afgemete tydlyn van jare staan die vleeswording en geboorte van ons Here Jesus Christus. Hy neem hierdie plek met reg in, want geen ander koms kon die mensdom so treffend beïnvloed nie. Die jare voor sy geboorte staan bekend as v.C., oftewel “voor Christus”, terwyl die jare daarna as n.C. bekend staan (Anno Domini, Latyn vir “die jaar van ons Here”). Hoewel sy geboorte heeltemal deur heidense invloede en persoonlike selfbevrediging deurmekaargekrap en vertroebel is, is die eenvoudige, stralende skoonheid van die gebeurtenis steeds beskikbaar vir almal wat die onbedorwe toneel maar eerlik wil aanskou.

Hoewel die kalender Christus se geboorte op 25 Desember plaas, het die meeste geleerdes tot die slotsom gekom dat hierdie datum nie korrek is nie. Daar is ook vasgestel dat die werklike jaar wat aan sy geboorte toegeskryf word, met 4–6 jaar verskil. Die datum is deur die biskop van Rome vasgestel in ooreenstemming met ’n gewilde heidense fees genaamd Saturnalia. Die heidense Romeine het Saturnus as die god van landbou aanbid deur fees te vier, partytjies te hou, hul huise met immergroen takke te versier, geskenke uit te ruil en oor die algemeen vrolik te wees. Die biskop se doel was om ’n heiligende invloed op die uitspattigheid uit te oefen en die algemene bevolking se gedagtes van selfsugtige selfbevrediging na God wat mens geword het, te keer. Soos ons kan verwag, het die heidense feestelikhede onverpoos voortgegaan. Die kerk, wat aanvanklik die voorstel afgekeur het, het uiteindelik die idee aanvaar en was teen die vierde eeu ten volle aangepas by en geïndoktrineer in die bastervermenging van die Christelike en die heidense.

Vandag sit ons dus met ’n dilemma. Hoe behoort ’n Christen Christus se geboorte te beskou? Moet ons probeer om Christus in Kersfees te hou, of Hom daaruit te haal? Ongeag ons mening moet elkeen van ons waarlik besluit om die betekenis van die maagdelike geboorte te verstaan, los van die emosionele bande met die basterviering, en die geboorte op ’n deur God bepaalde wyse te erken. In teenstelling met die miljoene wat sy geboorte in ons tyd vier, was daar maar ’n handjievol wat die werklike gebeurtenis kon bywoon en waardig was om dit by te woon.

Daar was herders in dieselfde streek wat in die oop veld gebly en snags oor hulle kudde wag gehou het. En kyk, ’n engel van die Here het by hulle kom staan, en die heerlikheid van die Here het rondom hulle geskyn, en hulle was baie bang. Toe sê die engel vir hulle: “Moenie bang wees nie, want kyk, ek bring vir julle goeie nuus van groot blydskap wat vir die hele volk sal wees. Vandag is daar vir julle in die stad van Dawid ’n Verlosser gebore, Christus die Here. Dit sal vir julle die teken wees: julle sal ’n baba vind wat in doeke toegedraai is en in ’n krip lê.” En skielik was daar saam met die engel ’n menigte van die hemelse leërmag wat God geprys en gesê het: “Eer aan God in die hoogste hemel, en vrede op aarde vir die mense in wie Hy ’n welbehae het.” –Lukas 2:8-14.

Dit was ’n groep nederige herders wat die eerste geboorteaankondiging ontvang het. Selfs hierdie eenvoudige, ongeleerde manne het geweet van die verwagte Messias en na Hom verlang. Maar jy, Betlehem-Efrata, al is jy klein onder die duisende van Juda, uit jou sal daar vir My iemand kom wat ’n heerser in Israel sal wees; sy oorsprong is uit die voortyd, uit die dae van die ewigheid. –Miga 5:2.

Toe die sterbesaaide hemelruim skielik lewendig word, het die herders in betowerde verwondering na die toneel voor hulle gestaar, en ’n nuwe dag het oor die horison van hulle siele begin aanbreek. Die engelekoor het sy boodskap aan die herders verkondig en toe kort daarna verdwyn; tog het die goeie nuus gebly. Die ontmoeting was maar ’n kortstondige damp, maar ’n drievoudige geur het in die brandende harte van hierdie manne bly hang: ’n Verlosser… ’n Teken… en ’n Lied…

…’n Verlosser

Die blote feit dat ’n Verlosser beloof word, impliseer dat daar iets is waarvan ons verlos moet word. Wat ons fisiese lot ook al mag wees, die mens se geestelike toestand is sedert die sondeval in Eden op die rand van wanhoop. Deur vier millennia heen het die mensdom onder die duiwelse wolk van sonde weggeskuil, en baie het die prooi geword van die dreigende duisternis daarvan. Sonde kan ’n kers van hoop neem en dit in ’n oomblik doodslaan. Dit kan sy yskoue asem oor die mooiste blomme blaas en hulle in ’n oomblik laat verwelk. Dit neem liefdevolle huwelike en dompel hulle in die maalstroom van interne oorlog. Dit neem die opregte bloei van die jeug en beroof dit van die geur van sy onskuld. Diegene wat daarin geslaag het om van die slawerny van die persoonlike onderwerping daaraan los te breek, kan maklik sien hoe hulle nouliks aan die waansinnige samelewing rondom hulle ontsnap het. Daarom het die nederige herders hulle verheug oor die koms van ’n Verlosser.

Almal het gesondig en onder die veroordeling daarvan gekom. Die blote gedagte aan bevryding van die naderende straf wat ons regverdig toekom, is soos ’n vars asemteug. God het immers nie sy Seun na die wêreld gestuur om die wêreld te veroordeel nie, maar sodat die wêreld deur Hom verlos kan word. –Johannes 3:17. Diegene wat waarlik tot bekering gekom het, dra die hoop op die ewige lewe en die belofte van die hemel in hul siele. Hulle word nuwe skeppings wanneer die Heilige Gees in hulle harte kom woon. Hoewel dit ’n dramatiese uitwerking op ’n gelowige se lewe het, is dit nie die enigste sake wat met verlossing verband hou nie. Hierdie Verlosser is ook ’n Here.

Net soos die titel “Verlosser” ’n dringende nood impliseer, so impliseer die naam “Christus, die Here” ook ’n oorheersende oorwinning. Wie sonde doen, is uit die duiwel, want die duiwel sondig van die begin af. Hiervoor het die Seun van God verskyn: om die werke van die duiwel te vernietig. –1 Johannes 3:8. Ons sal nie net van die veroordeling van sonde bevry word nie, maar moet ook van die mag en invloed daarvan gered word. Die verwoestende gewoontes wat ons in ons sondige natuur opgebou het, moet ’n dodelike slag toegedien word. Die hartstogte en begeertes wat ons oorweldig het voordat sy invloed in ons lewens gekom het, moet aan Hom onderworpe wees. Die egoïstiese trots en onbeheerste humeur in die mens, wat verhoudings vernietig en die lewens van diegene vir wie ons lief is om ons heen verwond het, moet ook in hierdie oorwinning verswelg word. As Christus nie ons Here is nie, is Hy ook nie ons Verlosser nie.

Watter kind is dit wat daar rus,
Op Maria se skoot aan die slaap?
Wie begroet die engele met lieflike lofliedere,
terwyl herders wag hou?
Dit, dit is Christus die Koning,
Wat herders bewaak en engele besing.
Haastig, haastig, bring Hom lof,
Die Baba, Maria se Seun.

…’n Teken

’n Mens sou tereg kon dink dat die engelverskyning ’n veel groter teken was as die baba in die krip. Wie van ons het al ooit die vreugde ervaar om so ’n hemelse koor te hoor? Wanneer ons die verhaal lees, kan ’n mens jou net die meesleurende skoonheid voorstel van ’n magdom hemelse stemme wat saam weerklink en die berghang vul met ’n glimp van die hemel soos die aarde dit sedert die skeppingsdag nog nooit geken het nie: Toe die môresterre saam gejubel het en al die hemelse wesens van vreugde uitgeroep het. –Job 38:7. Tog was die engele nie die teken nie.

Die feit dat hierdie kind deur die Heilige Gees verwek is, soos in Matteus 1:20 uiteengesit, moet deur die geloof aanvaar word en kan kwalik as ’n aardse teken beskou word. Dat die kind in doeke toegedraai was, was niks buitengewoons nie, want al die moeders van daardie tyd het dit gedoen. In een van die mees grafiese hoofstukke wat ’n kind se geboorte uitbeeld, noem God dat niemand vir Israel se geboorte omgegee het nie: Wat jou geboorte betref, op die dag toe jy gebore is, is jou naelstring nie afgesny nie, jy is nie met water gewas om jou skoon te maak nie; jy is glad nie met sout ingevryf of in doeke toegedraai nie. –Esegiël 16:4. Hierdie leidrade sal nutteloos wees in ’n soektog na die kind. Die onmiskenbare teken van hierdie gebeurtenis word aangedui deur die baba se wieg. Geen moeder sou ’n veestal as geboortekamer kies en haar pasgebore baba in ’n voerbak neerlê tensy noodsaaklikheid dit vereis het nie.

Die teken van die krip, saam met hulle kennis van die Skrif oor Betlehem, was al wat die herders nodig gehad het om die kind te vind. Die Skrif maak hoegenaamd geen melding van die gerief van ’n stal nie. Die herders was goed vertroud met die dele van die dorp wat vir die diere bestem was, en hulle het vertrek.

Daarom het Jesus ook buite die poort gely om die volk deur sy eie bloed te heilig. Laat ons dan na Hom toe uitgaan, buite die kamp, en sy smaad dra. –Hebreërs 13:12-13. Hierdie teken vra om persoonlike deelname. Elkeen wie se hart lojaal aan die toneel klop, moet ook saam met Hom gaan. Dit sal nie vervul word deur ’n lewende geboortetoneel by te woon, ’n “Messias”-uitvoering te sien of vir Ouma se Kersete te gaan nie. Ons moet deel hê aan sy lyding, soos Tomas toe hy gesê het …vir sy mededissipels: “Laat ons ook gaan, sodat ons saam met Hom kan sterf.” –Johannes 11:16.

Om die Christuskind te besoek, sal vereis dat ons buite die herberg bly. Die Herbergskare is die plek van gewilde ontvangs, gewilde begrip en gewilde gedrag. Daar wag die gerief van vriende, familie en kameraadskap, terwyl dit ’n gevoel van tuishoort en aanvaarding bied. Christus het nie sulke weelde geken tydens sy geboorte of sy dood nie, en Hy het sy keuse buite die Herbergskare gemaak.

Wie het geglo wat ons gehoor het? En aan wie is die arm van die HERE geopenbaar? Hy het voor Hom opgegroei soos ’n jong loot, soos ’n wortel uit droë grond. Hy het geen gestalte of prag gehad dat ons na Hom sou kyk nie, geen voorkoms dat ons Hom sou begeer nie. Hy is verag en deur mense verwerp, ’n man van smarte, vertroud met lyding. Soos iemand vir wie mense hulle gesig verberg, is Hy verag, en ons het Hom nie geag nie. –Jesaja 53:1-3.

Die veragte herders het die grootste deel van hulle lewens buite die Herbergskare deurgebring en was die eerstes wat in Hom geglo en Hom ontvang het. Lojaliteit aan Christus vereis dat ons ons afskei van die lojaliteite van die wêreld, met inbegrip van die meeste van sy immergewilde viering van Christus se geboorte. Dit is ’n oproep om sy keuse te volg en buite die kamp te gaan. Dit is die verskil tussen blote naam-aanbidding en die hartgrondige lof van sy verlostes wat Hom wel tot by die krip sal volg.

Waarom lê Hy in so ’n nederige plek,
Waar os en esel vreet?
Goeie Christene, vrees, want hier pleit die stille Woord vir sondaars.

Spykers, spiese sal Hom deurboor,
Die kruis het Hy vir my, vir jou gedra.
Wees gegroet, wees gegroet, die Woord wat vlees geword het,
Die Baba, Maria se Seun.

…’n Lied

Diegene wat Hom wil ken, moet buite die Herberg waag en deel hê aan …die gemeenskap aan sy lyding, deur aan sy dood gelykvormig te word. –Filippense 3:10. Terwyl hulle die spot en veragting van die Herbergskare oes, sal hulle ook ontdek dat hulle met ’n hemelse lied begroet word. Eer aan God in die hoogste hemel, en vrede op aarde vir die mense in wie Hy ’n welbehae het. –Lukas 2:14.

Namate ons deel in hierdie aardse lewe afneem, sal ons mate van heerlike lof toeneem. Die Jode het aanstoot geneem omdat die Messias nie gekom het om hulle ’n groter deel en die oorwinning oor die Romeinse wêreld te gee nie. Jesus …het die stad gesien en daaroor gehuil en gesê: “As jy, ja jy, op hierdie dag maar geweet het wat vir jou vrede bring! Maar nou is dit vir jou oë verborge.” –Lukas 19:41-42. Vrede op aarde sal nooit deur omgewingsvolmaaktheid verkry word nie. Diegene wat in Die Herberg tuisgaan, vind hul vrede in mekaar se skoon, gerieflike en hoflike geselskap. Dit is die gewilde, vertroetelde vrede wat die wêreld bevorder en uitbeeld, maar dit strook nie met dié van die baba in die armoedige krip nie. Maar dit was dié buite die herberg wat die lied geleer het.

En hulle het ’n nuwe lied gesing … en niemand kon daardie lied leer nie, behalwe die honderd-vier-en-veertigduisend wat van die aarde losgekoop is. –Openbaring 14:3. Dit is mense wat vrede het met hul aardse lot. Hulle sal nie ontsteld raak wanneer iemand anders bevorder word, meer aardse besittings het of meer aandag kry nie. Hulle is tevrede met ’n kothuis terwyl ander hulle in ’n kasteel afsonder. Hulle kan nie daartoe verlei word om jaloers te wees nie, al is ander… op pad daarheen, doen dit, of besit een. Ander …vind dit vreemd dat julle nie saam met hulle in dieselfde losbandige uitspattigheid hardloop nie, en beswadder julle daarom. –1 Petrus 4:4.

Vrede op aarde is niks anders nie as die groot wins wat saam met godsvrug en vergenoegdheid kom. Sommige wonder hoe Dawid met Batseba in sonde kon verval terwyl hy sy veelvuldige vroue gehad het. Hoe kon hy nie? ’n Oorvloed keuses kweek nie groter vergenoegdheid nie. Die kind wat in die winkel kla en skree, doen dit omdat sy hande vol is en hy nie meer kan kry nie. So verkleineer die motelkenners van ons tyd enige verblyf wat nie volmaak is nie. Hulle kan die lof van ’n vyfsterhotel en -restaurant besing, maar is blind vir die lied by die krip.

Diegene wie se harte van welwillendheid teenoor mense weerklink, ervaar groot vreugde as die rykstes van die aarde se bewoners. Hulle kan hulle verheug oor ’n ander se bevordering, voorspoed en sukses. Deur dit te doen, beërf hulle die aarde. Dit is die lied wat Stefanus gesing het voordat hy hierdie aardse lewe verlaat het. Hy het gepraat van Abraham wat uit sy land vertrek, Handelinge 7:3; van Josef wat uit sy huis verkoop is, v.9; en van Moses wat weggestuur is en na Midian gevlug het, v.21. Dit is hy wat in die kerk in die woestyn was, v.38. Dit was dieselfde veragte kerk waarby Stefanus aangesluit het, en daarom het hy dieselfde behandeling ontvang. Toe het hulle met ’n harde stem uitgeroep, hulle ore toegedruk en soos een man op hom afgestorm. Hulle het hom uit die stad uitgegooi en hom gestenig … Hy het op sy knieë geval en hard uitgeroep: “Here, reken hulle hierdie sonde nie toe nie!” Nadat hy dit gesê het, het hy ontslaap. –Handelinge 7:57-60.

Bring Hom dan wierook, goud en mirre,
Kom, boer en koning, erken Hom.
Die Koning van konings bring verlossing,
Laat liefdevolle harte Hom as Koning ontvang.

Dit is heerlikheid aan God. Dit is vrede op aarde. Dit is welwillendheid teenoor mense.

I used to pray for sunshine,
No storms to mark the sky.
For cool breezes and flowers
To please and turn my eye.

I used to pray for happiness,
For smiles, joy, and peace.
That all things would be easy,
And all harsh things would cease.

I used to pray for someone,
To walk with in this life.
To love, laugh with, and cherish,
And dissipate all strife.

I used to pray that always
Life’s pathways would be clear.
That no unwanted circumstance
Would make existence drear.

But those prayers seemed to go unheeded,
For life didn’t flow that way.
The storms—they came uninvited,
Thick rains made many a dark day.

The flowers were not to be seen,
The wind did cut and slash.
No peace could be found about me;
Instead, the thunder did crash.

Not one was found to walk with me,
Alone, through rough ways I did roam.
Gone were the dreams of tranquility,
My soul cried with desire for a home.

Then, a rich voice spoke inside me,
“You’ve been seeking the things you can see.
The true prayers of your heart can be answered,
If you would only but look unto Me.

I have heard your needs and desires,
Your prayers did not fall unheard.
But I saw that your heart needed different
Than the way that ease had preferred.

You prayed for clear skies and sunshine,
For cool breezes and flowers to start.
But I saw that just these would not yield you
The real peace you sought in your heart.

I ordered the rough ways you have followed,
Not to disappoint, but to purge.
For I knew that true happiness begins only
In the heart that with Me does merge.”

So I fell at the feet of my Master
And yielded to His will and His plan.
No longer demanding my wants now,
But trusting He’d finish what He began.

Not long after, I found I was happy;
Not a cloud in my heart could prevail.
Even if my circumstances seemed weary,
No outer storm my inner Sunshine could pale.

The cool breezes of sweet rest in Him,
Did calm all my worries and fears.
And always the flowers of His promises,
Were visible when life brought me tears.

I found also, I no longer walked alone;
The Good Shepherd was there by my side!
With Him I could share my joys and sorrows,
And amidst any battle, in Him I could hide.

So now instead of praying
For things of earthly ease,
I thank the Lord for sending things
That brought me to my knees.

I pray instead for humility,
To lead me through the day.
For an eye to serve, and share the blessings,
That the Lord does send my way.

I pray that my heart would be yielded,
To the touch of the Master’s hand.
Allowing His will to change me,
Through everything He has planned.

For I’ve found that true happiness,
Is not in a smooth, perfect life.
But it’s found when in Christ we are rooted,
Not moved through fire or strife.

If He rules the inmost being,
Then nothing outside will disturb.
For He is the solid Foundation,
And the real source of True Life superb.

Dulu aku berdoa memohon sinar mentari,
Tanpa badai yang menggores langit.
Memohon angin sejuk dan bunga-bunga
Yang menyenangkan dan memikat mataku.

Dulu aku berdoa memohon kebahagiaan,
Senyuman, sukacita, dan kedamaian.
Agar segala sesuatu berjalan mudah,
Dan semua yang sulit segera berlalu.

Dulu aku berdoa memohon seseorang,
Untuk menemani langkahku menjalani hidup ini.
Untuk mencintai, tertawa bersama, dan menyayangi,
Serta mengakhiri segala pertikaian.

Dulu aku selalu berdoa
Agar jalan hidupku terbentang jelas.
Agar tak ada keadaan yang tak kuinginkan
Membuat hidup terasa suram.

Namun, doa-doa itu seolah tak terjawab,
Sebab hidup tak berjalan seperti itu.
Badai datang tanpa diundang,
Hujan lebat membuat banyak hari kelam.

Bunga-bunga tak tampak,
Angin menerpa dan mengiris.
Tak ada kedamaian di sekelilingku;
Yang terdengar hanyalah gemuruh guntur.

Tak seorang pun kutemukan untuk berjalan bersamaku,
Sendirian, aku mengembara di jalan-jalan yang sulit.
Sirnalah impian akan ketenteraman,
Jiwaku merintih mendambakan sebuah rumah.

Lalu, suara yang penuh kelembutan berbicara di dalam diriku,
“Engkau telah mencari hal-hal yang dapat kaulihat.
Doa-doa sejati dalam hatimu dapat terjawab,
Asalkan engkau mau memandang kepada-Ku.

Aku telah mendengar kebutuhan dan keinginanmu,
Doa-doamu tidaklah luput dari pendengaran-Ku.
Namun, Aku melihat bahwa hatimu membutuhkan hal yang berbeda
Dari apa yang diinginkan oleh kenyamanan.

Engkau berdoa memohon langit cerah dan sinar mentari,
Angin sejuk dan bunga-bunga bermekaran.
Namun, Aku melihat bahwa semua itu saja tak akan memberimu
Kedamaian sejati yang kau cari di dalam hati.

Aku menetapkan jalan-jalan sulit yang kautempuh,
Bukan untuk mengecewakan, melainkan untuk memurnikanmu.
Sebab Aku tahu bahwa kebahagiaan sejati hanya dimulai
Di dalam hati yang menyatu dengan-Ku.”

Maka aku pun tersungkur di kaki Tuanku
Dan berserah kepada kehendak dan rencana-Nya.
Tak lagi menuntut apa yang kuinginkan,
Melainkan percaya bahwa Dia akan menyelesaikan apa yang telah dimulai-Nya.

Tak lama kemudian, aku mendapati diriku bahagia;
Tak ada awan yang dapat menguasai hatiku.
Sekalipun keadaanku terasa melelahkan,
Tak ada badai di luar yang dapat meredupkan Sinar Mentari di dalam diriku.

Angin sejuk dari ketenteraman manis di dalam Dia
Menenangkan segala kekhawatiran dan ketakutanku.
Dan bunga-bunga janji-Nya senantiasa
Tampak saat hidup membuatku menangis.

Selain itu, kusadari bahwa aku tak lagi berjalan sendirian;
Gembala yang Baik ada di sisiku!
Bersama-Nya aku dapat berbagi sukacita dan dukaku,
Dan dalam peperangan apa pun, aku dapat berlindung di dalam Dia.

Maka kini, alih-alih berdoa
Memohon kenyamanan duniawi,
Aku bersyukur kepada Tuhan karena mengirimkan hal-hal
Yang membuatku berlutut.

Sebaliknya, aku berdoa memohon kerendahan hati,
Agar menuntunku sepanjang hari.
Memohon mata yang peka untuk melayani dan berbagi berkat,
Yang Tuhan kirimkan kepadaku.

Aku berdoa agar hatiku berserah,
Pada sentuhan tangan Sang Guru.
Membiarkan kehendak-Nya mengubah diriku,
Melalui segala yang telah direncanakan-Nya.

Sebab aku telah mendapati bahwa kebahagiaan sejati
Bukanlah hidup yang mulus dan sempurna.
Kebahagiaan ditemukan saat kita berakar di dalam Kristus,
Tak tergoyahkan oleh api ataupun pertikaian.

Jika Dia memerintah batin terdalam,
Maka tak ada apa pun di luar yang akan mengusik.
Sebab Dialah Dasar yang kokoh,
Dan sumber sejati Kehidupan Sejati yang agung.

The last several years God has been leading me through a valley, a long and seemingly unending one. It seems as soon as one situation resolves; another one pops up. These difficulties demand a response. Many times, it’s not so much a response of physical action as it is a response of the spirit. For me, it took about two years before I came to a place of beginning to learn healthy and, even more importantly, Biblical emotional choices.

“Spirit” in this article is defined as “a temper or disposition of the mind or outlook.” The Bible mentions several types of spirits that God has been teaching me. Two are more general for everyone and two are specifically given for us ladies.

Before it is of any value to discuss what a Biblical and healthy spirit is, it is essential that we understand that it is a choice. It is not a result of circumstances. It will not come upon us on a whim. As young ladies, especially, we find it very easy to be driven by emotions. But most emotions that “drive” us are not healthy. A Biblical spirit is a result of conscious—not emotional, circumstance-driven—choices. If we let them, unhealthy emotions can become monstrous and pull us downward to many undesirable places such as depression, bitterness, and immorality. In response, God calls us to intentionally choose the type of spirit that is defined in the Bible.

A Broken Spirit

For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite [crushed] and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones –Isaiah 57:15.

Above all else, it is essential that we choose to become broken. It is hard to stress the importance of this enough. If we do not allow ourselves to become broken, we are opening the door for all manner of negative emotions, reactions, and, especially, sin.

Brokenness is a difficult, almost impossible choice to make on our own. Often God leads us into difficult situations where we must make a choice—either godly brokenness, or something unhealthy like anger or discouragement. Brokenness strips everything away. It requires us to surrender our control over bad things such as sickness or disappointment and over good things like our desires for the future. Brokenness means we give God control of everything; we keep nothing. Most times deep brokenness doesn’t happen all at once; it’s a painful journey in which we give up, and give up, and give up again. Without becoming bitter. Without losing faith in God. In fact, the times of crushing are when we choose to believe good things of God even if there seems to be no good reason to.

Brokenness is a choice—a very difficult one which paves the way for God to receive glory, since it is the process of eliminating self. It also makes it possible for other finer qualities to reveal themselves.

A Sober Spirit

Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind, [and] be sober… –1 Peter 1:13.

The definition of “sober” in this verse is “to be calm and collected in spirit; to be temperate, dispassionate.” This is an intriguing word. According to this verse, we are commanded to be calm and collected in spirit. As young ladies, we know how easy and even automatic it is to let our feelings about situations and circumstances spiral out of control.

For myself, I was at a place of limbo and uncertainty, and I was so discouraged that I could hardly go on. I could not focus on important things like work and reaching out to others. While studying this verse, God convicted me that, yes, even though I was in a very dark time, His command to me was to be calm and not let my raging emotions control. He brought me to a place where I had to choose, moment by moment, to take control of my spirit. I found that as I chose God’s way, He gave me the grace to live accordingly, resulting in a much more stable and restful spirit.

So, take heart in the dark times! Choose to respond to circumstances in God’s way. As He refines your spirit and your character, He also wants to receive the glory for it. This is a journey God is taking me on, and I’m thankful to Him for continuing to patiently break and shape my spirit for His glory.

A Meek Spirit

But let it be … the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit… –1 Peter 3:4.

In many ways a meek spirit is a yielded spirit. It is a spirit that is totally under the control of Almighty God. It does not fight unpleasant circumstances or strive to make life “better.” But neither is it a passive, “roll with punches”, cowering attitude. Actually, this spirit denotes someone who has gifts and abilities, is trained and effective, and could be very useful to the work of the church, yet is in complete subjection to God, moving only at His will.

A Quiet Spirit

But let it be … the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit… –1 Peter 3:4.

A quiet and restful spirit is an amazing quality. It is not humanly possible to achieve. When you see this spirit in someone, you can know it comes from a heart of brokenness. According to Isaiah, it is a choice: …In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not –Isaiah 30:15.

A quiet spirit and a meek spirit go hand in hand. It is an attitude of sitting back and letting God lead—whether exciting or boring, whether easy or difficult—and not resisting Him in any way.

There are times when we feel very disquieted in spirit, and it’s not possible to pull ourselves out of it by sheer willpower. But the Word of God is life-giving, and by studying the promises of God we can receive peace and rest for our spirits, as well as courage and grace to go on. I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved. Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope –Psalms 16:8, 9.

Nos últimos anos, Deus tem me conduzido por um vale, um vale longo e aparentemente interminável. Parece que, assim que uma situação se resolve, outra surge. Essas dificuldades exigem uma resposta. Muitas vezes, não se trata tanto de uma resposta em forma de ação física, mas de uma resposta do espírito. Para mim, foram necessários cerca de dois anos até chegar ao ponto de começar a aprender a fazer escolhas emocionais saudáveis e, mais importante ainda, bíblicas.

Neste artigo, “espírito” é definido como “temperamento ou disposição da mente ou perspectiva”. A Bíblia menciona vários tipos de espírito sobre os quais Deus tem me ensinado. Dois são mais gerais, para todos, e dois são dados especificamente a nós, mulheres.

Antes que seja útil discutir o que é um espírito bíblico e saudável, é essencial que entendamos que se trata de uma escolha. Não é resultado das circunstâncias. Não nos sobrevém por capricho. Especialmente quando somos jovens, é muito fácil sermos guiadas pelas emoções. Mas a maioria das emoções que nos “guiam” não é saudável. Um espírito bíblico resulta de escolhas conscientes — não emocionais, nem movidas pelas circunstâncias. Se permitirmos, emoções pouco saudáveis podem se tornar monstruosas e nos arrastar para muitos lugares indesejáveis, como a depressão, a amargura e a imoralidade. Em resposta, Deus nos chama a escolher intencionalmente o tipo de espírito definido na Bíblia.

Um espírito quebrantado

Pois assim diz o Alto e Sublime, que habita a eternidade, cujo nome é Santo: Habito no lugar alto e santo, e também com aquele que tem espírito contrito [quebrantado] e humilde, para vivificar o espírito dos humildes e vivificar o coração dos contritos –Isaías 57:15.

Acima de tudo, é essencial que escolhamos nos tornar quebrantadas. É difícil enfatizar suficientemente a importância disso. Se não permitirmos que nos tornemos quebrantadas, estaremos abrindo a porta para todo tipo de emoção e reação negativa e, especialmente, para o pecado.

O quebrantamento é uma escolha difícil, quase impossível de fazer por conta própria. Muitas vezes, Deus nos conduz a situações difíceis nas quais precisamos escolher — ou o quebrantamento piedoso, ou algo prejudicial, como a ira ou o desânimo. O quebrantamento tira tudo de nós. Exige que abramos mão do controle sobre coisas ruins, como doenças ou decepções, e sobre coisas boas, como nossos desejos para o futuro. Quebrantamento significa entregar a Deus o controle de tudo; não guardamos nada para nós. Na maioria das vezes, o quebrantamento profundo não acontece de uma só vez; é uma jornada dolorosa na qual desistimos, e desistimos, e desistimos novamente. Sem nos tornarmos amargas. Sem perdermos a fé em Deus. Na verdade, os momentos de esmagamento são aqueles em que escolhemos crer coisas boas a respeito de Deus, mesmo quando parece não haver nenhuma boa razão para isso.

O quebrantamento é uma escolha — muito difícil, que prepara o caminho para que Deus receba a glória, pois é o processo de eliminar o eu. Também torna possível que outras qualidades mais refinadas se revelem.

Um espírito sóbrio

Portanto, cingindo os lombos do vosso entendimento, [e] sede sóbrias… –1 Pedro 1:13.

O significado de “sóbrio” neste versículo é “ser calma e serena de espírito; ser moderada, sem se deixar levar pelas emoções”. É uma palavra intrigante. De acordo com este versículo, recebemos a ordem de ser calmas e serenas de espírito. Como jovens, sabemos como é fácil, e até automático, deixar que nossos sentimentos a respeito de situações e circunstâncias saiam do controle.

Quanto a mim, eu estava num estado de indefinição e incerteza, e tão desanimada que mal conseguia seguir em frente. Não conseguia me concentrar em coisas importantes, como o trabalho e o cuidado com os outros. Enquanto estudava este versículo, Deus me convenceu de que, sim, mesmo estando num período muito sombrio, a ordem que me dava era para que eu permanecesse calma e não deixasse minhas emoções descontroladas me dominarem. Ele me levou a um ponto em que eu precisava escolher, momento a momento, assumir o controle do meu espírito. Descobri que, quando escolhia o caminho de Deus, Ele me concedia a graça de viver de acordo com ele, resultando num espírito muito mais estável e tranquilo.

Portanto, tenham coragem nos momentos sombrios! Escolham responder às circunstâncias à maneira de Deus. Ao refinar seu espírito e seu caráter, Ele também quer receber a glória por isso. Esta é uma jornada pela qual Deus está me conduzindo, e sou grata a Ele por continuar, com paciência, a quebrantar e moldar meu espírito para a Sua glória.

Um espírito manso

Mas seja … o adorno de um espírito manso e tranquilo… –1 Pedro 3:4.

Em muitos aspectos, um espírito manso é um espírito submisso. É um espírito que está totalmente sob o controle do Deus Todo-Poderoso. Não luta contra circunstâncias desagradáveis nem se esforça para tornar a vida “melhor”. Mas também não é uma atitude passiva de “aceitar os golpes”, que se encolhe de medo. Na verdade, esse espírito caracteriza alguém que tem dons e habilidades, é treinado e eficaz e poderia ser muito útil para o trabalho da igreja, mas está em completa sujeição a Deus, agindo somente segundo a vontade dEle.

Um espírito tranquilo

Mas seja … o adorno de um espírito manso e tranquilo… –1 Pedro 3:4.

Um espírito tranquilo e sereno é uma qualidade extraordinária. Não é possível alcançá-la por meios humanos. Quando você vê esse espírito em alguém, pode saber que ele vem de um coração quebrantado. De acordo com Isaías, é uma escolha: …No retorno e no descanso estaria a vossa salvação; na tranquilidade e na confiança estaria a vossa força: mas vós não quisestes –Isaías 30:15.

Um espírito tranquilo e um espírito manso caminham juntos. É uma atitude de recuar e deixar Deus conduzir — seja algo empolgante ou entediante, fácil ou difícil — sem resistir a Ele de maneira alguma.

Há momentos em que nos sentimos muito inquietas de espírito, e não é possível sair disso apenas pela força de vontade. Mas a Palavra de Deus dá vida e, ao estudarmos as promessas de Deus, podemos receber paz e descanso para o nosso espírito, bem como coragem e graça para seguir em frente. Tenho posto o SENHOR continuamente diante de mim; porque ele está à minha direita, não serei abalada. Portanto, o meu coração está alegre, e a minha glória exulta; também a minha carne repousará em esperança –Salmos 16:8, 9.

The last several years God has been leading me through a valley, a long and seemingly unending one. It seems as soon as one situation resolves; another one pops up. These difficulties demand a response. Many times, it’s not so much a response of physical action as it is a response of the spirit. For me, it took about two years before I came to a place of beginning to learn healthy and, even more importantly, Biblical emotional choices.

“Spirit” in this article is defined as “a temper or disposition of the mind or outlook.” The Bible mentions several types of spirits that God has been teaching me. Two are more general for everyone and two are specifically given for us ladies.

Before it is of any value to discuss what a Biblical and healthy spirit is, it is essential that we understand that it is a choice. It is not a result of circumstances. It will not come upon us on a whim. As young ladies, especially, we find it very easy to be driven by emotions. But most emotions that “drive” us are not healthy. A Biblical spirit is a result of conscious—not emotional, circumstance-driven—choices. If we let them, unhealthy emotions can become monstrous and pull us downward to many undesirable places such as depression, bitterness, and immorality. In response, God calls us to intentionally choose the type of spirit that is defined in the Bible.

A Broken Spirit

For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite [crushed] and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones –Isaiah 57:15.

Above all else, it is essential that we choose to become broken. It is hard to stress the importance of this enough. If we do not allow ourselves to become broken, we are opening the door for all manner of negative emotions, reactions, and, especially, sin.

Brokenness is a difficult, almost impossible choice to make on our own. Often God leads us into difficult situations where we must make a choice—either godly brokenness, or something unhealthy like anger or discouragement. Brokenness strips everything away. It requires us to surrender our control over bad things such as sickness or disappointment and over good things like our desires for the future. Brokenness means we give God control of everything; we keep nothing. Most times deep brokenness doesn’t happen all at once; it’s a painful journey in which we give up, and give up, and give up again. Without becoming bitter. Without losing faith in God. In fact, the times of crushing are when we choose to believe good things of God even if there seems to be no good reason to.

Brokenness is a choice—a very difficult one which paves the way for God to receive glory, since it is the process of eliminating self. It also makes it possible for other finer qualities to reveal themselves.

A Sober Spirit

Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind, [and] be sober… –1 Peter 1:13.

The definition of “sober” in this verse is “to be calm and collected in spirit; to be temperate, dispassionate.” This is an intriguing word. According to this verse, we are commanded to be calm and collected in spirit. As young ladies, we know how easy and even automatic it is to let our feelings about situations and circumstances spiral out of control.

For myself, I was at a place of limbo and uncertainty, and I was so discouraged that I could hardly go on. I could not focus on important things like work and reaching out to others. While studying this verse, God convicted me that, yes, even though I was in a very dark time, His command to me was to be calm and not let my raging emotions control. He brought me to a place where I had to choose, moment by moment, to take control of my spirit. I found that as I chose God’s way, He gave me the grace to live accordingly, resulting in a much more stable and restful spirit.

So, take heart in the dark times! Choose to respond to circumstances in God’s way. As He refines your spirit and your character, He also wants to receive the glory for it. This is a journey God is taking me on, and I’m thankful to Him for continuing to patiently break and shape my spirit for His glory.

A Meek Spirit

But let it be … the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit… –1 Peter 3:4.

In many ways a meek spirit is a yielded spirit. It is a spirit that is totally under the control of Almighty God. It does not fight unpleasant circumstances or strive to make life “better.” But neither is it a passive, “roll with punches”, cowering attitude. Actually, this spirit denotes someone who has gifts and abilities, is trained and effective, and could be very useful to the work of the church, yet is in complete subjection to God, moving only at His will.

A Quiet Spirit

But let it be … the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit… –1 Peter 3:4.

A quiet and restful spirit is an amazing quality. It is not humanly possible to achieve. When you see this spirit in someone, you can know it comes from a heart of brokenness. According to Isaiah, it is a choice: …In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not –Isaiah 30:15.

A quiet spirit and a meek spirit go hand in hand. It is an attitude of sitting back and letting God lead—whether exciting or boring, whether easy or difficult—and not resisting Him in any way.

There are times when we feel very disquieted in spirit, and it’s not possible to pull ourselves out of it by sheer willpower. But the Word of God is life-giving, and by studying the promises of God we can receive peace and rest for our spirits, as well as courage and grace to go on. I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved. Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope –Psalms 16:8, 9.

Depuis plusieurs années, Dieu me conduit à travers une vallée, une vallée longue et apparemment interminable. Il semble qu’à peine une situation se résout, une autre surgit. Ces difficultés exigent une réponse. Bien souvent, il ne s’agit pas tant d’une action physique que d’une réponse de l’esprit. Pour ma part, il m’a fallu environ deux ans avant d’en arriver à commencer à apprendre à faire des choix émotionnels sains et, plus important encore, conformes à la Bible.

Dans cet article, le mot « esprit » est défini comme « une disposition ou une attitude de l’esprit ». La Bible mentionne plusieurs types d’esprits que Dieu m’enseigne. Deux sont plus généraux et s’appliquent à tout le monde, et deux sont spécifiquement présentés pour nous, les femmes.

Avant de pouvoir discuter de ce qu’est un esprit sain et conforme à la Bible, il est essentiel de comprendre qu’il s’agit d’un choix. Il ne résulte pas des circonstances. Il ne nous vient pas sur un coup de tête. En tant que jeunes femmes, nous trouvons particulièrement facile de nous laisser guider par nos émotions. Mais la plupart des émotions qui nous « gouvernent » ne sont pas saines. Un esprit conforme à la Bible résulte de choix conscients — et non émotionnels ou dictés par les circonstances. Si nous les laissons faire, les émotions malsaines peuvent devenir monstrueuses et nous entraîner vers de nombreux états indésirables, comme la dépression, l’amertume et l’immoralité. En réponse, Dieu nous appelle à choisir délibérément le type d’esprit défini dans la Bible.

Un esprit brisé

Car ainsi parle Celui qui est élevé et sublime, qui demeure éternellement et dont le nom est saint : j’habite dans les lieux élevés et saints, mais aussi avec celui qui est contrit [brisé] et humble d’esprit, afin de ranimer l’esprit des humbles et de ranimer le cœur des contrits –Ésaïe 57:15.

Par-dessus tout, il est essentiel que nous choisissions de devenir brisées. Il est difficile d’insister assez sur l’importance de cela. Si nous ne nous laissons pas briser, nous ouvrons la porte à toutes sortes d’émotions et de réactions négatives, et surtout au péché.

La brisure est un choix difficile, presque impossible à faire par nous-mêmes. Souvent, Dieu nous conduit dans des situations difficiles où nous devons faire un choix : la brisure selon Dieu, ou quelque chose de malsain comme la colère ou le découragement. La brisure dépouille de tout. Elle exige que nous renoncions à notre contrôle sur les choses mauvaises, comme la maladie ou la déception, ainsi que sur les bonnes choses, comme nos désirs pour l’avenir. Être brisé signifie que nous laissons Dieu tout contrôler ; nous ne gardons rien. La plupart du temps, la brisure profonde ne survient pas d’un seul coup ; c’est un chemin douloureux où nous renonçons, puis renonçons encore, et encore. Sans devenir amères. Sans perdre la foi en Dieu. En fait, c’est dans les moments où nous sommes écrasées que nous choisissons de croire que Dieu est bon, même s’il semble n’y avoir aucune bonne raison de le faire.

La brisure est un choix — un choix très difficile qui ouvre la voie à la gloire de Dieu, puisqu’il s’agit d’éliminer le moi. Elle permet aussi à d’autres qualités plus nobles de se révéler.

Un esprit sobre

C’est pourquoi, ceignez les reins de votre entendement, [et] soyez sobres… –1 Pierre 1:13.

Dans ce verset, « sobre » signifie « être calme et maître de soi dans son esprit ; être modéré, exempt de passion ». C’est un mot intéressant. Selon ce verset, il nous est ordonné d’être calmes et maîtresses de nous-mêmes dans notre esprit. En tant que jeunes femmes, nous savons combien il est facile, voire automatique, de laisser nos sentiments à propos de situations et de circonstances s’emballer.

Pour ma part, je me trouvais dans une période d’incertitude et d’indécision, et j’étais si découragée que j’avais du mal à continuer. Je n’arrivais pas à me concentrer sur des choses importantes comme mon travail et le fait d’aller vers les autres. En étudiant ce verset, Dieu m’a convaincue que oui, même si je traversais une période très sombre, son commandement pour moi était de rester calme et de ne pas laisser mes émotions déchaînées me contrôler. Il m’a amenée à un point où je devais choisir, instant après instant, de prendre le contrôle de mon esprit. J’ai constaté qu’en choisissant la voie de Dieu, il m’accordait la grâce de vivre ainsi, ce qui a rendu mon esprit beaucoup plus stable et paisible.

Alors, gardez courage dans les moments sombres ! Choisissez de répondre aux circonstances à la manière de Dieu. Tandis qu’il affine votre esprit et votre caractère, il veut aussi en recevoir la gloire. C’est un chemin sur lequel Dieu me conduit, et je lui suis reconnaissante de continuer patiemment à briser et à façonner mon esprit pour sa gloire.

Un esprit doux

Mais que ce soit … la parure d’un esprit doux et paisible… –1 Pierre 3:4.

À bien des égards, un esprit doux est un esprit soumis. C’est un esprit entièrement sous le contrôle du Dieu tout-puissant. Il ne lutte pas contre les circonstances désagréables et ne s’efforce pas de rendre la vie « meilleure ». Mais ce n’est pas non plus une attitude passive, qui se contente de « subir les coups » et de se recroqueviller. En réalité, cet esprit caractérise une personne qui a des dons et des capacités, qui est formée et efficace, et qui pourrait être très utile à l’œuvre de l’Église, mais qui est néanmoins entièrement soumise à Dieu et n’agit que selon sa volonté.

Un esprit paisible

Mais que ce soit … la parure d’un esprit doux et paisible… –1 Pierre 3:4.

Un esprit paisible et serein est une qualité merveilleuse. Il est impossible de l’atteindre par des moyens humains. Quand vous voyez cet esprit chez quelqu’un, vous pouvez savoir qu’il vient d’un cœur brisé. Selon Ésaïe, c’est un choix : …C’est dans le retour à moi et le repos que sera votre salut, c’est dans le calme et la confiance que sera votre force : mais vous ne l’avez pas voulu –Ésaïe 30:15.

Un esprit paisible et un esprit doux vont de pair. C’est une attitude qui consiste à prendre du recul et à laisser Dieu conduire — que ce soit passionnant ou ennuyeux, facile ou difficile — sans lui résister en aucune façon.

Il nous arrive de nous sentir très agitées dans notre esprit, et il nous est impossible de nous en sortir par la seule force de la volonté. Mais la Parole de Dieu donne la vie, et en étudiant les promesses de Dieu, nous pouvons recevoir la paix et le repos pour notre esprit, ainsi que le courage et la grâce nécessaires pour continuer. J’ai constamment l’Éternel devant moi ; quand il est à ma droite, je ne chancelle pas. Aussi mon cœur est dans la joie, ma gloire exulte, et ma chair repose dans l’espérance –Psaumes 16:8, 9.

Sitting squarely on the great divide of our measured timeline of years lies the incarnate birth of our Lord Jesus Christ. He rightfully owns this place, for no other advent could so astutely impact humanity. The years before His birth are known as B.C. or “Before Christ”, while the years following are known as A.D. (Anno Domini, Latin for “The year of our Lord”). While His birth has been utterly cluttered and confused by pagan influences and personal indulgence, the simple radiant beauty of the occasion is still available for all who will but candidly gaze upon the unbeguiled scene.

While the calendar has placed the birth of Christ on December 25, most scholars have concluded that this date is inaccurate. It has also been determined that the actual year ascribed to His birth is also inaccurate by 4-6 years. The date was set by the bishop of Rome in accordance with a popular pagan festival called Saturnalia. The heathen Romans worshiped Saturn as the god of agriculture by feasting, parties, adorning their houses with evergreens, the exchanging of gifts, and general merry making. It was the bishop’s endeavor to provide a sanctifying influence upon the revelry and turn the minds of the general populace away from selfish indulgence to God incarnate. As we may well expect, the heathen festivities never missed a beat and continued on at the same pace. The church that initially frowned upon the proposition eventually accepted the idea and by the fourth century was fully acclimated and indoctrinated to the hybrid mixture of that which was Christian and pagan.

Thus, we are left with a dilemma today. How should a Christian regard the birth of Christ? Should we attempt to keep Christ in Christmas or get Him out? Regardless of our opinion, each of us must veritably resolve to understand the significance of the virgin birth apart from the emotional ties to the hybrid celebration and recognize the birth in a God-ordained fashion. In contrast to the millions who celebrate His birth in our day, there were but a paltry handful who were able and worthy to attend the actual event.

And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night. And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid. And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord. And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger. And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying, Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men –Luke 2:8-14.

It was a band of lowly shepherds who received the first birth announcement. Even these foolish and unlearned men knew of, and longed for, the anticipated Messiah. But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting –Micah 5:2.

As the star-spangled heavens erupted to life, the shepherds gazed in mesmerized awe at the scene before them and a new day began to dawn upon the horizon of their souls. The angelic host proclaimed their message to the shepherds, then soon vanished; yet the good news remained. The encounter was but a brief vapor, yet a three-fold fragrance lingered in the burning hearts of these men: A Savior… A Sign… and A Song…

…A Savior

The very fact that a Savior is promised, implies that there is something that we need to be saved from. Whatever our physical lot may be, man’s spiritual condition has been on the precipice of despair since the fall in Eden. Through four millennia, the human race had cowered under the diabolical cloud of sin and many had fallen prey to its menacing darkness. Sin can take a candle of hope and snuff it out in an instant. It can breathe its icy breath upon the fairest of flowers and wilt them in an instant. It takes loving marriages and introduces them to the throes of internal war. It takes the sincere bloom of youth and robs it of the fragrance of its innocence. Those who have managed to break free from the bondage of its personal subjugation can easily see their narrow escape from the mad society about them. Thus, the humble shepherds rejoiced at the advent of a Savior.

All have sinned and come under its condemnation. The very thought of freedom from the impending jurisdiction of our just punishment is a breath of fresh air. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved –John 3:17. Those who have been genuinely converted carry in their soul the hope of eternal life and the promise of heaven. They become new creatures as the Holy Spirit takes up residence in their hearts. While this bears a dramatic effect on the life of a believer, these are not the only issues of salvation. This Savior is also a Lord.

Just as the title of “Savior” implies a desperate need, so likewise, the name of “Christ, the Lord” implies a dominating victory. He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil –1 John 3:8. Not only shall we be freed from the condemnation of sin, we must also be rescued from its power and influence as well. The debilitating habits that we have accumulated in our sinful nature must be dealt a death blow. The passions and lusts that overpowered us before His influence came upon our lives must be subject to Him. The egotistical pride and driving temper within man that has destroyed relationships and wounded the lives of those that we love about us, must also be swallowed up in this victory. If Christ is not our Lord, then neither is He our Savior.

What child is this. Who laid to rest,
On Mary’s lap is sleeping?
Whom angels greet with anthems sweet,
While shepherds watch are keeping?
This, this is Christ the King,
Whom shepherds guard and angels sing.
Haste, haste to bring Him laud,
The Babe the Son of Mary.

…A Sign

One may well think that the angelic visitation was a much larger sign than the infant in the manger. Who among us has ever experienced the delight of hearing such a heavenly chorus? As we read the account, one can only imagine the enrapturing beauty of a myriad of celestial voices resounding together and filling the mountainside with a glimmer of heaven that earth has never known since the day of creation, When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy –Job 38:7. Yet the angels were not the sign.

The fact that this child was conceived by the Holy Ghost as detailed in Matthew 1:20, must be received by faith and can hardly be reckoned as a terrestrial sign. The fact that the child was wrapped in swaddling clothes was nothing unusual, for all mothers of the day did that. In one of the most graphic chapters depicting the birth of a child, God mentions that no one cared for Israel at their birth: And as for thy nativity, in the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed in water to supple thee; thou wast not salted at all, nor swaddled at all –Ezekiel 16:4. These clues will be useless in a search for the child. The tell-tale sign of this event is marked by the cradle of the infant. No mother would choose a cattle lot for a birthing suite and lay her newborn in a feed trough unless necessity demanded it.

The sign of the manger in conjunction with their scriptural knowledge of Bethlehem were all that was needed for the shepherds to find the child. Scripture makes no mention of the comforts of a stable at all. The shepherds were intimately familiar with the areas of town allotted for the animals and their journey began.

Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach –Hebrews 13:12-13. This sign calls for personal participation. Everyone whose heart beats loyal to the scene must also go to accompany Him. This will not be fulfilled by attending a living nativity scene, a “Messiah” performance, or by going to Grandmother’s house for Christmas dinner. We must be a partaker in his sufferings as Thomas when he said …unto his fellow disciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him –John 11:16.

To visit the Christ child will require us to haunt the place outside the inn. The Inn Crowd is the place of popular reception, popular understanding, and popular behavior. There awaits the comforts of friends, family, and fraternity, while it ministers a sense of belonging and acceptance. Christ knew no such luxury in His birth nor in His death, and He made His choice outside of the Inn Crowd.

Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed? For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not –Isaiah 53:1-3.

The despised shepherds lived most of their lives outside of the Inn Crowd and were the first to believe and receive Him. Loyalty to Christ requires separation from the loyalties of the world including most of its ever-popular celebration of Christ’s birth. It is a call to follow His choice to go without the camp. This is the difference between nominal worship and the heartfelt praise of His redeemed who will but follow Him to the manger.

Why lies He in such mean estate,
Where ox and ass are feeding?
Good Christians, fear, for sinners here
The silent Word is pleading.
Nails, spears shall pierce him through,
The cross he bore for me, for you.
Hail, hail the Word made flesh,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

…A Song

Those who desire to know him must venture outside The Inn and partake in …the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10. As they reap the scoffing and scorn of the Inn Crowd, they will also find that they are greeted with a heavenly song. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men –Luke 2:14.

As our portion in this earthly life diminishes, our quantum of glorious praise shall increase. The Jews were offended that the Messiah did not come to give them a larger portion and victory over the Roman world. Jesus …beheld the city, and wept over it, Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes –Luke 19:41-42. Peace on earth will never be apprehended by environmental perfection. Those lodged at The Inn, find their peace within the clean, convenient, and courteous companionship of each other. This is the popular, pampered peace the world promotes and portrays, but does not coincide with that of the babe in the meager manger. But it was those outside the inn that learned the song.

And they sung as it were a new song … and no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth –Revelation 14:3. These are those who are at peace with their earthly lot. These shall not be moved when someone else is promoted, carries more earthly possessions, or receives more attention. They are content with a cottage while others cloister in a castle. They cannot be persuaded to envy though others are… going there, doing that, or owning one. Others …think it strange that ye run not with them to the same excess of riot, speaking evil of you –1 Peter 4:4.

Peace on earth is nothing more than the great gain that arrives with godliness and contentment. Some wonder how David could fall into sin with Bathsheba while he possessed his multiple wives. How could he not? An abundance of options does not breed greater contentment. The fussing child in the store bawls because his hands are full, and he cannot have more. So, do the motel connoisseurs on our day depreciate any lodging accommodations that are less than perfect. They can sing the praises of a five-star hotel and diner, but are oblivious to the song by the manger.

Those whose hearts resound with goodwill to men, experience great joy as the wealthiest of earth’s inhabitants. They can rejoice in another’s promotion, good fortune, and success. In doing so, they inherit the earth. This is the song that Stephen sang proceeding his earthly departure. He spake of Abraham removing himself from his land, Acts 7:3 of Joseph being sold out of his home, vs.9 and of Moses being cast out, and fleeing to Midian. vs.21. This is he, that was in the church in the wilderness. vs.38. This was the same despised church that Stephen took up membership in and thus he received the same treatment. Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, And cast him out of the city, and stoned him … And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep –Acts 7:57-60.

So bring him incense, gold, and myrrh,
Come, peasant, king, to own him.
The King of kings salvation brings,
Let loving hearts enthrone him.

This is glory to God. This is peace on earth. This is goodwill toward men.
