Bem no centro da grande divisão de nossa linha do tempo, medida em anos, está o nascimento encarnado de nosso Senhor Jesus Cristo. Ele ocupa legitimamente esse lugar, pois nenhum outro advento poderia ter um impacto tão profundo sobre a humanidade. Os anos anteriores ao seu nascimento são conhecidos como a.C., ou «antes de Cristo», enquanto os anos posteriores são conhecidos como d.C. (Anno Domini, em latim, «o ano de nosso Senhor»). Embora seu nascimento tenha sido inteiramente obscurecido e confundido por influências pagãs e pela indulgência pessoal, a beleza simples e radiante da ocasião ainda está ao alcance de todos os que contemplarem com sinceridade a cena sem disfarces.

Embora o calendário situe o nascimento de Cristo em 25 de dezembro, a maioria dos estudiosos concluiu que essa data é inexata. Também se determinou que o ano efetivamente atribuído ao seu nascimento está incorreto em 4 a 6 anos. A data foi estabelecida pelo bispo de Roma de acordo com uma popular festa pagã chamada Saturnália. Os romanos pagãos adoravam Saturno como deus da agricultura, com banquetes, festas, adornos de sempre-vivas em suas casas, troca de presentes e celebrações em geral. O bispo procurou exercer uma influência santificadora sobre a folia e desviar a atenção da população em geral da indulgência egoísta para Deus encarnado. Como bem podemos esperar, as festividades pagãs não perderam o ritmo e continuaram no mesmo compasso. A igreja, que inicialmente desaprovou a proposta, acabou aceitando a ideia e, no século IV, já estava plenamente adaptada e doutrinada na mistura híbrida do cristão com o pagão.

Assim, hoje nos deparamos com um dilema. Como deve um cristão considerar o nascimento de Cristo? Devemos tentar manter Cristo no Natal ou tirá-lo de lá? Qualquer que seja nossa opinião, cada um de nós precisa realmente resolver compreender o significado do nascimento virginal, separado dos vínculos emocionais com a celebração híbrida, e reconhecer o nascimento de uma maneira ordenada por Deus. Em contraste com os milhões que celebram seu nascimento em nossos dias, houve apenas um punhado insignificante de pessoas capazes e dignas de presenciar o acontecimento.

Ora, havia naquela mesma região pastores que viviam nos campos e guardavam o seu rebanho durante a noite. E eis que um anjo do Senhor veio sobre eles, e a glória do Senhor os cercou de resplendor; e tiveram grande temor. E o anjo lhes disse: Não temais, porque eis que vos trago boas-novas de grande alegria, que serão para todo o povo. Pois, na cidade de Davi, vos nasceu hoje um Salvador, que é Cristo, o Senhor. E isto vos servirá de sinal: encontrareis o menino envolto em faixas e deitado numa manjedoura. E, de repente, apareceu com o anjo uma multidão da hoste celestial, louvando a Deus e dizendo: Glória a Deus nas alturas, e paz na terra, boa vontade para com os homens –Lucas 2:8-14.

Foi um grupo de humildes pastores que recebeu o primeiro anúncio do nascimento. Até mesmo esses homens simples e sem instrução sabiam da existência do Messias esperado e ansiavam por ele. Mas tu, Belém Efrata, embora pequena entre os milhares de Judá, de ti sairá aquele que há de governar Israel; cujas origens são desde os tempos antigos, desde a eternidade –Miqueias 5:2.

Quando os céus salpicados de estrelas ganharam vida, os pastores contemplaram, maravilhados e fascinados, a cena diante deles, e um novo dia começou a raiar no horizonte de suas almas. A hoste angelical proclamou sua mensagem aos pastores e logo desapareceu; contudo, as boas-novas permaneceram. O encontro não passou de um breve vapor, mas uma fragrância tríplice perdurou nos corações ardentes daqueles homens: um Salvador… um Sinal… e um Cântico…

…Um Salvador

O próprio fato de que um Salvador é prometido implica que há algo de que precisamos ser salvos. Seja qual for nossa condição física, a condição espiritual do ser humano está à beira do desespero desde a queda no Éden. Durante quatro milênios, a raça humana se encolheu sob a nuvem diabólica do pecado, e muitos foram vítimas de sua escuridão ameaçadora. O pecado pode tomar uma vela de esperança e apagá-la num instante. Pode soprar seu hálito gelado sobre as mais belas flores e fazê-las murchar num instante. Ele leva casamentos amorosos e os lança nas convulsões de uma guerra interna. Toma o sincero florescer da juventude e rouba-lhe a fragrância da inocência. Os que conseguiram libertar-se da servidão de sua subjugação pessoal podem ver com facilidade como escaparam por pouco da sociedade enlouquecida que os cerca. Assim, os humildes pastores se alegraram com a vinda de um Salvador.

Todos pecaram e estão sob a condenação do pecado. Só de pensar em nos livrarmos da jurisdição iminente de nossa justa punição já sentimos uma lufada de ar fresco. Porque Deus enviou o seu Filho ao mundo, não para condenar o mundo, mas para que o mundo fosse salvo por meio dele –João 3:17. Os que foram verdadeiramente convertidos levam na alma a esperança da vida eterna e a promessa do céu. Tornam-se novas criaturas quando o Espírito Santo passa a habitar em seu coração. Embora isso tenha um efeito profundo na vida do crente, esses não são os únicos aspectos da salvação. Esse Salvador também é Senhor.

Assim como o título «Salvador» implica uma necessidade desesperadora, também o nome «Cristo, o Senhor» implica uma vitória dominante. Quem comete pecado é do diabo, porque o diabo peca desde o princípio. Para este propósito se manifestou o Filho de Deus: para destruir as obras do diabo –1 João 3:8. Não só seremos libertos da condenação do pecado, como também precisamos ser resgatados de seu poder e influência. Os hábitos debilitantes que acumulamos em nossa natureza pecaminosa precisam receber um golpe mortal. As paixões e os desejos que nos dominavam antes de sua influência alcançar nossa vida precisam submeter-se a ele. O orgulho egocêntrico e o temperamento impetuoso dentro do ser humano, que destruíram relacionamentos e feriram a vida daqueles que amamos, também precisam ser tragados por esta vitória. Se Cristo não é nosso Senhor, tampouco é nosso Salvador.

Que menino é este, que repousa,
Dormindo no colo de Maria?
A quem os anjos saúdam com doces hinos,
Enquanto os pastores vigiam?
Este, este é Cristo, o Rei,
A quem os pastores guardam e os anjos cantam.
Depressa, depressa, tragam-lhe louvor,
O menino, o Filho de Maria.

…Um Sinal

Bem se poderia pensar que a visita dos anjos foi um sinal muito maior do que o menino na manjedoura. Quem entre nós já experimentou o prazer de ouvir um coro tão celestial? Ao lermos o relato, só podemos imaginar a beleza arrebatadora de uma miríade de vozes celestiais ressoando juntas e enchendo a encosta da montanha com um vislumbre do céu que a terra nunca mais conheceu desde o dia da criação, quando as estrelas da manhã cantavam juntas, e todos os filhos de Deus bradavam de alegria –Jó 38:7. No entanto, os anjos não eram o sinal.

O fato de que essa criança foi concebida pelo Espírito Santo, conforme descrito em Mateus 1:20, deve ser recebido pela fé e dificilmente pode ser considerado um sinal terrestre. O fato de a criança estar envolta em faixas não tinha nada de extraordinário, pois todas as mães da época faziam isso. Num dos capítulos mais vívidos que retratam o nascimento de uma criança, Deus menciona que ninguém cuidou de Israel ao nascer: Quanto ao teu nascimento, no dia em que nasceste, não te cortaram o cordão umbilical, nem te lavaram com água para te amaciar; de modo algum te salgaram, nem te envolveram em faixas –Ezequiel 16:4. Essas pistas seriam inúteis na busca pelo menino. O sinal distintivo desse acontecimento está marcado pelo berço do menino. Nenhuma mãe escolheria um estábulo como sala de parto e colocaria o recém-nascido numa manjedoura, a menos que a necessidade a obrigasse.

O sinal da manjedoura, junto com o conhecimento que tinham das Escrituras sobre Belém, era tudo de que os pastores precisavam para encontrar o menino. As Escrituras não mencionam em absoluto os confortos de um estábulo. Os pastores conheciam muito bem as áreas da cidade destinadas aos animais, e sua jornada começou.

Por isso também Jesus, para santificar o povo com o seu próprio sangue, sofreu fora da porta. Saiamos, pois, a ele, fora do acampamento, levando o seu opróbrio –Hebreus 13:12-13. Esse sinal exige participação pessoal. Todos cujo coração bate em lealdade àquela cena também precisam ir acompanhá-lo. Isso não se cumprirá assistindo a uma encenação de presépio vivo, a uma apresentação do «Messias» ou indo à casa da avó para a ceia de Natal. Precisamos ser participantes de seus sofrimentos, como Tomé, quando disse …aos seus companheiros discípulos: Vamos também nós, para morrermos com ele –João 11:16.

Visitar o menino Cristo exigirá que frequentemos o lugar fora da hospedaria. A Turma da Hospedaria é o lugar da aceitação popular, da compreensão popular e do comportamento popular. Ali se encontram os confortos dos amigos, da família e da fraternidade, enquanto se oferece uma sensação de pertencimento e aceitação. Cristo não conheceu tal luxo nem em seu nascimento nem em sua morte, e escolheu ficar fora da Turma da Hospedaria.

Quem creu em nosso relato? E a quem foi revelado o braço do SENHOR? Porque ele crescerá diante dele como um renovo e como raiz de uma terra seca; não tinha aparência nem formosura e, quando o olhávamos, não havia beleza que nos agradasse. Foi desprezado e rejeitado pelos homens, homem de dores e familiarizado com o sofrimento; e escondemos dele o rosto, por assim dizer; ele foi desprezado, e não lhe demos valor –Isaías 53:1-3.

Os pastores desprezados passaram a maior parte da vida fora da Turma da Hospedaria e foram os primeiros a crer nele e recebê-lo. A lealdade a Cristo exige separação das lealdades do mundo, incluindo a maior parte de sua sempre popular celebração do nascimento de Cristo. É um chamado a seguir a escolha dele de sair do acampamento. Essa é a diferença entre a adoração nominal e o louvor de coração dos redimidos que se dispõem a segui-lo até a manjedoura.

Por que jaz ele em tão humilde lugar,
Onde se alimentam o boi e o jumento?
Bons cristãos, temam: pelos pecadores aqui,
A Palavra silenciosa suplica.
Pregos e lanças o traspassarão,
A cruz que ele carregou por mim e por ti.
Salve, salve a Palavra feita carne,
O menino, o Filho de Maria.

…Um Cântico

Os que desejam conhecê-lo precisam aventurar-se para fora da Hospedaria e participar …da comunhão dos seus sofrimentos, conformando-se com a sua morte –Filipenses 3:10. Ao colherem as zombarias e o desprezo da Turma da Hospedaria, também descobrirão que são recebidos com um cântico celestial. Glória a Deus nas alturas, e paz na terra, boa vontade para com os homens –Lucas 2:14.

À medida que nossa porção nesta vida terrena diminui, aumenta nossa medida de louvor glorioso. Os judeus se ofenderam porque o Messias não veio para lhes dar uma porção maior e vitória sobre o mundo romano. Jesus …contemplou a cidade e chorou por ela, dizendo: Ah! Se tu conhecesses, ao menos neste teu dia, as coisas que pertencem à tua paz! Mas agora estão ocultas aos teus olhos –Lucas 19:41-42. A paz na terra jamais será alcançada por meio da perfeição ambiental. Os que se hospedam na Hospedaria encontram sua paz na companhia limpa, conveniente e cortês uns dos outros. Essa é a paz popular e mimada que o mundo promove e retrata, mas que não coincide com a do menino na humilde manjedoura. Foram, porém, os que estavam fora da hospedaria que aprenderam o cântico.

E cantavam como que um cântico novo … e ninguém podia aprender aquele cântico, senão os cento e quarenta e quatro mil que foram redimidos da terra –Apocalipse 14:3. Estes são os que estão em paz com sua condição terrena. Não se abalarão quando outra pessoa for promovida, tiver mais bens terrenos ou receber mais atenção. Contentam-se com uma casa modesta enquanto outros se recolhem num castelo. Não se deixam persuadir a invejar, mesmo que outros estejam… indo a algum lugar, fazendo aquilo ou possuindo tal coisa. Outros …acham estranho que não corrais com eles no mesmo excesso de devassidão e falam mal de vós –1 Pedro 4:4.

A paz na terra não é mais do que o grande ganho que vem com a piedade e o contentamento. Alguns se perguntam como Davi pôde pecar com Bate-Seba quando possuía várias esposas. Como poderia não pecar? Uma abundância de opções não gera maior contentamento. A criança que faz birra na loja berra porque está com as mãos cheias e não pode ter mais. Da mesma forma, os conhecedores de motéis de nossos dias depreciam qualquer hospedagem que não seja perfeita. Podem cantar os louvores de um hotel e restaurante cinco estrelas, mas não percebem o cântico junto à manjedoura.

Os que têm o coração ressoando com boa vontade para com os homens experimentam grande alegria, como os habitantes mais ricos da terra. Podem alegrar-se com a promoção, a boa fortuna e o sucesso de outra pessoa. Ao fazê-lo, herdam a terra. Esse é o cântico que Estêvão entoou antes de partir desta vida terrena. Ele falou de Abraão deixando sua terra, Atos 7:3; de José sendo vendido e afastado de sua casa, v.9; e de Moisés sendo expulso e fugindo para Midiã, v.21. Este é aquele que estava na igreja no deserto, v.38. Essa era a mesma igreja desprezada à qual Estêvão se filiou e, por isso, recebeu o mesmo tratamento. Então clamaram em alta voz, taparam os ouvidos e, todos juntos, avançaram contra ele, lançaram-no fora da cidade e o apedrejaram … E, pondo-se de joelhos, clamou em alta voz: Senhor, não lhes imputes este pecado. E, tendo dito isso, adormeceu –Atos 7:57-60.

Trazei-lhe, pois, incenso, ouro e mirra,
Venham, camponês e rei, reconhecê-lo.
O Rei dos reis traz salvação;
Que corações amorosos o entronizem.

Isto é glória a Deus. Isto é paz na terra. Isto é boa vontade para com os homens.

How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! –Romans 10:14-15.

Truth is urgent. Earnestly and passionately preaching the truth is urgent. Even though it eventually cost Him His life, Jesus urgently and passionately taught the will of His Father in Heaven. Paul urgently and passionately declared the whole counsel of God until his conscience was free from the guilt of the blood of all men.

Passionate, urgent, Spirit-anointed preaching is prophetic …for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy –Revelation 19:10. It is prophetic as it bears witness to the life of Jesus. Upon the choices of mankind hinge the earthly spread of either the kingdom of darkness or the Kingdom of Light. Urgency-filled, passionate preaching furthers the cause of Christ.

For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God … For … it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe … Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men –1 Corinthians 1:18-25.

Passionate preaching is a forceful factor in identifying that there is no middle ground in Biblical warfare. This passionate preaching stirs the conscience and convicts the heart. It drives the listener to …choose you this day whom ye will serve… –Joshua 24:15. He cannot hang in the deceptive clutches of ambiguous indecision. Passionate preaching urges the faithful to ongoing surrender and awakens the drunken sleeper to repentance. It defines sin, separating it from holiness, thereby compelling a decision.

…Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts –Zechariah 4:6, in demonstration of the Spirit and of power. Urgency filled, passionate preaching propels, teaches, convicts, and moves individuals in ways that even urgent personal Bible study, personal devotions, and discipleship cannot. No other form of teaching can effectively replace this God-ordained method of ministry in the churches of Jesus the Christ. God ordains that His work, first done in the heart of the preacher, makes possible the persuasion of men. Such messages clearly define kingdom boundaries and bear upon the listener irresistible accountability. Sovereignty deems that under passionate, Spirit-anointed preaching, the conscience cannot resist accountability. Without revoke and aside from choice, upon the conscience of the hearer is laid either damnation or assurance.

Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine –2 Timothy 4:2. Our Anabaptist forefathers believed in the urgency of passionately calling men and women to more than a mere understanding of truth. They called for active faith—obedience. They preached with expectancy, believing that their voices would move people at the core and bring about radical lifestyle changes. They expected their preaching to send men into evangelistic endeavors… even unto death. They expected their influence to move men and women to live under the banner and direction of Jesus’ practical example.

Current preaching styles have trended from Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men… –2 Corinthians 5:11 and …We ought to obey God rather than men –Acts 5:29; to “God understands and feels your pain.” Such is not erroneous, per se, but passionate urgency must fill the preacher’s heart to convince, to convict, and to pierce the darkness of today.

If preachers, sermon after sermon, simply present facts in monotone manners, and speak without passion, they dull the hearers’ conscience. They urge them to lackadaisical living, leaving them unmoved. It sears and hardens. It kills vision and burden. It is a seed bed for apostasy. It heightens satisfaction in hypocritical living. It entrenches complacent legalism into the core of the heart of man.

But if all prophesy [preach], and there come in one that believeth not, or one unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth –1 Corinthians 14:24-25.

Conviction never lacks emotion. Neither does Holy Spirit-anointed preaching. Emotionless preaching covertly identifies to listeners that the preacher lacks compelling passion for his own words. Whether a message is encouragement, warning, or doctrine, urgent passion and emotion are urgently imperative.

The secret closet of the preacher must be full of Light… Biblical Light. The “Sword” he bears must first be severely laid to the roots of his own flesh. Indeed, it presses upon his soul until the fire in his bones can no longer be silent and the Lord is honored.

No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier –2 Timothy 2:4. The preacher needs to be intellectually prepared. God must have worked through his personal Bible study and his prayerful preparation. Less preparation is a symbol of a preacher’s own complacency and will be the ruin of his God-appointed accountability. He cannot wield the Sword (Word) of the Lord effectively …to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit… –Hebrews 4:12, unless it happens within his own heart first. The husbandman must first taste and feed on his own fruits. Through such enabling grace, the parishioners will either be spiritually moved to deeper levels of passionate living, or their conscience will be hardened against the Holy Spirit’s convicting influence. Through faith, obedience, and the blood of the Lamb, it defeats willful sin, fiendish demons, sensual flesh, and Satan. Thus, urgent, Spirit-anointed, passionate preaching removes all middle ground while it purifies the church.

Πώς, λοιπόν, θα επικαλεστούν εκείνον στον οποίο δεν έχουν πιστέψει; Και πώς θα πιστέψουν σε εκείνον για τον οποίο δεν έχουν ακούσει; Και πώς θα ακούσουν χωρίς κήρυκα; Και πώς θα κηρύξουν, αν δεν αποσταλούν; Όπως είναι γραμμένο: Πόσο όμορφα είναι τα πόδια εκείνων που κηρύττουν το ευαγγέλιο της ειρήνης και φέρνουν χαρμόσυνα νέα για αγαθά πράγματα! –Ρωμαίους 10:14-15.

Η αλήθεια είναι επείγουσα υπόθεση. Η ένθερμη και παθιασμένη κήρυξη της αλήθειας είναι επείγουσα υπόθεση. Παρόλο που τελικά Του κόστισε τη ζωή Του, ο Ιησούς δίδαξε με αίσθηση του επείγοντος και πάθος το θέλημα του Πατέρα Του στους ουρανούς. Ο Παύλος διακήρυττε με αίσθηση του επείγοντος και πάθος όλη τη βουλή του Θεού, ώσπου η συνείδησή του να είναι ελεύθερη από την ενοχή για το αίμα όλων των ανθρώπων.

Το παθιασμένο κήρυγμα με αίσθηση του επείγοντος και χρίσμα του Πνεύματος είναι προφητικό …γιατί η μαρτυρία για τον Ιησού είναι το πνεύμα της προφητείας –Αποκάλυψη 19:10. Είναι προφητικό, καθώς μαρτυρεί τη ζωή του Ιησού. Από τις επιλογές της ανθρωπότητας εξαρτάται η εξάπλωση στη γη είτε του βασιλείου του σκότους είτε της Βασιλείας του Φωτός. Το παθιασμένο κήρυγμα, γεμάτο αίσθηση του επείγοντος, προωθεί την υπόθεση του Χριστού.

Γιατί το κήρυγμα του σταυρού είναι ανοησία για εκείνους που χάνονται, ενώ για εμάς που σωζόμαστε είναι δύναμη Θεού … Επειδή … ευδόκησε ο Θεός, μέσω της ανοησίας του κηρύγματος, να σώσει εκείνους που πιστεύουν … Γιατί η ανοησία του Θεού είναι σοφότερη από τους ανθρώπους, και η αδυναμία του Θεού είναι ισχυρότερη από τους ανθρώπους –1 Κορινθίους 1:18-25.

Το παθιασμένο κήρυγμα αποτελεί καθοριστικό παράγοντα για να αναγνωρίσουμε ότι στον βιβλικό πόλεμο δεν υπάρχει ουδέτερη ζώνη. Αυτό το παθιασμένο κήρυγμα αφυπνίζει τη συνείδηση και ελέγχει την καρδιά. Ωθεί τον ακροατή να …διαλέξετε σήμερα ποιον θα υπηρετήσετε… –Ιησούς του Ναυή 24:15. Δεν μπορεί να παραμένει παγιδευμένος στα απατηλά δεσμά της αμφίσημης αναποφασιστικότητας. Το παθιασμένο κήρυγμα προτρέπει τους πιστούς να συνεχίσουν να παραδίδουν τον εαυτό τους και ξυπνά τον μεθυσμένο κοιμισμένο άνθρωπο σε μετάνοια. Ορίζει την αμαρτία, διαχωρίζοντάς την από την αγιότητα, και έτσι επιβάλλει μια απόφαση.

…Όχι με δύναμη ούτε με ισχύ, αλλά με το Πνεύμα μου, λέει ο Κύριος των δυνάμεων –Ζαχαρίας 4:6, με απόδειξη του Πνεύματος και δύναμης. Το παθιασμένο κήρυγμα που είναι γεμάτο αίσθηση του επείγοντος ωθεί, διδάσκει, ελέγχει και κινεί τους ανθρώπους με τρόπους που δεν μπορούν να πετύχουν ούτε η επείγουσα προσωπική μελέτη της Γραφής, ούτε οι προσωπικές στιγμές λατρείας, ούτε η μαθητεία. Καμία άλλη μορφή διδασκαλίας δεν μπορεί να αντικαταστήσει αποτελεσματικά αυτή τη μέθοδο διακονίας, που έχει ορίσει ο Θεός, στις εκκλησίες του Ιησού Χριστού. Ο Θεός ορίζει ότι το έργο Του, όταν επιτελείται πρώτα στην καρδιά του κήρυκα, καθιστά δυνατή την πειθώ των ανθρώπων. Τέτοια μηνύματα ορίζουν καθαρά τα όρια της βασιλείας και επιβάλλουν στον ακροατή ακαταμάχητη ευθύνη. Η κυριαρχία του Θεού ορίζει ότι, υπό το παθιασμένο κήρυγμα με χρίσμα του Πνεύματος, η συνείδηση δεν μπορεί να αντισταθεί στην ευθύνη. Χωρίς δυνατότητα ανάκλησης και ανεξάρτητα από την επιλογή, στη συνείδηση του ακροατή τίθεται είτε η καταδίκη είτε η βεβαιότητα.

Κήρυξε τον λόγο· επίμενε είτε είναι εύκαιρο είτε όχι· έλεγξε, επίπληξε, παρακάλεσε με κάθε μακροθυμία και διδασκαλία –2 Τιμόθεο 4:2. Οι Αναβαπτιστές πρόγονοί μας πίστευαν ότι ήταν επείγον να καλούν με πάθος άντρες και γυναίκες σε κάτι περισσότερο από μια απλή κατανόηση της αλήθειας. Ζητούσαν ενεργή πίστη—υπακοή. Κήρυτταν με προσδοκία, πιστεύοντας ότι τα λόγια τους θα άγγιζαν τους ανθρώπους βαθιά και θα επέφεραν ριζικές αλλαγές στον τρόπο ζωής τους. Περίμεναν ότι το κήρυγμά τους θα έστελνε άντρες σε ευαγγελιστικές προσπάθειες… ακόμη και μέχρι θανάτου. Περίμεναν ότι η επιρροή τους θα έκανε άντρες και γυναίκες να ζουν κάτω από τη σημαία και σύμφωνα με την κατεύθυνση που έδινε το πρακτικό παράδειγμα του Ιησού.

Τα σύγχρονα κηρυγματικά ύφη έχουν μετατοπιστεί από το Γνωρίζοντας, λοιπόν, τον φόβο του Κυρίου, πείθουμε τους ανθρώπους… –2 Κορινθίους 5:11 και το …Πρέπει να υπακούμε στον Θεό μάλλον παρά στους ανθρώπους –Πράξεις 5:29· προς το «Ο Θεός καταλαβαίνει και νιώθει τον πόνο σου». Αυτό δεν είναι κατ’ ανάγκην εσφαλμένο, αλλά η καρδιά του κήρυκα πρέπει να είναι γεμάτη παθιασμένη αίσθηση του επείγοντος, ώστε να πείθει, να ελέγχει και να διαπερνά το σημερινό σκοτάδι.

Αν οι κήρυκες, κήρυγμα μετά το κήρυγμα, απλώς παρουσιάζουν γεγονότα μονότονα και μιλούν χωρίς πάθος, αμβλύνουν τη συνείδηση των ακροατών. Τους παρακινούν σε μια νωθρή ζωή, αφήνοντάς τους ασυγκίνητους. Καυτηριάζει και σκληραίνει. Σκοτώνει το όραμα και το βάρος της ευθύνης. Είναι το σπορείο της αποστασίας. Ενισχύει την ικανοποίηση από μια υποκριτική ζωή. Ριζώνει τον αυτάρεσκο νομικισμό στον πυρήνα της ανθρώπινης καρδιάς.

Αν όμως όλοι προφητεύουν [κηρύττουν], και μπει κάποιος άπιστος ή αμαθής, ελέγχεται από όλους και κρίνεται από όλους· και έτσι φανερώνονται τα μυστικά της καρδιάς του· και τότε, πέφτοντας με το πρόσωπο στη γη, θα προσκυνήσει τον Θεό και θα ομολογήσει ότι ο Θεός είναι πραγματικά ανάμεσά σας –1 Κορινθίους 14:24-25.

Ο έλεγχος της συνείδησης δεν στερείται ποτέ συναισθήματος. Ούτε το κήρυγμα που έχει χριστεί από το Άγιο Πνεύμα. Το άχρωμο κήρυγμα φανερώνει έμμεσα στους ακροατές ότι ο κήρυκας δεν έχει πειστικό πάθος για τα ίδια του τα λόγια. Είτε το μήνυμα είναι ενθάρρυνση, προειδοποίηση ή διδασκαλία, το παθιασμένο αίσθημα του επείγοντος και το συναίσθημα είναι απολύτως απαραίτητα.

Ο κρυφός τόπος του κήρυκα πρέπει να είναι γεμάτος Φως… Βιβλικό Φως. Το «Σπαθί» που κρατά πρέπει πρώτα να έχει εφαρμοστεί αυστηρά στις ρίζες της δικής του σάρκας. Πράγματι, πιέζει την ψυχή του ώσπου η φωτιά στα κόκαλά του να μην μπορεί πια να σιωπά και να τιμάται ο Κύριος.

Κανένας στρατιώτης δεν εμπλέκεται στις υποθέσεις της ζωής, για να ευαρεστήσει εκείνον που τον στρατολόγησε –2 Τιμόθεο 2:4. Ο κήρυκας χρειάζεται να είναι διανοητικά προετοιμασμένος. Ο Θεός πρέπει να έχει εργαστεί μέσα από την προσωπική του μελέτη της Γραφής και την προσευχητική προετοιμασία του. Η λιγότερη προετοιμασία αποτελεί σύμβολο του εφησυχασμού του ίδιου του κήρυκα και θα οδηγήσει στην καταστροφή της ευθύνης που του ανέθεσε ο Θεός. Δεν μπορεί να χειρίζεται αποτελεσματικά το Σπαθί (τον Λόγο) του Κυρίου …για τον διαχωρισμό ψυχής και πνεύματος… –Εβραίους 4:12, αν αυτό δεν συμβεί πρώτα μέσα στη δική του καρδιά. Ο γεωργός πρέπει πρώτα να γευτεί και να τραφεί από τους δικούς του καρπούς. Μέσω μιας τέτοιας ενδυναμωτικής χάρης, οι ενορίτες είτε θα κινηθούν πνευματικά σε βαθύτερα επίπεδα παθιασμένης ζωής είτε η συνείδησή τους θα σκληρύνει απέναντι στην ελεγκτική επιρροή του Αγίου Πνεύματος. Με την πίστη, την υπακοή και το αίμα του Αρνίου, νικά την εκούσια αμαρτία, τους δαιμονικούς δαίμονες, τη σαρκική αισθησιακότητα και τον Σατανά. Έτσι, το παθιασμένο κήρυγμα με αίσθηση του επείγοντος και χρίσμα του Πνεύματος εξαλείφει κάθε ουδέτερη ζώνη, ενώ εξαγνίζει την εκκλησία.

Editor’s Note:

Normally, we haven’t used our magazine to bring focus to any specific individual. However, in regard to Mose, we felt it would be fitting to provide a small tribute. Mose was instrumental in helping to get The Heartbeat of the Remnant magazine started way back over twenty years ago when it was first begun. Then years later when several churches divided some of the various aspects of ministry between themselves, Ephrata Christian Fellowship with Mose as one of its leaders, took on the publishing of the magazine as their own effort. They continued this for a number of years until it eventually went out of print temporarily due to their editors moving out of the area. Fast forward to 2016, when we (The Berean Voice) wanted to begin publishing a newsletter/magazine. When Mose realized what we were about to do, he requested that we take over the publication of their magazine since he and his fellow laborers wished to see it continue in print. In short, this is how we ended up publishing a magazine that had originally been published by another church in another state. Thus, it seems fitting to give recognition to the life Mose has lived and the path he has endeavored to blaze for others. It is with gratefulness that we remember the life and example Mose has left us with. And it is with humility that we will persevere in our efforts to keep this torch (the magazine) burning for Truth.

Mose S. Stoltzfus entered into his eternal rest on December 6, 2020, following a brief battle with Covid-19. The testimony of his life was that of a race well run, leaving a legacy of godly faithfulness to the end which others can follow. Brother Mose, as he was often referred to by his church brethren, will be greatly missed. Family, friends, business associates, and church brethren remember with gratitude how his life was a blessing to them. Most of all, he will be missed by his beloved wife, Rhoda.

Mose grew up in a home where he was taught the “fear of the Lord” and had a new birth into the Kingdom of God at the age of 15. This was the beginning of his love for God and His Word, the Holy Scriptures. This was a love which he pursued for the rest of his life, and which in time enabled him to be mighty in word and deed.

It has been my privilege to have known Brother Mose for nearly 30 years. Most of the fellowship we had together was related to the work of the Church, and of the Kingdom of God. What I want to share here concerning Brother Mose is largely related to his ministry in the Gospel.

One of the prominent gifts the Lord gave to Brother Mose was the gift of preaching. It was a gift that he pursued with zeal, not by constraint, but willingly. Whether it was just a few gathered in a living room or hundreds gathered in a community hall, he loved to preach the Gospel of Jesus Christ. He often preached to men and women who had troubled souls and were seeking a Savior. He preached to small assemblies of believers where new churches were beginning, helping them to be established in the faith. He preached in large churches and fellowship gatherings of saints encouraging and exhorting them to follow Christ.

Those who were around Brother Mose during his years of ministry know that he loved singing. He encouraged believers to open their mouth and praise the Lord in song, both individually and in the church assembly. Between 2010 and 2015, he took a small choir with him on several trips to Canada, singing and preaching as they visited various churches. He also made at least two trips to Germany during those years as well. The choir of youth that traveled with him would sing, and then he would preach in the German language. They visited about a dozen churches over the course of each three-week trip. On one trip, they also included a stop in a city for street witnessing and passing out tracts. Here again, Brother Mose preached in the German language to those under the sound of his voice.

When I consider the spirit and zeal of Brother Mose, the words of the Apostle Paul to the Romans seem very fitting: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise. So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also –Romans 1:14-15. Brother Mose saw himself as a debtor to make Christ known to many and was ready to preach wherever there was an open door. His ‘Rome’ was across America, Canada, and beyond. He was …not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: boldly proclaiming it to be …the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek –Romans 1:16.

For nearly two decades, from the late 1980’s and onward, Brother Mose frequently teamed up with Denny Kenaston, and they would travel to communities where they had an invitation to preach. Often, this would be a weekend event, starting Friday evening, going all day Saturday, and Sunday morning and afternoon. Sometimes it was a whole week or more of evening messages. One of them would preach one night, and the other the next night throughout the week. With much unction from the Holy One, they would preach the Gospel. There are many testimonies of new conversions, of repentance from sin, of revival, and of straying souls returning to the Savior.

Brother Mose sought the lost from any background and any place where they would come to listen. He even preached on city streets to those who never went to church. When he held meetings, many evangelical, protestant denominations were represented in those who came to hear him preach. But it was the various conservative, Anabaptist groups toward which his heart was especially drawn, since this was his own background. His specific concern was regarding those who had backslidden or strayed from the way of Truth. Whether those he encountered were Mennonite, Amish, or Hutterite, he could relate to their background and was well versed in the history of each group. He was able to preach in a powerful way to expose sin and error, while warning of judgment to come. He preached the cross of Christ as the hope of salvation to all who would believe.

Another gift Brother Mose had was in speaking with individuals one-on-one. It could be a middle-aged person on a hospital bed, a youth in a living room, or a young adult who had responded to the Holy Spirit’s moving after a preaching service. He had a way of gently asking them about the needs in their life, and then explaining clearly what needed to be done in order for them to be reconciled to God.

Throughout his ministry, Brother Mose labored much to establish churches on a right foundation. He was directly involved in the formation of a number of new churches, as well as advising and helping already established groups. He ordained men for the ministry in many churches, often with the assistance of elders from his own fellowship or those of a sister church. Issues such as brotherhood, unity, and proper leadership were important to him.

Brother Mose was often the watchman on the wall for the church in this generation. He would frequently warn against false doctrines that threatened to creep into churches. He was on guard against false teachers, false prophets, and even false brethren. In the face of these dangers to the church, he gave much attention to teaching sound doctrine. The Word of God was lifted up as the safe and sure foundation by which to judge what is true and what is false.

Brother Mose was a true leader. He led by direct action and by example. One thing that seemed to make him restless in spirit was to observe a situation where there was lack of leadership, for want of a man to stand in the gap. He was ready to step forward and serve when occasion called for it. But even as a strong leader, he surrounded himself with men who would labor with him. Throughout his years of ministry, he worked as a member of the body. Many of his preaching events across the country would be with fellow ministers preaching alongside him. When dealing with church problems, he would frequently seek out the council of fellow ministers. In the last handful of years, he was actively involved in the annual ministers’ meetings held in Indiana as the “Agape Christian Fellowship” group was being formulated and established. He would express, sometimes with tears, his rejoicing in the fellowship and council of his brethren who were laboring with him for the welfare of the various churches represented. There was also humility of mind in looking back over the years at those things that should have been done differently, whether errors or omissions, and acknowledging them as such. His passion was to see the church endure faithful unto the end.

And now Brother Mose has entered into his eternal rest. To those of us who knew him and labored with him remains the responsibility of carrying on the work of the Kingdom until Christ returns for His Church. May we be found of Him in peace, without spot and blameless.

Σημείωση του εκδότη:

Κανονικά, δεν έχουμε χρησιμοποιήσει το περιοδικό μας για να στρέψουμε την προσοχή σε κάποιο συγκεκριμένο πρόσωπο. Ωστόσο, όσον αφορά τον Mose, θεωρήσαμε ότι θα ήταν ταιριαστό να του αποτίσουμε έναν μικρό φόρο τιμής. Ο Mose συνέβαλε καθοριστικά στο να ξεκινήσει το περιοδικό The Heartbeat of the Remnant πριν από περισσότερα από είκοσι χρόνια, όταν πρωτοεκδόθηκε. Χρόνια αργότερα, όταν αρκετές εκκλησίες μοίρασαν μεταξύ τους διάφορες πτυχές της διακονίας, η Ephrata Christian Fellowship, με τον Mose ως ένα από τα ηγετικά της μέλη, ανέλαβε την έκδοση του περιοδικού ως δική της προσπάθεια. Συνέχισαν για αρκετά χρόνια, μέχρι που τελικά η έκδοσή του διακόπηκε προσωρινά, επειδή οι συντάκτες τους έφυγαν από την περιοχή. Ας προχωρήσουμε στο 2016, όταν εμείς (The Berean Voice) θέλαμε να αρχίσουμε να εκδίδουμε ένα ενημερωτικό δελτίο/περιοδικό. Όταν ο Mose κατάλαβε τι επρόκειτο να κάνουμε, μας ζήτησε να αναλάβουμε την έκδοση του δικού τους περιοδικού, καθώς εκείνος και οι συνεργάτες του επιθυμούσαν να συνεχίσει να εκδίδεται. Με λίγα λόγια, έτσι καταλήξαμε να εκδίδουμε ένα περιοδικό που αρχικά είχε εκδοθεί από μια άλλη εκκλησία σε άλλη πολιτεία. Γι’ αυτό, φαίνεται ταιριαστό να αναγνωρίσουμε τη ζωή που έζησε ο Mose και το μονοπάτι που προσπάθησε να ανοίξει για τους άλλους. Με ευγνωμοσύνη θυμόμαστε τη ζωή και το παράδειγμα που μας άφησε ο Mose. Και με ταπεινοφροσύνη θα επιμείνουμε στις προσπάθειές μας να κρατήσουμε αναμμένη αυτή τη δάδα (το περιοδικό) για την Αλήθεια.

Ο Mose S. Stoltzfus αναπαύθηκε αιώνια στις 6 Δεκεμβρίου 2020, ύστερα από μια σύντομη μάχη με την Covid-19. Η μαρτυρία της ζωής του ήταν μιας κούρσας που έτρεξε καλά, αφήνοντας ως κληρονομιά ευσέβεια και πιστότητα μέχρι τέλους, ώστε να μπορούν να την ακολουθήσουν και άλλοι. Ο αδελφός Mose, όπως τον αποκαλούσαν συχνά οι αδελφοί του στην εκκλησία, θα μας λείψει πολύ. Η οικογένειά του, οι φίλοι, οι επαγγελματικοί συνεργάτες και οι αδελφοί της εκκλησίας θυμούνται με ευγνωμοσύνη πώς η ζωή του ήταν ευλογία γι’ αυτούς. Περισσότερο απ’ όλους, θα λείψει στην αγαπημένη του σύζυγο, Rhoda.

Ο Mose μεγάλωσε σε ένα σπίτι όπου διδάχτηκε τον «φόβο του Κυρίου» και αναγεννήθηκε στη Βασιλεία του Θεού σε ηλικία 15 ετών. Αυτή ήταν η αρχή της αγάπης του για τον Θεό και τον Λόγο Του, τις Άγιες Γραφές. Αυτή την αγάπη την καλλιέργησε σε όλη την υπόλοιπη ζωή του, και με τον καιρό αυτή τον κατέστησε δυνατό στον λόγο και στην πράξη.

Είχα το προνόμιο να γνωρίζω τον αδελφό Mose σχεδόν 30 χρόνια. Το μεγαλύτερο μέρος της συναναστροφής μας αφορούσε το έργο της Εκκλησίας και της Βασιλείας του Θεού. Όσα θέλω να μοιραστώ εδώ για τον αδελφό Mose σχετίζονται κυρίως με τη διακονία του στο Ευαγγέλιο.

Ένα από τα εξέχοντα χαρίσματα που έδωσε ο Κύριος στον αδελφό Mose ήταν το χάρισμα του κηρύγματος. Το ασκούσε με ζήλο, όχι από εξαναγκασμό, αλλά πρόθυμα. Είτε ήταν λίγοι συγκεντρωμένοι σε ένα καθιστικό είτε εκατοντάδες σε μια κοινοτική αίθουσα, αγαπούσε να κηρύττει το Ευαγγέλιο του Ιησού Χριστού. Συχνά κήρυττε σε άνδρες και γυναίκες με ταραγμένη ψυχή, που αναζητούσαν έναν Σωτήρα. Κήρυττε σε μικρές συνάξεις πιστών, όπου ξεκινούσαν νέες εκκλησίες, βοηθώντας τες να στερεωθούν στην πίστη. Κήρυττε σε μεγάλες εκκλησίες και συναθροίσεις πιστών, ενθαρρύνοντάς τους και προτρέποντάς τους να ακολουθούν τον Χριστό.

Όσοι βρίσκονταν κοντά στον αδελφό Mose κατά τα χρόνια της διακονίας του γνωρίζουν ότι αγαπούσε το τραγούδι. Ενθάρρυνε τους πιστούς να ανοίγουν το στόμα τους και να δοξάζουν τον Κύριο με ύμνους, τόσο ατομικά όσο και στη σύναξη της εκκλησίας. Από το 2010 έως το 2015, πήρε μαζί του μια μικρή χορωδία σε αρκετά ταξίδια στον Καναδά, όπου τραγουδούσαν και κήρυτταν καθώς επισκέπτονταν διάφορες εκκλησίες. Εκείνα τα χρόνια πραγματοποίησε επίσης τουλάχιστον δύο ταξίδια στη Γερμανία. Η νεανική χορωδία που ταξίδευε μαζί του τραγουδούσε και μετά εκείνος κήρυττε στα γερμανικά. Σε κάθε ταξίδι τριών εβδομάδων επισκέπτονταν περίπου δώδεκα εκκλησίες. Σε ένα ταξίδι, συμπεριέλαβαν επίσης μια στάση σε μια πόλη, όπου έδιναν μαρτυρία στους δρόμους και μοίραζαν φυλλάδια. Και εκεί, ο αδελφός Mose κήρυττε στα γερμανικά σε όσους άκουγαν τη φωνή του.

Όταν σκέφτομαι το πνεύμα και τον ζήλο του αδελφού Mose, τα λόγια του αποστόλου Παύλου προς τους Ρωμαίους φαίνονται πολύ ταιριαστά: Οφειλέτης είμαι και στους Έλληνες και στους βαρβάρους, και στους σοφούς και στους ασύνετους. Έτσι, όσο εξαρτάται από εμένα, είμαι έτοιμος να κηρύξω το ευαγγέλιο και σε εσάς που βρίσκεστε στη Ρώμη –Ρωμαίους 1:14-15. Ο αδελφός Mose θεωρούσε τον εαυτό του οφειλέτη, ώστε να γνωρίσουν πολλοί τον Χριστό, και ήταν έτοιμος να κηρύξει όπου υπήρχε ανοιχτή πόρτα. Η δική του «Ρώμη» βρισκόταν σε όλη την Αμερική, τον Καναδά και πέρα από αυτούς. Δεν ντρεπόταν για το ευαγγέλιο του Χριστού: το διακήρυττε με τόλμη ως δύναμη Θεού για σωτηρία σε καθέναν που πιστεύει, πρώτα στον Ιουδαίο και επίσης στον Έλληνα –Ρωμαίους 1:16.

Για σχεδόν δύο δεκαετίες, από τα τέλη της δεκαετίας του 1980 και έπειτα, ο αδελφός Mose συνεργαζόταν συχνά με τον Denny Kenaston και ταξίδευαν σε κοινότητες όπου είχαν προσκληθεί να κηρύξουν. Συχνά επρόκειτο για εκδηλώσεις του Σαββατοκύριακου: άρχιζαν το βράδυ της Παρασκευής, συνεχίζονταν όλο το Σάββατο και ολοκληρώνονταν το πρωί και το απόγευμα της Κυριακής. Μερικές φορές διαρκούσαν μια ολόκληρη εβδομάδα ή και περισσότερο, με κηρύγματα κάθε βράδυ. Τη μία νύχτα κήρυττε ο ένας και την επόμενη ο άλλος, καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια της εβδομάδας. Με μεγάλη έμπνευση από τον Άγιο, κήρυτταν το Ευαγγέλιο. Υπάρχουν πολλές μαρτυρίες για ανθρώπους που πίστεψαν πρόσφατα, για μετάνοια από την αμαρτία, για αναζωπύρωση και για ψυχές που είχαν απομακρυνθεί και επέστρεψαν στον Σωτήρα.

Ο αδελφός Mose αναζητούσε τους χαμένους από κάθε υπόβαθρο και σε κάθε μέρος όπου θα έρχονταν να ακούσουν. Κήρυττε ακόμη και στους δρόμους των πόλεων σε ανθρώπους που δεν πήγαιναν ποτέ στην εκκλησία. Στις συναθροίσεις που διοργάνωνε, ανάμεσα σε όσους έρχονταν να τον ακούσουν εκπροσωπούνταν πολλές ευαγγελικές, προτεσταντικές ομολογίες. Όμως η καρδιά του στρεφόταν ιδιαίτερα προς τις διάφορες συντηρητικές αναβαπτιστικές ομάδες, καθώς αυτό ήταν και το δικό του υπόβαθρο. Ιδιαίτερη ανησυχία του ήταν όσοι είχαν αποστατήσει ή είχαν παρεκκλίνει από την οδό της Αλήθειας. Είτε όσοι συναντούσε ήταν Μεννονίτες, Άμις ή Χουτερίτες, μπορούσε να κατανοήσει το υπόβαθρό τους και γνώριζε καλά την ιστορία κάθε ομάδας. Μπορούσε να κηρύττει με ισχυρό τρόπο, αποκαλύπτοντας την αμαρτία και την πλάνη, ενώ προειδοποιούσε για την επερχόμενη κρίση. Κήρυττε τον σταυρό του Χριστού ως την ελπίδα της σωτηρίας για όλους όσοι θα πίστευαν.

Ένα άλλο χάρισμα του αδελφού Mose ήταν η ικανότητά του να συνομιλεί κατ’ ιδίαν με τους ανθρώπους. Μπορούσε να είναι ένας μεσήλικας σε κρεβάτι νοσοκομείου, ένας νέος σε ένα καθιστικό ή ένας νεαρός ενήλικας που είχε ανταποκριθεί στην κίνηση του Αγίου Πνεύματος μετά από μια συνάθροιση κηρύγματος. Είχε τον τρόπο να τους ρωτάει με ευγένεια για τις ανάγκες της ζωής τους και έπειτα να εξηγεί με σαφήνεια τι έπρεπε να γίνει για να συμφιλιωθούν με τον Θεό.

Σε όλη τη διάρκεια της διακονίας του, ο αδελφός Mose εργάστηκε σκληρά για να θεμελιώσει εκκλησίες σε σωστό θεμέλιο. Συμμετείχε άμεσα στην ίδρυση αρκετών νέων εκκλησιών, ενώ παράλληλα συμβούλευε και βοηθούσε ήδη εδραιωμένες ομάδες. Χειροτόνησε άνδρες στη διακονία σε πολλές εκκλησίες, συχνά με τη συνδρομή πρεσβυτέρων από τη δική του συντροφιά ή από μια αδελφή εκκλησία. Θέματα όπως η αδελφότητα, η ενότητα και η σωστή ηγεσία είχαν μεγάλη σημασία γι’ αυτόν.

Ο αδελφός Mose ήταν συχνά ο φύλακας πάνω στο τείχος για την εκκλησία αυτής της γενιάς. Προειδοποιούσε συχνά για ψεύτικες διδασκαλίες που απειλούσαν να παρεισφρήσουν στις εκκλησίες. Αγρυπνούσε για ψευδοδιδασκάλους, ψευδοπροφήτες, ακόμη και ψευδαδέλφους. Μπροστά σε αυτούς τους κινδύνους για την εκκλησία, έδινε μεγάλη έμφαση στη διδασκαλία της ορθής διδαχής. Ο Λόγος του Θεού υψωνόταν ως το ασφαλές και βέβαιο θεμέλιο με το οποίο μπορούσε κανείς να κρίνει τι είναι αληθινό και τι ψεύτικο.

Ο αδελφός Mose ήταν αληθινός ηγέτης. Ηγούνταν με άμεση δράση και με το παράδειγμά του. Κάτι που φαινόταν να τον αναστατώνει ήταν να παρατηρεί μια κατάσταση όπου έλειπε η ηγεσία, επειδή δεν υπήρχε άνδρας να σταθεί στο χάσμα. Ήταν έτοιμος να βγει μπροστά και να υπηρετήσει όταν το απαιτούσαν οι περιστάσεις. Όμως, ακόμη και ως ισχυρός ηγέτης, περιέβαλλε τον εαυτό του με άνδρες που εργάζονταν μαζί του. Σε όλα τα χρόνια της διακονίας του, εργαζόταν ως μέλος του σώματος. Σε πολλές από τις κηρυκτικές εκδηλώσεις του σε όλη τη χώρα, κήρυτταν μαζί του και άλλοι διάκονοι. Όταν αντιμετώπιζε προβλήματα της εκκλησίας, συχνά ζητούσε τη συμβουλή άλλων διακόνων. Τα τελευταία λίγα χρόνια συμμετείχε ενεργά στις ετήσιες συναντήσεις διακόνων που πραγματοποιούνταν στην Ιντιάνα, καθώς διαμορφωνόταν και εδραιωνόταν η ομάδα «Agape Christian Fellowship». Κάποιες φορές, με δάκρυα, εξέφραζε τη χαρά του για την κοινωνία και τη συμβουλή των αδελφών του, οι οποίοι εργάζονταν μαζί του για την ευημερία των διαφόρων εκκλησιών που εκπροσωπούνταν. Υπήρχε επίσης ταπεινοφροσύνη όταν αναπολούσε τα χρόνια και όσα θα έπρεπε να είχαν γίνει διαφορετικά, είτε επρόκειτο για λάθη είτε για παραλείψεις, και τα αναγνώριζε ως τέτοια. Το πάθος του ήταν να δει την εκκλησία να παραμένει πιστή μέχρι τέλους.

Και τώρα ο αδελφός Mose έχει αναπαυθεί αιώνια. Σε εμάς που τον γνωρίσαμε και εργαστήκαμε μαζί του απομένει η ευθύνη να συνεχίσουμε το έργο της Βασιλείας μέχρι να επιστρέψει ο Χριστός για την Εκκλησία Του. Είθε να μας βρει εν ειρήνη, χωρίς κηλίδα και άμεμπτους.

How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! –Romans 10:14-15.

Truth is urgent. Earnestly and passionately preaching the truth is urgent. Even though it eventually cost Him His life, Jesus urgently and passionately taught the will of His Father in Heaven. Paul urgently and passionately declared the whole counsel of God until his conscience was free from the guilt of the blood of all men.

Passionate, urgent, Spirit-anointed preaching is prophetic …for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy –Revelation 19:10. It is prophetic as it bears witness to the life of Jesus. Upon the choices of mankind hinge the earthly spread of either the kingdom of darkness or the Kingdom of Light. Urgency-filled, passionate preaching furthers the cause of Christ.

For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God … For … it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe … Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men –1 Corinthians 1:18-25.

Passionate preaching is a forceful factor in identifying that there is no middle ground in Biblical warfare. This passionate preaching stirs the conscience and convicts the heart. It drives the listener to …choose you this day whom ye will serve… –Joshua 24:15. He cannot hang in the deceptive clutches of ambiguous indecision. Passionate preaching urges the faithful to ongoing surrender and awakens the drunken sleeper to repentance. It defines sin, separating it from holiness, thereby compelling a decision.

…Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts –Zechariah 4:6, in demonstration of the Spirit and of power. Urgency filled, passionate preaching propels, teaches, convicts, and moves individuals in ways that even urgent personal Bible study, personal devotions, and discipleship cannot. No other form of teaching can effectively replace this God-ordained method of ministry in the churches of Jesus the Christ. God ordains that His work, first done in the heart of the preacher, makes possible the persuasion of men. Such messages clearly define kingdom boundaries and bear upon the listener irresistible accountability. Sovereignty deems that under passionate, Spirit-anointed preaching, the conscience cannot resist accountability. Without revoke and aside from choice, upon the conscience of the hearer is laid either damnation or assurance.

Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine –2 Timothy 4:2. Our Anabaptist forefathers believed in the urgency of passionately calling men and women to more than a mere understanding of truth. They called for active faith—obedience. They preached with expectancy, believing that their voices would move people at the core and bring about radical lifestyle changes. They expected their preaching to send men into evangelistic endeavors… even unto death. They expected their influence to move men and women to live under the banner and direction of Jesus’ practical example.

Current preaching styles have trended from Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men… –2 Corinthians 5:11 and …We ought to obey God rather than men –Acts 5:29; to “God understands and feels your pain.” Such is not erroneous, per se, but passionate urgency must fill the preacher’s heart to convince, to convict, and to pierce the darkness of today.

If preachers, sermon after sermon, simply present facts in monotone manners, and speak without passion, they dull the hearers’ conscience. They urge them to lackadaisical living, leaving them unmoved. It sears and hardens. It kills vision and burden. It is a seed bed for apostasy. It heightens satisfaction in hypocritical living. It entrenches complacent legalism into the core of the heart of man.

But if all prophesy [preach], and there come in one that believeth not, or one unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth –1 Corinthians 14:24-25.

Conviction never lacks emotion. Neither does Holy Spirit-anointed preaching. Emotionless preaching covertly identifies to listeners that the preacher lacks compelling passion for his own words. Whether a message is encouragement, warning, or doctrine, urgent passion and emotion are urgently imperative.

The secret closet of the preacher must be full of Light… Biblical Light. The “Sword” he bears must first be severely laid to the roots of his own flesh. Indeed, it presses upon his soul until the fire in his bones can no longer be silent and the Lord is honored.

No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier –2 Timothy 2:4. The preacher needs to be intellectually prepared. God must have worked through his personal Bible study and his prayerful preparation. Less preparation is a symbol of a preacher’s own complacency and will be the ruin of his God-appointed accountability. He cannot wield the Sword (Word) of the Lord effectively …to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit… –Hebrews 4:12, unless it happens within his own heart first. The husbandman must first taste and feed on his own fruits. Through such enabling grace, the parishioners will either be spiritually moved to deeper levels of passionate living, or their conscience will be hardened against the Holy Spirit’s convicting influence. Through faith, obedience, and the blood of the Lamb, it defeats willful sin, fiendish demons, sensual flesh, and Satan. Thus, urgent, Spirit-anointed, passionate preaching removes all middle ground while it purifies the church.

Como, pois, invocarão aquele em quem não creram? E como crerão naquele de quem não ouviram falar? E como ouvirão, se não há quem pregue? E como pregarão, se não forem enviados? Como está escrito: Quão formosos são os pés dos que pregam o evangelho da paz e anunciam boas-novas de coisas boas! –Romanos 10:14-15.

A verdade é urgente. Pregar a verdade com fervor e paixão é urgente. Embora isso acabasse lhe custando a vida, Jesus ensinou com urgência e paixão a vontade de seu Pai no Céu. Paulo declarou com urgência e paixão todo o desígnio de Deus, até que sua consciência estivesse livre da culpa pelo sangue de todos os homens.

A pregação apaixonada, urgente e ungida pelo Espírito é profética …pois o testemunho de Jesus é o espírito da profecia –Apocalipse 19:10. É profética porque dá testemunho da vida de Jesus. Das escolhas da humanidade depende a expansão terrena do reino das trevas ou do Reino da Luz. A pregação urgente e apaixonada promove a causa de Cristo.

Pois a pregação da cruz é loucura para os que perecem, mas para nós, que somos salvos, é o poder de Deus… Pois… aprouve a Deus salvar os que creem por meio da loucura da pregação… Porque a loucura de Deus é mais sábia do que os homens, e a fraqueza de Deus é mais forte do que os homens –1 Coríntios 1:18-25.

A pregação apaixonada é um fator decisivo para identificar que, na guerra bíblica, não há terreno neutro. Essa pregação apaixonada desperta a consciência e convence o coração. Ela leva o ouvinte a …escolhei hoje a quem servireis… –Josué 24:15. Ele não pode permanecer preso às garras enganosas da indecisão ambígua. A pregação apaixonada exorta os fiéis à entrega contínua e desperta o que dorme embriagado para o arrependimento. Ela define o pecado, distinguindo-o da santidade e, assim, compelindo a uma decisão.

…Não por força nem por poder, mas pelo meu Espírito, diz o SENHOR dos Exércitos –Zacarias 4:6, em demonstração do Espírito e de poder. A pregação urgente e apaixonada impulsiona, ensina, convence e move as pessoas de maneiras que nem mesmo o estudo bíblico pessoal feito com urgência, as devoções pessoais e o discipulado conseguem. Nenhuma outra forma de ensino pode substituir eficazmente esse método de ministério ordenado por Deus nas igrejas de Jesus Cristo. Deus ordena que sua obra, realizada primeiro no coração do pregador, torne possível persuadir os homens. Mensagens assim definem claramente os limites do reino e impõem ao ouvinte uma responsabilidade irresistível. A soberania determina que, sob uma pregação apaixonada e ungida pelo Espírito, a consciência não pode resistir à responsabilidade. Sem possibilidade de revogação e independentemente da escolha, sobre a consciência de quem ouve recai a condenação ou a certeza.

Pregue a palavra; insista a tempo e fora de tempo; repreenda, censure, exorte com toda a paciência e doutrina –2 Timóteo 4:2. Nossos antepassados anabatistas acreditavam na urgência de chamar homens e mulheres apaixonadamente a algo além de uma mera compreensão da verdade. Eles convocavam à fé ativa — à obediência. Pregavam com expectativa, acreditando que suas vozes tocariam as pessoas profundamente e provocariam mudanças radicais de estilo de vida. Esperavam que sua pregação levasse homens a empreendimentos evangelísticos… até mesmo à morte. Esperavam que sua influência levasse homens e mulheres a viver sob a bandeira e a orientação do exemplo prático de Jesus.

Os estilos de pregação atuais têm se afastado de Sabendo, portanto, o temor do Senhor, persuadimos os homens… –2 Coríntios 5:11 e de …Antes, importa obedecer a Deus do que aos homens –Atos 5:29; para “Deus compreende e sente a sua dor”. Isso não é, em si, errado, mas a urgência apaixonada deve encher o coração do pregador para convencer, despertar convicção e penetrar as trevas de hoje.

Se os pregadores, sermão após sermão, simplesmente apresentam fatos em tom monótono e falam sem paixão, entorpecem a consciência dos ouvintes. Incentivam-nos a viver com indolência, deixando-os indiferentes. Isso cauteriza e endurece. Mata a visão e o senso de responsabilidade. É um terreno propício à apostasia. Aumenta a satisfação com uma vida hipócrita. Enraíza o legalismo complacente no mais profundo do coração humano.

Mas, se todos profetizarem [pregarem], e entrar alguém que não crê ou que não é instruído, ele será convencido por todos e julgado por todos; e assim os segredos de seu coração serão revelados; e, prostrando-se com o rosto em terra, adorará a Deus e declarará que Deus está verdadeiramente em vocês –1 Coríntios 14:24-25.

A convicção nunca está desprovida de emoção. Tampouco a pregação ungida pelo Espírito Santo. Uma pregação sem emoção comunica sutilmente aos ouvintes que falta ao pregador paixão convincente pelas próprias palavras. Quer a mensagem seja de encorajamento, advertência ou doutrina, a paixão e a emoção urgentes são absolutamente imprescindíveis.

O aposento secreto do pregador deve estar repleto de Luz… Luz bíblica. A “Espada” que ele carrega deve primeiro ser aplicada severamente às raízes de sua própria carne. De fato, ela comprime sua alma até que o fogo em seus ossos já não possa permanecer em silêncio e o Senhor seja honrado.

Nenhum soldado em serviço se envolve nos negócios desta vida, a fim de agradar àquele que o alistou –2 Timóteo 2:4. O pregador precisa estar intelectualmente preparado. Deus deve ter operado por meio de seu estudo bíblico pessoal e de sua preparação em oração. Uma preparação menor é sinal da própria complacência do pregador e será a ruína da responsabilidade que Deus lhe confiou. Ele não pode manejar eficazmente a Espada (a Palavra) do Senhor …para dividir alma e espírito… –Hebreus 4:12, a menos que isso aconteça primeiro em seu próprio coração. O agricultor deve primeiro provar e alimentar-se dos próprios frutos. Por meio dessa graça capacitadora, os membros da congregação serão movidos espiritualmente a níveis mais profundos de vida apaixonada, ou sua consciência será endurecida contra a influência convincente do Espírito Santo. Pela fé, pela obediência e pelo sangue do Cordeiro, ela vence o pecado deliberado, os demônios malignos, a carne sensual e Satanás. Assim, a pregação urgente, apaixonada e ungida pelo Espírito elimina todo terreno neutro enquanto purifica a igreja.

Sitting squarely on the great divide of our measured timeline of years lies the incarnate birth of our Lord Jesus Christ. He rightfully owns this place, for no other advent could so astutely impact humanity. The years before His birth are known as B.C. or “Before Christ”, while the years following are known as A.D. (Anno Domini, Latin for “The year of our Lord”). While His birth has been utterly cluttered and confused by pagan influences and personal indulgence, the simple radiant beauty of the occasion is still available for all who will but candidly gaze upon the unbeguiled scene.

While the calendar has placed the birth of Christ on December 25, most scholars have concluded that this date is inaccurate. It has also been determined that the actual year ascribed to His birth is also inaccurate by 4-6 years. The date was set by the bishop of Rome in accordance with a popular pagan festival called Saturnalia. The heathen Romans worshiped Saturn as the god of agriculture by feasting, parties, adorning their houses with evergreens, the exchanging of gifts, and general merry making. It was the bishop’s endeavor to provide a sanctifying influence upon the revelry and turn the minds of the general populace away from selfish indulgence to God incarnate. As we may well expect, the heathen festivities never missed a beat and continued on at the same pace. The church that initially frowned upon the proposition eventually accepted the idea and by the fourth century was fully acclimated and indoctrinated to the hybrid mixture of that which was Christian and pagan.

Thus, we are left with a dilemma today. How should a Christian regard the birth of Christ? Should we attempt to keep Christ in Christmas or get Him out? Regardless of our opinion, each of us must veritably resolve to understand the significance of the virgin birth apart from the emotional ties to the hybrid celebration and recognize the birth in a God-ordained fashion. In contrast to the millions who celebrate His birth in our day, there were but a paltry handful who were able and worthy to attend the actual event.

And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night. And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid. And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord. And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger. And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying, Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men –Luke 2:8-14.

It was a band of lowly shepherds who received the first birth announcement. Even these foolish and unlearned men knew of, and longed for, the anticipated Messiah. But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting –Micah 5:2.

As the star-spangled heavens erupted to life, the shepherds gazed in mesmerized awe at the scene before them and a new day began to dawn upon the horizon of their souls. The angelic host proclaimed their message to the shepherds, then soon vanished; yet the good news remained. The encounter was but a brief vapor, yet a three-fold fragrance lingered in the burning hearts of these men: A Savior… A Sign… and A Song…

…A Savior

The very fact that a Savior is promised, implies that there is something that we need to be saved from. Whatever our physical lot may be, man’s spiritual condition has been on the precipice of despair since the fall in Eden. Through four millennia, the human race had cowered under the diabolical cloud of sin and many had fallen prey to its menacing darkness. Sin can take a candle of hope and snuff it out in an instant. It can breathe its icy breath upon the fairest of flowers and wilt them in an instant. It takes loving marriages and introduces them to the throes of internal war. It takes the sincere bloom of youth and robs it of the fragrance of its innocence. Those who have managed to break free from the bondage of its personal subjugation can easily see their narrow escape from the mad society about them. Thus, the humble shepherds rejoiced at the advent of a Savior.

All have sinned and come under its condemnation. The very thought of freedom from the impending jurisdiction of our just punishment is a breath of fresh air. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved –John 3:17. Those who have been genuinely converted carry in their soul the hope of eternal life and the promise of heaven. They become new creatures as the Holy Spirit takes up residence in their hearts. While this bears a dramatic effect on the life of a believer, these are not the only issues of salvation. This Savior is also a Lord.

Just as the title of “Savior” implies a desperate need, so likewise, the name of “Christ, the Lord” implies a dominating victory. He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil –1 John 3:8. Not only shall we be freed from the condemnation of sin, we must also be rescued from its power and influence as well. The debilitating habits that we have accumulated in our sinful nature must be dealt a death blow. The passions and lusts that overpowered us before His influence came upon our lives must be subject to Him. The egotistical pride and driving temper within man that has destroyed relationships and wounded the lives of those that we love about us, must also be swallowed up in this victory. If Christ is not our Lord, then neither is He our Savior.

What child is this. Who laid to rest,
On Mary’s lap is sleeping?
Whom angels greet with anthems sweet,
While shepherds watch are keeping?
This, this is Christ the King,
Whom shepherds guard and angels sing.
Haste, haste to bring Him laud,
The Babe the Son of Mary.

…A Sign

One may well think that the angelic visitation was a much larger sign than the infant in the manger. Who among us has ever experienced the delight of hearing such a heavenly chorus? As we read the account, one can only imagine the enrapturing beauty of a myriad of celestial voices resounding together and filling the mountainside with a glimmer of heaven that earth has never known since the day of creation, When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy –Job 38:7. Yet the angels were not the sign.

The fact that this child was conceived by the Holy Ghost as detailed in Matthew 1:20, must be received by faith and can hardly be reckoned as a terrestrial sign. The fact that the child was wrapped in swaddling clothes was nothing unusual, for all mothers of the day did that. In one of the most graphic chapters depicting the birth of a child, God mentions that no one cared for Israel at their birth: And as for thy nativity, in the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut, neither wast thou washed in water to supple thee; thou wast not salted at all, nor swaddled at all –Ezekiel 16:4. These clues will be useless in a search for the child. The tell-tale sign of this event is marked by the cradle of the infant. No mother would choose a cattle lot for a birthing suite and lay her newborn in a feed trough unless necessity demanded it.

The sign of the manger in conjunction with their scriptural knowledge of Bethlehem were all that was needed for the shepherds to find the child. Scripture makes no mention of the comforts of a stable at all. The shepherds were intimately familiar with the areas of town allotted for the animals and their journey began.

Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate. Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach –Hebrews 13:12-13. This sign calls for personal participation. Everyone whose heart beats loyal to the scene must also go to accompany Him. This will not be fulfilled by attending a living nativity scene, a “Messiah” performance, or by going to Grandmother’s house for Christmas dinner. We must be a partaker in his sufferings as Thomas when he said …unto his fellow disciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him –John 11:16.

To visit the Christ child will require us to haunt the place outside the inn. The Inn Crowd is the place of popular reception, popular understanding, and popular behavior. There awaits the comforts of friends, family, and fraternity, while it ministers a sense of belonging and acceptance. Christ knew no such luxury in His birth nor in His death, and He made His choice outside of the Inn Crowd.

Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the LORD revealed? For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him. He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not –Isaiah 53:1-3.

The despised shepherds lived most of their lives outside of the Inn Crowd and were the first to believe and receive Him. Loyalty to Christ requires separation from the loyalties of the world including most of its ever-popular celebration of Christ’s birth. It is a call to follow His choice to go without the camp. This is the difference between nominal worship and the heartfelt praise of His redeemed who will but follow Him to the manger.

Why lies He in such mean estate,
Where ox and ass are feeding?
Good Christians, fear, for sinners here
The silent Word is pleading.
Nails, spears shall pierce him through,
The cross he bore for me, for you.
Hail, hail the Word made flesh,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

…A Song

Those who desire to know him must venture outside The Inn and partake in …the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10. As they reap the scoffing and scorn of the Inn Crowd, they will also find that they are greeted with a heavenly song. Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men –Luke 2:14.

As our portion in this earthly life diminishes, our quantum of glorious praise shall increase. The Jews were offended that the Messiah did not come to give them a larger portion and victory over the Roman world. Jesus …beheld the city, and wept over it, Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes –Luke 19:41-42. Peace on earth will never be apprehended by environmental perfection. Those lodged at The Inn, find their peace within the clean, convenient, and courteous companionship of each other. This is the popular, pampered peace the world promotes and portrays, but does not coincide with that of the babe in the meager manger. But it was those outside the inn that learned the song.

And they sung as it were a new song … and no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth –Revelation 14:3. These are those who are at peace with their earthly lot. These shall not be moved when someone else is promoted, carries more earthly possessions, or receives more attention. They are content with a cottage while others cloister in a castle. They cannot be persuaded to envy though others are… going there, doing that, or owning one. Others …think it strange that ye run not with them to the same excess of riot, speaking evil of you –1 Peter 4:4.

Peace on earth is nothing more than the great gain that arrives with godliness and contentment. Some wonder how David could fall into sin with Bathsheba while he possessed his multiple wives. How could he not? An abundance of options does not breed greater contentment. The fussing child in the store bawls because his hands are full, and he cannot have more. So, do the motel connoisseurs on our day depreciate any lodging accommodations that are less than perfect. They can sing the praises of a five-star hotel and diner, but are oblivious to the song by the manger.

Those whose hearts resound with goodwill to men, experience great joy as the wealthiest of earth’s inhabitants. They can rejoice in another’s promotion, good fortune, and success. In doing so, they inherit the earth. This is the song that Stephen sang proceeding his earthly departure. He spake of Abraham removing himself from his land, Acts 7:3 of Joseph being sold out of his home, vs.9 and of Moses being cast out, and fleeing to Midian. vs.21. This is he, that was in the church in the wilderness. vs.38. This was the same despised church that Stephen took up membership in and thus he received the same treatment. Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, And cast him out of the city, and stoned him … And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep –Acts 7:57-60.

So bring him incense, gold, and myrrh,
Come, peasant, king, to own him.
The King of kings salvation brings,
Let loving hearts enthrone him.

This is glory to God. This is peace on earth. This is goodwill toward men.
